Conform three RR packages to the generator folder shape (drop catalog/, tabs/; flatten testing root)
Three `packages/react-router-*` libraries carry structure that is NOT part of the canonical `@tools/generators:folders` shape. Bring them into line: the only sanctioned top-level folders inside `src/` are `components/`, `config/`, `data/`, `hooks/`, `utils/` (each with its own `__tests__/`), plus a root `types.ts` and a single barrel `index.ts` (and the existing `index.css`). Specs live in the nearest `__tests__/`.

## Canonical shape (source of truth)
`tools/generators/src/generators/folders/` — template tree + `CANONICAL_ROUTING_SUBTREE.md`. Allowed per area: `components/ config/ data/ hooks/ utils/`, each with `__tests__/`; root `types.ts`; `config/defaults.ts`, `utils/formatters.ts`, `utils/parsers.ts` are canonical seed files. No other top-level folders.

## Ground truth gathered during planning
- All THREE packages are source-first (`main`/`types` -> `./src/index.ts`); consuming apps' Vite transpiles them. No `build` target to worry about; `dist/` is stale output — ignore it.
- Every EXTERNAL consumer imports via the package barrel only. No deep subpath imports (`.../catalog`, `.../tabs`, `.../env`, etc.) exist in `applications/` or other packages. So only the barrel + intra-package relative imports must be rewired.
- Validation per package: `pnpm nx run <project>:lint`, `:typecheck`, `:test`. There is NO `build` target on these source-first libs — use a consumer app (`openthrottle-developer`) `:typecheck`/`:build` as the integration check, and `pnpm nx run monorepo:knip` for dead-export drift.

## Scope
1. `@openthrottle/react-router-rollout` — dissolve `src/catalog/`.
2. `@openthrottle/react-router-testing` — flatten `src/*.ts` modules into subfolders, specs into `__tests__/`, keep one root barrel.
3. `@openthrottle/react-router-ui` — dissolve `src/tabs/`.

Constraints: no public API (barrel export) changes — same named exports out of each package `index.ts`. Preserve `@public` JSDoc tags so Knip keeps exports. Alphabetize barrel exports/object keys where order is immaterial (repo style). Conventional commits with `Plan-Id:`/`Task-Id:` footers; commit per task.

Author an `ot-onboarding` skill: get new users set up on OpenThrottle
Create a new hand-authored, repo-specific skill `skills/ot-onboarding/SKILL.md` whose job is to onboard a person (or agent-driven session) onto OpenThrottle end-to-end: confirm the OT MCP is installed/configured and healthy, then walk them through the basics of the system — the mental model, the core apps, keyboard shortcuts, workflows, and the wider skill catalog. The "kitchen sink" orientation skill new users invoke first.

## Why
OpenThrottle has a lot of surface area — a plans/tasks SSOT in OT, an Nx+pnpm monorepo, a NestJS GraphQL server, several React Router apps, a growing catalog of skills (`skills/` + managed `.agents/skills/`), Workflow/OT Loop orchestration, and MCP tooling. There's no single guided on-ramp. New users (and fresh agent sessions) rediscover setup and conventions ad hoc. `ot-onboarding` is the front door: one skill that verifies the environment is wired correctly and then teaches the essentials with pointers into the deeper skills.

## Scope / behavior
1. **MCP install + health gate first.** Detect whether the `openthrottle-mcp` server is configured for the current agent (`.mcp.json` / per-tool config), run the `health` tool, and if it's missing or unhealthy, guide the user through install/auth using the existing runbook (see the "Stale in-session OT MCP" / AUTH.md guidance) rather than silently proceeding. Fail loudly with the exact remediation.
2. **System basics tour.** Explain the OT mental model (plans/tasks are the SSOT, created via MCP not Markdown), the monorepo shape (`applications/`, `packages/`, `tools/`, `databases/`), and how to run the core dev servers via Nx (`openthrottle-server:dev`, `openthrottle-developer:dev`) — linking to CLAUDE.md / MONOREPO.md instead of duplicating them.
3. **Keyboard shortcuts + workflows.** Surface the shortcuts and everyday workflows a new user needs (agent keybindings, the `/loop` recurring runner, Workflow multi-agent orchestration, the OT Loop, `/github/*` skills) so they know what levers exist.
4. **The wider skill catalog.** Teach how skills work here (authored `skills/` vs managed `.agents/skills/`, fan-out via `skill-sync`, how to invoke a skill), and point at the handful of skills a newcomer should know first (`ot-plans`, `openthrottle-generators`, `openthrottle-folders`, `skill-sync`).
5. **Wire it in.** Follow the repo's skill architecture: author under `skills/ot-onboarding/`, run `skill-sync` to fan out to `.agents/skills` + `.claude/skills`, register it in `skills/README.md` / `skills/AGENTS.md`, and pass the skill-sync `--check` drift gate.

## Non-goals
- Not a replacement for CLAUDE.md/MONOREPO.md/CONTRIBUTING.md — it orients and links, it doesn't re-document.
- No new tooling, generators, or MCP tools — pure skill authoring + wiring.

## Definition of done
`skills/ot-onboarding/SKILL.md` exists with correct frontmatter (`name`, discoverable `USE WHEN` description), covers the five areas above, is fanned out by `skill-sync`, registered in the skills README/AGENTS index, and passes `skill-sync --check`. Invoking `/ot-onboarding` (or the trigger phrases) produces a coherent guided on-ramp.

Shard the openthrottle-developer Vitest suite to recover CI wall-clock
## Context

The `openthrottle-developer` app has a large Vitest suite (~354 files / ~1,580 tests). It previously ran on `pool: 'vmForks'` for speed, but under CI memory pressure the reused vmForks worker accumulates V8 VM contexts and **crashes** — surfacing as in-flight files reporting `(0 test)` with no error stack and no Vitest summary. This is a flaky, non-deterministic CI failure with zero real assertion failures (seen on PR #264 / branch `ot/chat-idle-timeout-retry`, run 30667852303 — 4 unrelated `plans.$planId._index*` + `PlanWorkflowRunTransparency` files reported `(0 test)`).

**Immediate mitigation (applied on `ot/chat-idle-timeout-retry`), 3 parts:**
1. `applications/openthrottle-developer/vitest.config.ts`: `pool: 'vmForks'` -> `pool: 'forks'` (reclaims memory per file; stable) + top-level `maxWorkers: 4` to cap concurrency and bound peak memory. NOTE: Vitest 4 removed `poolOptions.forks.maxForks`/`minForks` and `minWorkers` — the cap is the top-level `maxWorkers` only, and `defineConfig` must be imported from `vitest/config` (not `vite`) for the `test` block to type-check.
2. `applications/openthrottle-developer/tests/setup.ts`: global `vi.mock('~/services/graphql-ws-client', () => ({ getGraphqlWsClient: () => null }))`. Switching to `forks` surfaced 4 pre-existing unhandled errors — test files that mount plan/task-detail routes open a real graphql-ws WebSocket (undici) that errors asynchronously after the test finishes; `vmForks` swallowed these on VM-context teardown, `forks` does not, so Vitest failed the run. Returning null matches the service's real SSR behavior and every subscription hook already guards for null.
3. Verified: full suite green under the final config — 354 files / 1,579 tests pass, 1 skipped, **0 errors**, exit 0. Wall-clock regressed (~90s under vmForks -> ~340s under forks; the `import`-per-file cost vmForks avoided).

## Goal

Recover the wall-clock regression from the vmForks -> forks switch by **sharding** the developer suite across CI runners/workers, so no single worker/process carries the entire 354-file graph. Keep stability (no return to the vmForks crash mode).

## Approach options to evaluate

- Vitest native `--shard=<i>/<n>` split across a CI matrix (parallel jobs), then merge coverage.
- Nx-level split / atomized test target (e.g. `n/ci` style per-file or per-folder targets) if it fits the Nx pipeline better than a manual matrix.
- Revisit `vmForks` **with** `memoryLimit` (Vitest 4 keeps `test.memoryLimit`) + a `maxWorkers` cap as an alternative to forks, benchmarking crash-resistance vs. speed.
- Tune `maxWorkers` / `fileParallelism` / `isolate` once sharding bounds per-shard memory.

## Constraints / notes

- Do not regress stability — the `(0 test)` crash must not reappear. Validate by running the full suite (and each shard) repeatedly under `CI=true`.
- `CI=true` is required locally to skip the interactive nx-sync prompt.
- Coverage must still merge correctly across shards (`coverage.provider: 'v8'`, reportsDirectory under `coverage/applications/openthrottle-developer`).
- Keep the config comment's rationale accurate as the pool/shard strategy evolves.
- Keep the shared-setup graphql-ws stub (or a per-shard equivalent) so subscription-mounting specs never open a real socket.
- This is a follow-up to the idle-timeout PR; not a blocker for it.
Split the 354-file developer test suite so no single Vitest worker carries the whole graph, recovering the wall-clock lost by moving vmForks -> forks for stability.

Tear down the unused validate-plan skill
## Why

`skills/validate-plan/SKILL.md` is an OT-owned skill that nothing invokes. It carries `disable-model-invocation: true`, so it can only ever fire as an explicit `/validate-plan` or as a lifecycle-hook `skillPath`, and no committed hook configuration, seed, or script attaches it. Its own body cross-references `docs/monorepo/lifecycle-hooks-design.md`, which does not exist in the repo — the design doc it was written against is gone. Meanwhile its frontmatter `description` sits in the always-on description budget of every session (docs/Skills.md § Always-on description budget), so it costs context on every run and returns nothing.

Its content is also fully redundant with what agents already do: `pnpm run check:local` / the affected lint+typecheck+test triad is documented in CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, and the ot-claude-loop skill.

## Scope of the reference audit (verified 2026-08-28)

Real references that must change:

- `skills/validate-plan/SKILL.md` — the skill itself (the only git-tracked file; the other three locations are gitignored generated symlinks).
- `.agents/skills/validate-plan` -> `../../skills/validate-plan`, `.claude/skills/validate-plan` and `.gemini/skills/validate-plan` -> `../../.agents/skills/validate-plan` — generated, reconciled by `ot-skill-sync`'s `sync.sh` straight from the filesystem. Do NOT `rm` these by hand.
- `docs/Skills.md:71` — lists validate-plan under "Agents/workflow".
- `docs/Skills.md:79` — the "Measured 2026-08-20: 20 skills, 6,212 chars, ~1,553 tokens" budget line goes stale (20 -> 19).
- `packages/nestjs-repositories/src/modules/skill-usage-events/skill-usage-outcomes.factory.ts:47` — `'validate-plan'` in a faker `arrayElement` pool for test/demo skill-usage rows.

Cosmetic references — test fixtures and placeholder copy that merely use the string as an example skill slug. They do not break, but they advertise a skill that no longer exists:

- `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routing/plans/data/data.copy.ts:113` (`skillSlugPlaceholder: 'e.g. validate-plan'`)
- `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routing/plans/components/__tests__/` — HookTaskList, AddHookDialog, PlanLifecycleHooks, PlanLifecycleHooksSection, PlanWorkflowConfigHookRowPrompt, PlanWorkflowConfigHookRowSelects
- `applications/openthrottle-server/src/graphql/plans/enqueue-plan-job-run-hooks.test.ts`
- `tools/workflows/src/utils/__tests__/hook-task-to-job-run-hook.test.ts`

## Known consideration (not a blocker)

The lifecycle-hooks feature is shipped (PlanLifecycleHooks UI, `enqueue-plan-job-run-hooks`, the hook-task -> job-run-hook bridge), and validate-plan was written as its canonical "validation-as-skill" reference implementation. Removing it leaves the hooks feature without a bundled example skill to attach. That is acceptable — an unused example costing always-on context is worse than no example — but the placeholder copy in task 4 should keep pointing at a skill that actually exists so the UI still teaches the shape.

## Out of scope

- Removing or changing the lifecycle-hooks feature itself.
- The pre-existing `docs/Skills.md:71` drift where `ot-loop` is missing from the Agents/workflow list — fix it opportunistically in task 2 since that line is already being edited.

Remove the OT-owned `validate-plan` skill from `skills/`, let ot-skill-sync reconcile the three generated symlinks, and clean up every doc/code reference so nothing points at a skill that no longer exists.

Enforce thin React Router route modules (route-primitive-shape)
Mirror the component-primitive-shape system for React Router route modules under `app/routes/*.tsx`.

## Problem

Route files are meant to stay thin and aligned with the route generator template (`tools/generators/src/generators/react-router/files/route/__name__.tsx`). In practice they accumulate module-scope helpers, constants, mappers, and config that belong in the feature folder under `app/routing/<area>/` (same layout the `folders` generator scaffolds: `components/`, `config/`, `data/`, `hooks/`, `utils/`).

Example violation: `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routes/skills.$slug.tsx` lines 29–60 define `SKILL_USAGE_RANGE_DAYS` and `toSkillDetailUsageData` at module scope inside the route file. Those should live under `app/routing/skills/` (e.g. `config/` / `utils/` / `data/`) and be imported back into the route.

## Goal

Add a second custom ESLint check in `@tools/dotfiles` (alongside `openthrottle/component-primitive-shape`) — tentatively `openthrottle/route-primitive-shape` — plus docs + optional audit script, so route modules stay template-shaped and non-route logic is hoisted into `app/routing/*`.

## Scope

- React Router apps with `app/routes/` + `app/routing/` (at least `openthrottle-developer`; extend to admin/email/website if they share the same layout).
- Generator template remains SSOT for the allowed route skeleton; the new doc/rule implement that contract.
- Canonical routing subtree already documented in `tools/generators/src/generators/folders/CANONICAL_ROUTING_SUBTREE.md` — reuse that destination map (utils/config/data/hooks).

## Out of scope

- Rewriting every existing route in one PR (inventory + phased remediation / opt-outs first).
- Changing React Router framework conventions (`loader`/`action`/`meta`/`handle`/`ErrorBoundary`/`default` export stay in the route file).
- Component-primitive-shape itself (already shipped).

## Success criteria

1. Written contract doc (e.g. `docs/monorepo/route-primitive-shape.md`) with stable rule ids (R1…).
2. ESLint rule in `tools/dotfiles` with unit tests + generator-template contract test (same pattern as `component-primitive-shape`).
3. Rule enabled on RR app route files; clear messages pointing at `app/routing/<area>/{utils,config,data,hooks}`.
4. Baseline inventory of current violations; at least the skills.$slug example (and similar easy wins) remediated as the reference fix.
5. Optional `audit:route-shape` script / `check:local` wiring when ready for a gate.

## Reference implementations to clone

- Rule: `tools/dotfiles/src/rules/component-primitive-shape.ts`
- Tests: `tools/dotfiles/src/__tests__/component-primitive-shape.test.ts`, `generator-template-contract.test.ts`
- Doc: `docs/monorepo/component-primitive-shape.md`
- Audit: `scripts/audit-component-shape.ts` + `pnpm run audit:component-shape*`
- Route template: `tools/generators/.../files/route/__name__.tsx`
- Routing folders: `CANONICAL_ROUTING_SUBTREE.md`

Scripts fresh coat of paint: shell → tsx, shared chalk UX, tests
# Scripts fresh coat of paint

## Why

`scripts/` is a mix of eras. ~30 scripts are already directly-executed TypeScript (`tsx ./scripts/*.ts` from package.json), many with Vitest coverage in `scripts/__tests__/`. But ~20 remain POSIX/bash shell (`create_worktree.sh`, the `setup_*.sh` family, `docker-smoke-test.sh`, `sync-subtree.sh`, `verify-openthrottle-mcp-env.sh`, `check-agent-assets-ssot.sh`, …) where logic is untyped, untested, and duplicated (env parsing, port lookups, logging). Meanwhile the .ts scripts themselves have no shared output conventions — exactly one (`setup_mcp-instructions.ts`) uses chalk; the rest are bare `console.log` with ad-hoc emoji.

Direction: keep leaning into executing `.ts` files directly (tsx / `node --experimental-strip-types`) so scripts get types, imports, shared utils, and tests — and use chalk (already in the pnpm catalog) for a consistent, pleasant CLI UX.

## Shape

1. **Shared toolkit first** — a `scripts/lib/` module (chalk logger with heading/step/success/warn/fail + verbose, env-file reader, exec/run helper, arg helper) with tests, piloted on 1–2 existing .ts scripts.
2. **Convert shell → .ts by family** — worktree scripts, setup scripts, standalone checks/utilities, MCP launchers — each family one task, preserving external contracts.
3. **Consistency pass** — adopt the shared toolkit across the existing .ts scripts so all output looks like one tool.

## Hard constraints (do not break)

- **Bootstrap ordering**: anything that runs before `pnpm install` has completed (parts of `setup_environment.sh` / `setup_software.sh`) cannot depend on node_modules (tsx, chalk). Keep a thin POSIX shim for the pre-install bootstrap; everything after install can be .ts.
- **`create_worktree.sh` is a Claude Code WorktreeCreate hook**: stdout must carry ONLY the worktree absolute path; all narration to stderr. It also has 3 invocation modes (CLI arg, hook JSON on stdin, provision-in-place). Any conversion must preserve this contract exactly and be verified against all 3 modes.
- **`worktree_ports.sh` is *sourced*, not exec'd** (exports OT_PORT_* into the caller). A .ts replacement needs an explicit design: print eval-able exports, or fold it into the .ts worktree provisioner as an import (preferred — imports are the whole point of the .ts move).
- **nx.json references**: `check-agent-assets-ssot.sh` is wired as a monorepo target with explicit `{workspaceRoot}` input globs (the root project owns 0 files — default inputs would hash nothing and cache-hit forever). Update the command AND the input globs on conversion.
- **MCP launcher scripts** (`run-openthrottle-mcp.sh`, `run-github-mcp.sh`, `mcp-git.sh`) are referenced from user-global MCP client configs written by `setup_mcp-instructions.ts`. Converting them means updating the emitted config and communicating a re-run of `pnpm run setup:mcp-instructions`.
- Scripts run via `tsx --env-file .env` in package.json — preserve the env-file behavior per script.
- No new TS enums; `as const`; explicit return types; `import type` (repo rules apply to scripts too).

## Conventions to establish (task 1 makes these concrete)

- One shared logger: chalk-based, honors NO_COLOR / non-TTY (chalk does this natively), stderr for narration in stdout-contract scripts.
- Exit-code discipline: non-zero on failure, `--strict` pattern where audits warn vs fail (matches existing audit-*.ts).
- Every converted script gets a Vitest file in `scripts/__tests__/` for its extractable logic (pure functions exported; thin main() shell).
- Testing recipe follows existing patterns (e.g. `openthrottle-database-migrations.test.ts`, `bootstrap-service-account-credentials.test.ts`).

## Out of scope

- `_worktree.sh` legacy shim if it's dead — delete rather than convert (verify with git grep + check-ignore first).
- Behavior changes to what scripts DO (migrations, seeding, GCS upload logic). This is a re-platform + UX pass, not a redesign.
- `skills/ot-skill-sync/scripts/sync.sh` (owned by the skills architecture, runs pre-install).
Modernize the highly useful scripts/ toolbox: continue the shift to directly-executed .ts (tsx) so scripts get types, imports, shared utils and Vitest coverage, and introduce a shared chalk-based CLI toolkit for a consistent, pleasant UX across every script.

Repositories route: nested table + toolbar + pagination
# Repositories route: nested table + toolbar + pagination

## Problem

`/settings/repositories` renders `RepositoriesSection` → a `<ul>` of `RepositoryCard`, one card per repository, each card containing an inner `<ul>` of checkouts with three inline `<Form>` action buttons apiece. This reads fine at 2–3 workspaces and degrades badly past ~10: no search, no sort, no pagination, and every checkout's full action set is always expanded on screen.

Every other list route in openthrottle-developer already converged on the same shape — `XxxToolbar` + `XxxTable` (shadcn `DataTable`) + `OpenThrottlePagination`, all state in search params, loader does filter/sort/slice. See `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routes/projects._index.tsx` as the canonical exemplar. Repositories is the outlier.

## Goal

Bring `/settings/repositories` in line with that pattern, while representing the repository → primary checkout → worktree hierarchy that a flat table would flatten away.

## Decisions (settled with the owner)

1. **Row grain: one row per checkout, nested.** Not one row per repository. But the rows are not flat — a repository's `kind: 'primary'` checkout is the parent row and its `kind: 'worktree'` checkouts nest beneath it as indented, expandable child rows. This is real data, not a derived guess: `RepositoryCheckoutObject.kind` is `'primary' | 'worktree'` and `packages/nestjs-repositories/src/modules/repositories/repository-checkouts.service.ts` genuinely writes `'worktree'` via `recordWorktreeCheckout` (`kind: data.kind ?? 'primary'` on the ordinary create path).
2. **Table only — retire the cards.** No `view=table|card` toggle. `RepositoryCard.tsx` and its test are deleted. The rich per-repository view already exists at the detail route `settings.repositories.$repositoryId._index.tsx`.

## Shape of the change

**Pagination unit is the parent row.** Paginate over primary checkouts (parent rows); a parent always carries its worktree children with it so a group is never split across a page boundary. `totalCount` = number of parent rows after filtering.

**Search** matches across repository name, checkout `displayName`, `filesystemPath`, `normalizedRemoteUrl`, and current branch. A child match pulls its parent in (and auto-expands that group), so searching a worktree branch name never yields an orphan row.

**Sort** at minimum: repository name, last updated, checkout count. Children sort within their parent group, never globally.

**Row actions** (refresh checkout, apply editor config, remove) move from three always-visible buttons into a single per-row actions menu. They stay `<Form method="post">` submissions against the existing `action` intents — no behavior change, no new mutations, no GraphQL/schema changes, no codegen. `settings.repositories._index.tsx.graphql` is untouched.

**`DataTable` needs sub-row support.** `packages/react-router-shadcn/src/components/DataTable.tsx` currently wires only `getCoreRowModel`. Nesting requires optional `getSubRows` + `getExpandedRowModel` + expansion state. This must be strictly additive — every existing caller (`ProjectsTable`, `PlansTable`, `SkillsTable`, `RulesTable`, `NotesTable`, `QueuesTable`, `PersonasTable`, `PullRequestsTable`, `ScheduleTable`, and the settings tables) passes neither prop and must render byte-identically.

## Non-goals

- No server-side pagination. Loader-side filter/sort/slice over `workspaceRepositories`, same as Projects does today.
- No changes to the repository detail or edit routes.
- No changes to `AddFolderDialog`, `CloneRepoDialog`, `AddFolderResult`, `DirectoryPicker`, or the picker/browse flow — those keep working exactly as they do now, above the table.
- No GraphQL schema, resolver, or migration work.

## Conventions

- Scaffold components with the generator, do not hand-write: `NX_ISOLATE_PLUGINS=false pnpm nx g @tools/generators:react-router --subGenerator=component --application=openthrottle-developer --folder=settings/repositories --name=RepositoriesTable,RepositoriesToolbar,RepositoryRowActions`.
- Keep the generated `// Hooks / Setup / Handlers / Markup / Life Cycle / 🔌 Short Circuit` section comments even when empty.
- Components export only the component + its props interface; lists/copy live in the nearest `data/` (`data.copy.ts`).
- No new TS enums — `as const` objects. No `as` casts. Alphabetized props/keys. `component` not `screen` in tests, `userEvent` not `fireEvent`.

## Validation

`pnpm nx run openthrottle-developer:lint`, `:typecheck`, `:test`, plus `pnpm nx run react-router-shadcn:test` for the `DataTable` change. Then `pnpm nx run openthrottle-developer:dev` and exercise the route by hand: expand/collapse, search hitting a worktree, sort, page 2, and each of the three row actions.
Replace the card list on /settings/repositories with a RepositoriesTable (nested primary checkout → worktree rows), RepositoriesToolbar (search + sort), and OpenThrottlePagination, matching the Projects/Skills/Rules route pattern. Retire RepositoryCard.

Pagination result label: /plans says "projects"
## Problem

On `/plans`, the pagination summary reads **"Showing 1–25 of 29 projects"** — it should say **plans**.

## Root cause

`OpenThrottlePagination` (`packages/react-router-ui/src/components/OpenThrottlePagination.tsx:40`) already supports a `resultLabel` prop, but it silently defaults to `'projects'`:

```ts
resultLabel = 'projects',
```

Any call site that forgets the prop inherits the wrong noun with no type error and no visual signal. The label IS already customizable — the defect is the entity-specific default plus two call sites that never opted in.

## Audit of every `OpenThrottlePagination` call site

| Call site | Entity | Passes `resultLabel`? | Renders |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routes/plans._index.tsx:203` | plans | no | "… of N **projects**" 🐞 |
| `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routing/projects/components/ProjectDetailTabs.tsx:161` | project **tasks** | no | "… of N **projects**" 🐞 |
| `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routes/projects._index.tsx:171` | projects | no (relies on default) | correct by accident |
| `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routes/skills._index.tsx:218` | skills | yes — `"skills"` | correct |
| `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routes/prompts._index.tsx:164` | prompts | yes — `"prompts"` | correct |
| `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routes/search._index.tsx:166` | results | yes — `"results"` | correct |
| `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routes/queues.$queueId._index.tsx:151` (`OpenThrottlePaginationSimple`) | jobs | yes — `"jobs"` | correct |

`OpenThrottlePaginationSimple` (`packages/react-router-ui/src/components/OpenThrottlePaginationSimple.tsx:29`) has the same prop but a safe neutral default (`'results'`) — that is the shape to converge on.

Note the same entity-specific bleed exists in the pagination internals: the shared `basePath` default is `/projects` and the query-string builder is `buildProjectsSearchParams` / `ProjectsSearchParamsExtras`. Renaming those is out of scope here, but worth flagging.

## Approach

1. Fix the two wrong call sites (`resultLabel="plans"`, `resultLabel="tasks"`).

CI: shard affected lint/typecheck/test across free runners
Re-enable the already-wired GitHub Actions matrix so `lint` / `typecheck` / `test` can run across a few free `ubuntu-latest` boxes instead of one.

## Why now

The shard loop in `.github/workflows/continuous-integration.yml` (the commented `parallelize-tasks.ts` step around the SCALING RISK note) and `scripts/parallelize-tasks.ts` were **disabled by design as a cost tradeoff**, not because the wiring was unfinished. That tradeoff died when CI moved to GitHub-hosted `ubuntu-latest` on this **public** repo (plan `6ced8d0e`): standard-runner minutes are unlimited and free. The remaining constraints are wall-clock (30-minute job ceiling), queue contention, and not wasting N× checkout/install on shards that do not pay for themselves.

Today the `build` job is still a 1×1 matrix (`jobCount: 1`, `jobIndex: [1]`, single `target: ['lint,typecheck,test']`). `ci-success` already exists as the stable required check so branch protection does **not** pin a matrix-suffixed job name — keep it that way.

## Do not blindly uncomment

Uncommenting the shard loop as-is would be wrong:

- The live `NX ${{ matrix.target }} affected` step would still run the **full** affected set on every box, then the shard loop would run it again. Replace, do not stack.
- Codegen drift, circular-deps, licenses, prettier, agent-asset SSOT, and `audit:strict` are **once-per-run** gates. Running them on every shard multiplies checkout+install for no coverage gain. Keep them on `jobIndex == 1` or extract a sibling `gates` job.
- The Nx Actions cache key is `…-${{ github.sha }}` with no shard suffix. N matrix legs of the same SHA race the save; only the first write wins and the others' task hashes are discarded. Include `matrix.jobIndex` (and `matrix.target` if targets split) in the key; keep the existing restore-key prefixes so shards still warm from prior runs.
- `parallelize-tasks.ts` takes `github.ref` as argv[5] and never uses it. The unquoted `${{ matrix.target }}` form breaks if a target ever contains spaces (`test --coverage`). Empty shards print nothing and the `while read` loop succeeds without running Nx — that is correct, but must stay explicit in comments/tests.
- Round-robin by project name (apps first, then packages) does **not** split `openthrottle-developer`'s Vitest suite. That suite is one Nx project; project sharding will not make it smaller. The vmForks + `vmMemoryLimit` work (plan `e448a51d` / PR #267) stays the lever for that suite. Per-box `nx affected --target=test --parallel` is a **separate** evidence-gated follow-up (see the serialized-test comment in the workflow); do not flip it in the same change as sharding.

## Recommended shape (v1)

Start with **project sharding**, not a target × jobIndex cross product:

- `jobCount: 2` or `3` (same integer as `jobIndex: [1, 2]` / `[1, 2, 3]` — they MUST stay in sync).
- Keep a single `target: ['lint,typecheck,test']` so v1 is 2–3 boxes, not 9.
- `strategy.fail-fast: false` so one red shard does not cancel the others (better signal).
- Each shard runs lint + typecheck + test **only for its project chunk** via `parallelize-tasks.ts` → `nx affected --exclude="*,$tags"`.
- Once-per-run gates stay on one box.

Measure current step timings on a fat affected graph **before** picking 2 vs 3. Typical `build` is ~6 min (ci-cost.md, 2026-08-18); checkout + `pnpm install` is a large fraction of that. If setup is ~2 min/box, a 3-box split of a 6-minute job can lose the wall-clock win. Shard count should be the smallest N where worst-case (full affected, approaching the 30 m ceiling) clearly improves, not a decorative matrix.

Target-split (`target: [lint, typecheck, test]`, still `jobCount: 1`) is a simpler alternative if measurement shows project shards are setup-bound: it parallelizes lint/typecheck against test but leaves the heavy test graph on one box. Record the choice in the workflow comment and in `docs/monorepo/ci-cost.md`.

## Docs / comments to retarget

The "deferred by design / cost tradeoff" language is now stale in:

- `.github/workflows/continuous-integration.yml` (SCALING RISK block, shard-loop comment, serialized-test note)
- `docs/monorepo/ci-cost.md` (open item on `--parallel=1`; note that minutes are free so the shard decision is wall-clock vs queue, not spend)
- `docs/monorepo/CI-quality-gates.md` (P4 row: sharded test is Off, tracked by the old coverage plan)
- `docs/monorepo/NX.md` ("pinned to a single runner as a deliberate cost tradeoff")
- `docs/reliability/developer-vitest-pool.md` and the matching comment in `applications/openthrottle-developer/vitest.config.ts` ("runners we intentionally don't pay for")

Related completed work: CI cost / free runners `6ced8d0e`; developer Vitest pool `e448a51d`. P4 in CI-quality-gates currently points at "Improve test coverage and CI test execution" — retarget that row at **this** plan once created.

## Success

A ready PR (or a few consecutive runs on a scratch branch) shows: shards partition affected projects with no overlap and no silent empty success when work existed; once-per-run gates still run exactly once; `ci-success` is green iff every shard + the changes gate succeeded; draft/docs skips still skip; no `(0 test)` OOM files; docs match the live matrix.
Shipped as PR #397 (merged, 97a3210a). CI now runs `lint,typecheck,test` across a 3-box `ubuntu-latest` project-shard matrix with fail-fast: false; `ci-success` remains the single required check.

Delivered: measured baseline chose N=3 over 2 and over a target-split (setup is ~1.6 min/box, 6-9% of the job, so shards are not setup-bound); `parallelize-tasks.ts` rewritten with types, 25 unit tests, and a round-trip self-check that exits non-zero if a shard's selector does not resolve back to exactly its chunk — which caught a silent-drop bug where the root `monorepo` project would have fallen off every shard while CI stayed green; eight whole-tree gates pinned to `matrix.jobIndex == 1`; the Nx Actions cache key gained an optional per-shard suffix (also applied to nx-dependency-graph and the vercel-deploy per-app matrix, where the same race was latent); six stale "deferred as a cost tradeoff" locations retargeted, including correcting a false claim that the affected test step ran `--parallel=1`.

Validated across four consecutive green non-docs PR runs plus one fat-affected main run: disjoint partition, explicit empty-shard no-op, no cache-save race, no OOM/(0 test) markers, longest fat shard 17m01s against a 28m24s single-box worst case.

Known limits, deliberately out of scope: `openthrottle-developer` is one Nx project and cannot be split by project sharding (vmForks / plan e448a51d stays the lever), and `nx affected --target=test --parallel` remains evidence-gated. Going private re-prices every box.

SSR-friendly frontmatter splitter for skill rendering ({ content, metadata })
# Problem

The skill detail route `/skills/:slug` (e.g. `/skills/create-cli`) reads the raw `SKILL.md` off disk in `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routing/skills/data/read-skill-file.server.ts` and passes the **entire file — YAML frontmatter block included — as `content`** to `SkillDetailTabs`. Every skill file begins with a `---` … `---` frontmatter block (name, description, metadata), so that raw YAML is rendered verbatim to the client instead of being parsed out.

We want a **SSR-friendly** helper that, given the raw file string, returns:

```ts
interface SplitFrontmatterResult {
  content: string;                    // the file body, frontmatter stripped
  metadata: Record<string, unknown>;  // the parsed frontmatter as an object
}
```

# Existing building blocks (reuse — do NOT add gray-matter)

`@openthrottle/openthrottle-skills` (already a `workspace:^` dependency of `openthrottle-developer`) already ships the two halves, both pure-JS / SSR-safe (backed by the `yaml` package, no `fs`/Buffer/DOM):

- `extractContentAfterFrontmatter(fileContent)` — tri-state body: original string when there is no frontmatter, the substring after the closing `---` when well-formed, and `null` when a block opens but never closes (malformed). Source: `packages/openthrottle-skills/src/frontmatter/extract-frontmatter-body.ts`.
- `parseYamlFrontmatter(fileContent)` — `{ fields }` where fields is `Record<string, FrontmatterScalar>` (a constrained `string | boolean | readonly string[] | undefined` union, not `Record<string, unknown>`). Source: `packages/openthrottle-skills/src/frontmatter/parse-yaml-frontmatter.ts`.

No combined `{ content, metadata }` function exists. `gray-matter` is NOT a dependency and should not be added — it drags in Buffer/`fs` shims and bundles poorly for SSR; the `yaml`-based path already covers us.

# Design decision to lock during task 1

The requested `metadata: Record<string, unknown>` is looser than the package's existing `FrontmatterScalar`-typed `fields`. Two viable approaches — pick one in task 1:

- **(Recommended) Widen from the existing parser.** Call `parseYamlFrontmatter` + `extractContentAfterFrontmatter`, return `{ content: body, metadata: fields }`. `Record<string, FrontmatterScalar>` is assignable to `Record<string, unknown>`, so the public return type is exactly `ResponseType` while behavior stays consistent with the rest of the codebase (same coercions, same unsupported-construct handling, same last-value-wins). Lowest risk, zero new YAML semantics.
- **Raw `yaml` parse for richer metadata.** Re-parse the frontmatter body with the `yaml` package directly to preserve nested maps/numbers/etc. as real values. Only choose this if a consumer actually needs nested/typed metadata; it diverges from the established scalar contract and needs its own corpus coverage.

# Malformed / edge-case contract to define

So `/settings/setup` lands first as a "which CLIs are installed + version" page (task 5), and the **install/update controls are a gated add-on** (tasks 3–4, 6) layered on once task 1's owner gate clears. Tasks split accordingly so the security surface never blocks shipping the status page.

## Core design decisions (locked in task 1)

1. **Install metadata belongs on the driver registry** (leaf, dep-free) as an optional `install`/`update` descriptor, so setup_software.sh and the server both derive from ONE source and can't drift. All 5 agent CLIs are `curl | shell` installers today (the brew items — openjdk, terraform, maestro — are NOT agent CLIs and are OUT of scope). So v1 only needs a `curl-shell` method: `{ url, installerShell: 'bash' | 'sh' }`. Update = re-run installer, unless a CLI has a real self-update subcommand (research per CLI: `claude update`, codex/grok/opencode/cursor equivalents).
2. **The confirmation moves to the UI.** The shell's interactive `read confirm_install` prompt is dropped; installers must run non-interactively. The Install/Update button IS the confirm.
3. **Security surface = the human gate.** Running `curl -fsSL <url> | bash` on the server host is effectively remote-code-execution-on-demand. It must be: (a) locked to registry-defined commands for an allowlisted backend — the mutation takes only a `backend` string validated against `ALL_DRIVERS`, never a URL/command from the client; (b) gated behind a WRITE permission (SETTINGS_WRITE or a dedicated `AGENT_SETUP_MANAGE`), not SETTINGS_READ; (c) gated behind an env/feature flag, DEFAULT-OFF for hosted/multi-tenant deploys — this is a local-developer-machine feature. This is the owner-judgment gate and blocks the install/update tasks (2–4, 6), NOT the read-only status view (task 5).
4. **Execution model:** install/update is long-running with streamed output. Decide sync-mutation-returns-runId + graphql-ws subscription (mirror conversation-stream) vs a BullMQ job. Invalidate the discovery SWR cache on success so the UI re-reflects state. Watch the PATH gotcha: installers drop binaries in ~/.local/bin (or similar) — the server process's PATH must include the install target dir or post-install discovery won't see the new binary.

- brew packages / maestro / python software in setup_software.sh.
- Auth/login for each CLI (install ≠ authenticated). Note it but don't build it.

Stable fix for the stale in-session openthrottle-mcp (connected but silently 401ing)
## Problem

`openthrottle-mcp` runs as a **long-lived stdio child** of the MCP client (Claude/Cursor), launched once at session start via `scripts/run-openthrottle-mcp.sh`. If it launches with an empty/invalid `OPENTHROTTLE_MCP_AUTH_TOKEN`, the client still connects and lists tools — but **every authenticated tool call 401s** for the rest of the session. It looks connected; it is dead. Recovery requires provisioning/fixing the token AND a client reconnect — and in the 2026-08-05 session the `/mcp reconnect` control was repeatedly unavailable ("MCP controls aren't available right now"), so the stale process could not be relaunched from the UI. Net: many wasted turns diagnosing, and OT writes only succeeded via a one-off stdio-fallback launcher.

Root symptom seen: `.mcp.json` passes `"OPENTHROTTLE_MCP_AUTH_TOKEN": "${OPENTHROTTLE_MCP_AUTH_TOKEN}"`; when the launching shell doesn't export it, that interpolates to empty, and the process was already running before the token was valid — so it held an empty token even though `.env` had a valid one.

## Already done (partial mitigation — track to merge)

On branch `fix/ot-mcp-token-placeholder-selfload` (draft PR pending):
- `run-openthrottle-mcp.sh` now does a **launch-time auth preflight**: refuses to start (loud banner + `exit 1`) when the token is unset or the server rejects it, so the client surfaces "failed to start" instead of silently connecting broken. Opt-out `OT_MCP_SKIP_PREFLIGHT=1`.
- Fixed a false-pass bug: the server answers auth failures with **HTTP 200 + an `errors` array** (with `"path":["listSources"]`), so a naive `grep "listSources"` passed a bad token. Both the preflight and `verify-openthrottle-mcp-env.sh` now decide on the body (`errors` ⇒ rejected).

## Residual gaps this plan must close

1. **Mid-session staleness.** The preflight only runs at launch. A token valid at boot but rotated/revoked later still 401s until the next relaunch — inherent to a long-lived stdio process. Need detection/refresh (periodic re-check, per-request token resolution, or a self-heal).
2. **Reconnect reliability.** When the client's reconnect control is unavailable, there's no in-band way to recover. Investigate a reliable relaunch path and/or a `whoami`/auth-status signal the client can act on.
3. **Prevent empty-token-at-launch.** Guarantee the launcher resolves a valid token before exec (it self-loads from `.env`, but ordering/placeholder edge cases remain), and align `.mcp.json` env handling so an unset shell var can't silently become an empty bearer token.

## Goal

Make it impossible to operate against a stale/broken MCP without a loud, actionable signal, and provide a reliable recovery path — covering launch-time (done), mid-session, and prevention.

## Key references
- `scripts/run-openthrottle-mcp.sh` (launcher + new preflight), `scripts/verify-openthrottle-mcp-env.sh`
- `.mcp.json` env block (`${OPENTHROTTLE_MCP_AUTH_TOKEN}` interpolation), `.cursor/mcp.json.example`
- Auth: `packages/openthrottle-mcp/src/auth/get-auth-token.ts` (resolution order: per-request store → env), `packages/openthrottle-mcp/docs/AUTH.md`
- Server returns HTTP 200 + `errors` (UNAUTHENTICATED) on bad token
- Prior findings: openthrottle-mcp auth config shadowing; OT MCP stdio fallback; OT MCP health-check first

Model discovery caching: faster repeat loads
## Problem

Agent-CLI and local-model discovery feel slow on repeat loads. Investigation of the current caching found that the ONLY real cache is two 60s in-process singleton caches on the server; the client re-fetches on every mount/navigation, and the home loader amplifies each load into 2x calls per query. Every ~60s the next request pays the full cold cost (spawning up to 5 `--version` + 3 `<cli> models` child processes with 3s/5s timeouts, plus ~48 HTTP probes for local models).

## Current caching (as-is)

- **Local models** — `NestjsModelDiscoveryService` (`packages/nestjs-model-discovery/src/nestjs-model-discovery.service.ts`): singleton, 60s TTL (`LLM_DISCOVERY_CACHE_TTL_MS`, default 60_000), has both cache + `inFlight` promise coalescing + `invalidate()`. Good citizen.
- **Agent CLIs** — `AgentDiscoveryService` (`applications/openthrottle-server/src/graphql/agent-discovery/agent-discovery.service.ts`): singleton, `CACHE_TTL_MS = 60_000`, cache-only. **NO in-flight dedup** — concurrent cache-miss callers each launch a full CLI sweep.
- **Client** — none. `executeGraphqlWithAuth` is plain fetch; no React Query/Apollo/localStorage/Jotai memoization. No HTTP cache headers on resolvers.

## Repeat-load amplifiers

- Home route loader `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routes/_index.tsx` fires all three discovery loaders every load; `loadDriverEndpointModels` (`models.server.ts`) re-issues BOTH GraphQL queries, so one home load triggers `discoverLocalModels` x2 and `discoverAgentClis` x2 (deduped only by the 60s server TTL, not the client).
- Header chat `useHeaderChatController.tsx` calls `optionsFetcher.load('/resources/chat-options')` per mount; a page reload re-fetches. `routes/resources.chat-options.tsx` re-runs both discovery loaders.
- Both loaders swallow errors -> `[]`, so failures silently re-probe next time.
- Multi-instance/serverless server deployments each keep their own in-memory cache -> low hit rate.

## GraphQL surface

- `discoverLocalModels` -> `ModelDiscoveryResolver` -> `NestjsModelDiscoveryService`
- `discoverAgentClis` -> `AgentDiscoveryResolver` -> `AgentDiscoveryService`
- Both guarded by `@Permissions(SETTINGS_READ)`. MCP tools go through the same cached queries.

## Levers to evaluate/apply

1. In-flight coalescing on `AgentDiscoveryService` (parity with model-discovery).
2. Stale-while-revalidate / background refresh: serve last-good snapshot instantly, refresh out of band, so repeat loads never pay cold cost.
3. Dedupe the double-fetch in `_index.tsx` / `loadDriverEndpointModels`.
4. Client-side caching so repeat mounts/navigations don't re-hit the server (persist loader result + `shouldRevalidate`, and/or HTTP cache headers on the resolvers).
5. Optional: shared cache (Redis) for multi-instance deployments — evaluate cost/benefit vs longer TTL.

## Approach

Design-first: task 1 measures current repeat-load cost and locks the chosen levers before code changes. Keep changes behind the existing config knobs where possible. Validate repeat-load latency drops and add regression tests.
Speed up agent-CLI + local-model discovery on repeat loads: add in-flight coalescing + stale-while-revalidate to the server caches, dedupe the home-loader double-fetch, and add client-side caching so repeat mounts/navigations don't re-probe.

Explore & ship a curated MCP **connectors** catalog with a connect flow, surfaced under `/settings/mcp` in `openthrottle-developer`.

## Context / gap
OpenThrottle today exposes *its own* tools **as** an MCP server (`packages/openthrottle-mcp`, `applications/openthrottle-server/src/modules/mcp-developer`). It has **no** concept of the platform *connecting to external* MCP servers (GitHub, Slack, Notion…) that agents could later consume. This plan adds the first vertical slice: a curated catalog + connect/enable flow.

## Locked decisions (2026-07-31)
- **Baseline** = curated **top ~10** connectors seeded across **3 registry/host providers**: (1) Anthropic connector directory, (2) the official MCP registry, (3) vendor-hosted remote MCP. Live registry tools returned nothing in-session, so Task 1 curates from known connectors rather than a live pull.
- **Scope** = **catalog + connect flow**: browse → connect (store credential / OAuth reference, mirroring `settings.keys`) → enable/disable. **No agent-run wiring** in this plan (explicit follow-up).
- **Route** = **`/settings/mcp`** (`settings.mcp._index.tsx` + `settings.mcp.$connectorId.tsx`).

## Proposed top-10 (finalized in Task 1)
GitHub, Linear, Notion, Slack, Atlassian (Jira/Confluence), Sentry, Google Drive, Figma, Stripe, Postgres/Supabase — each tagged with its source provider + auth type (OAuth vs token) + remote transport config.

## Key patterns to follow
- Flat routes (`settings.mcp.*.tsx`) + companion `.graphql` docs + `__tests__`; logic/components under `app/routing/settings/`.
- Credential storage mirrors the service-account-credential flow in `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routes/settings.keys.tsx` and its server resolvers.
- Code-first GraphQL in `openthrottle-server` (Result/ListResult types; never break fields, `@deprecated`); regenerate `applications/openthrottle-server/schema.gql` + codegen.
- Generators first (`NX_ISOLATE_PLUGINS=false pnpm nx g @tools/generators:react-router --subGenerator=...`), one component/file, keep section comments, no TS enums (`as const`).
- Authed pages need permissions → prefer render-level Vitest (repo memory: developer-app-live-verify-auth-permission).

## Out of scope (future plans)
Wiring enabled connectors into live agent runs / drivers; per-connector tool allow-lists; org-vs-user connection scoping beyond the baseline.
Curated top-10 MCP connectors catalog (seeded across 3 registry/host providers) with a connect + enable/disable flow, surfaced at /settings/mcp in openthrottle-developer. No agent-run wiring in this plan.

openthrottle-showroom: typed TS video scripts, variants and YouTube-ready metadata
# openthrottle-showroom

Season 1's content pipeline outgrew both its file format and its address.

**The address.** The screencast pipeline lives at `applications/openthrottle-developer/tests/demo/` — nine directories of runner, TTS, ffmpeg assembly, leak scanning, typeset surfaces, fixtures and a demo-database seeder, parked inside an app's test folder. It stopped being test scaffolding for that app several tasks ago.

**The format.** `docs/marketing/scripts/05-connect-ot-mcp.md` is the proof: YAML front matter plus a markdown beats table, parsed independently by three ad-hoc regex parsers, with A/B variants expressed as **copy-pasted sibling files** (`05-connect-ot-mcp-v0.md` … `-v3.md`, plus the canonical `05-connect-ot-mcp.md` — five near-identical files for one episode).

This plan does both, in that order: **scaffold `packages/openthrottle-showroom` and relocate the pipeline into it first**, then build the typed layer in its final home. One **typed TypeScript episode module per video**: variants as an array, metadata grouped by concern, and the YouTube publishing surface (title patterns, description block, tag baseline, playlists, chapters, thumbnails) modelled in types rather than described in prose.

## What is wrong today

**Format.** YAML front matter is stringly-typed. `format`, `status`, `recording`, `release`, `blockedOn`, `titleCard`, `tags` are all validated (when at all) by three separate regexes in three files:

- `scripts/validate-video-scripts.ts` — budget check; **rewrites `spokenWords` back into the file**, a derived value stored as source.
- `.../tests/demo/narrate/parse-script.ts` — the TTS input path.
- `.../tests/demo/assemble/assemble.ts` — pulls `title` and `titleCard` by regex and scrapes tags with `/^ {2}- (.+)$/gm`, which matches **any** two-space bullet anywhere in the file, not just the `tags:` block.

Three parsers, three notions of what a script is, no compiler.

**Variants.** There is no room for A/B testing an episode. Today it is five files that share a `release: 6`, drift independently, all get counted by the validator, and give the pipeline no way to say "render variant 3, keep variant 1's take on disk".

**Metadata.** Flat and half-derived. The description block in `assemble.ts` is hardcoded; playlist, chapters, thumbnail copy, publish state and `blockedOn` never reach `metadata.json`. `docs/marketing/youtube-format.md` and `publishing.md` specify the title patterns, the verbatim description block, the 6–10 tag rule with a 5-tag baseline, four playlists and the long-form chapter list — all prose, none enforced.

## The package

`packages/openthrottle-showroom`, generated with `@tools/generators:package` (`--type=node`) and following the `openthrottle-mcp` naming precedent. It owns the whole content pipeline end to end:

```text
src/
├── episodes/    # typed episode modules — the new script format
├── flows/       # demo flows (transcriptions of the action column)
├── surfaces/    # typeset shell/HTML surfaces
├── fixtures/    # the fictional demo workspace
├── runner/      # Playwright capture
├── narrate/     # TTS + timings
├── assemble/    # ffmpeg masters, captions, cards, metadata
└── scan/        # leak scan
```

The `video-record`, `video-narrate`, `video-assemble`, `video-scan` and `video-seed` Nx targets move with it.

**Source-first, private, OpenThrottle-only.** No `build` target — `main`/`types` point at `./src/index.ts` and consumers transpile the source, matching `packages/nodejs-utils` and `packages/react-router-chat`. `private: true`, tagged `publish:false` and `production:false` (content tooling, not code in a deployed app). Nothing outside this repo consumes it, so it is not designed for external consumers: no generalised plugin seams, no abstraction built for a second user that does not exist. Depending on repo internals is expected. Shipping it on its own is a later decision with its own evidence.

**The one coupling to protect through the move:** the demo README argues the pipeline sits beside `tests/e2e/` because a demo video *is* an E2E flow, and both must drive the **same** selectors so the app never grows two parallel sets of test hooks. Leaving the app does not dissolve that constraint, it just makes it easier to break silently — so it gets an explicit mechanism, not a hope.

## The script shape

One module per episode, roughly:

```ts
export const episode: VideoEpisode = {
  id: '05-connect-ot-mcp',
  format: 'short',
  production: { recording: 'live', flow: '05-connect-ot-mcp', titleCard: [...], blockedOn: [] },
  release: { order: 6, status: 'draft', playlist: 'getting-started' },
  youtube: { title: '...', summary: '...', tags: [...], chapters: [...] },
  selectedVariant: 'payoff-first',
  variants: [
    { id: 'payoff-first', thesis: '...', beats: [{ t: '0:00', action: '...', narration: '...' }] },
    ...
  ],
};
```

Derived values (`spokenWords`, estimated spoken seconds, budget headroom) are **computed, never stored** — which deletes the validator's file-rewriting step entirely.

## Principles

- **Scaffold before you move, move before you rewrite.** The relocation is a diff a human can read only if it is a move and nothing else.
- **One loader, one type.** Narrate, assemble, scan and the validator all read the same typed registry. A field exists once.
- **Variants are first class, takes are namespaced.** `--variant` threads through narrate → record → assemble; outputs land under `output/<slug>/<variant>/` and the variant id is recorded in `timings.json` and `metadata.json`, so a take always traces to the words that produced it.
- **YouTube rules become types + tests.** Title pattern, tag baseline, playlist enum, chapter requirements and the standard description block move out of prose and into the module the assembler already emits from.
- **The narration column stays the literal TTS input** and the action column stays the literal flow step. The format changes; the contract does not.
- **Nothing aspirational ships.** `status` + `blockedOn` gate publishing in the validator, as the publish checklist already asks of a human.
- **Build for this repo only.** The package has exactly one consumer and it is this monorepo.

## Out of scope

- Publishing the package, or designing its API for anyone outside this repo.
- Upload automation. `publishing.md` sets the trigger for that; this plan does not move it.
- Re-recording or re-writing existing episodes. Migration is mechanical and content-preserving.
- Changing the beat structure, the format spec (`docs/marketing/format.json`) or the demo flows themselves.
- The demo database's separateness, which the task-3 spike settled and this plan carries over unchanged.
Scaffold an openthrottle-showroom package, relocate the whole recording pipeline into it, and replace YAML+markdown video scripts with typed TS episode modules: variants as an array for A/B, metadata grouped by concern, YouTube publishing rules modelled in types rather than prose.

Test-coverage guard-rail: warn-mode audit:test-coverage for routes/components/hooks/utils
## Goal

Extend our custom `audit:*` guard-rails with a **test-coverage audit** that enforces every route, component, hook, and util ships a co-located spec matching the starting point our generators scaffold. We've split the UI into many small, easy-to-work-with components and moved a lot around — great for maintainability, but it opened significant test gaps. This audit surfaces those gaps.

**Ship in warning mode first** (report-only, non-blocking). Once the baseline is captured, we carve out separate remediation plans to fill the gaps, then flip categories to strict.

## Prior art (reuse, don't reinvent)

Our audits are repo-root `scripts/audit-*.ts` run via `tsx`, exposed as `audit:*` npm scripts, **report-only by default** with `--strict` → `process.exit(1)`, `--json` for baselines, and a first-line opt-out pragma. Cross-file/repo-wide dimensions live in scripts; per-file dimensions live in `@tools/dotfiles` ESLint rules. The component-shape gate is mirrored byte-identical across `.husky/lib/component-shape-gate.sh`, `.husky/pre-commit`, `.husky/pre-push`, and CI.

- Cleanest template to copy: `scripts/audit-route-shape.ts` (single walker, `--json`/`--strict`, report-only default, opt-out pragma, per-project rollup).
- Reference scope/exclusions: `scripts/audit-component-shape.ts`, `scripts/audit-route-shape.ts`.
- Generator spec templates (the "starting point" to enforce): `tools/generators/src/generators/{react-router,react}/files/*/__tests__/__name__.test.tsx`.

## Convention this audit encodes

A source file is **tested** when EITHER exists (both are in-tree conventions):
- a sibling `Foo.test.tsx`, OR
- `__tests__/Foo.test.tsx` (sibling folder; loader/deep-link variants like `Foo.loader.test.ts` also count).

Universal suffix is `.test.tsx` (even non-JSX utils/api-routes). Honor a per-file opt-out pragma `test-coverage: opt-out`. Two scaffolds ship placeholder assertions (`FIXME: should be defined`) — hook + util — so a spec that is still the untouched placeholder should be reported as **stub coverage**, not real coverage.

### Exclusions (reuse verbatim from existing audits)
`**/__tests__/**`, `**/*.test.*`, `**/*.spec.*`, `**/*.stories.tsx`, `**/*.example.tsx`, `**/*-test-utils.tsx`, `**/*.server.tsx`, `**/__generated__/**`, `**/*.graphql` (incl. `*.tsx.graphql` route sidecars), `**/*.d.ts`, `index.tsx` barrels, `root.tsx`, `.gitkeep`-only `__tests__/` dirs.

## Categories

- **Enforced (warn now → strict later):** `routes`, `components`, `hooks`, `utils`.
- **Outliers — informational only:** `config`, `data` (mostly static: `defaults.ts`, `data.copy.ts` `*_COPY as const`, status maps). Report counts but never gate. Note: **no generator emits a `config` test template**, and there is no `react-router` `util` test template (util template lives in the `react` generator) — flag these as template gaps, don't invent conformance we can't scaffold.

## Approximate gap (openthrottle-developer alone)

routes 26 missing / 89 · components 73 / 279 · hooks 27 / 34 · utils 61 / 128 · (config 23/25, data 51/68 — informational). ~260 missing specs in the developer app; hooks/config/data are worst-covered proportionally. Shared `react-router-*` packages add substantially more (e.g. react-router-shadcn ~88 components missing).

## Deliverables

1. `scripts/audit-test-coverage.ts` — classifies files by category, applies the tested-OR-`__tests__` predicate, honors the opt-out pragma, flags placeholder stubs, and prints a per-project/per-category rollup. `--json` baseline, `--strict` gate (opt-in, per-category), report-only default.
2. Unit tests mirroring `scripts/__tests__/audit-component-shape.test.ts`.
3. `audit:test-coverage` (+ `:json`, `:strict`) npm scripts, wired into CI as a **non-blocking warning step** — explicitly NOT added to the husky gate yet.
4. A committed baseline JSON inventory that future remediation plans carve from.
5. Docs at `docs/monorepo/test-coverage-audit.md`.

## Out of scope

Actually writing the missing specs. Those are separate remediation plans spawned from the baseline (final task triages + drafts them). Flipping any category to strict is a later, deliberate step once its gap is closed.
Report-only audit flagging routes/components/hooks/utils missing a generator-shaped spec; ships in warning mode to baseline the test gap before remediation plans, mirroring our existing audit:* guard-rails.

Share URL pagination parsing from @openthrottle/react-router-utils
Lift the duplicated `?page=` / `?limit=` search-param parsing that loaders (and a few client pagers) reimplement by hand into `@openthrottle/react-router-utils`, then switch every developer-app copy onto that helper.

## Why

`settings.repositories._index` is one of many near-identical copies of:

```ts
const page = Math.max(1, Number(url.searchParams.get('page')) || 1);
const limit = Math.max(1, Math.min(100, Number(url.searchParams.get('limit')) || DEFAULT));
```

The package already exports `DEFAULT_PAGINATION_PAGE` (1) and `DEFAULT_PAGINATION_LIMIT` (25), and `/skills` already extracted `parsePaginationPage` / `parsePaginationLimit` — but those live in the app (`routing/skills/utils/parse-skills-pagination.ts`) instead of the shared package. Plans, prompts, projects, project-detail tasks, search, and queue jobs each re-roll the same logic with slightly different `Number` vs `parseInt` vs `Number.isFinite` dances and inconsistent flooring/clamping.

`readSearchParam` (`q` / `search`) already lives in `@openthrottle/react-router-ui-global` and should stay there — this plan is only the numeric pager params.

## Shared API (target)

Add to `packages/react-router-utils/src/utils/parsers.ts` (already re-exported from `src/index.ts`):

```ts
parsePagination(searchParams: URLSearchParams, options?: {
  readonly defaultLimit?: number; // DEFAULT_PAGINATION_LIMIT
  readonly defaultPage?: number;  // DEFAULT_PAGINATION_PAGE
  readonly maxLimit?: number;     // omit = no upper cap
  readonly minLimit?: number;     // default 1
}): { readonly limit: number; readonly offset: number; readonly page: number }
```

Keep `parsePaginationPage(raw)` / `parsePaginationLimit(raw, options)` as the primitives (skills already uses that shape) so client-side pagers that only have a raw string can call them without wrapping a `URLSearchParams`.

Canonical parse rules (unify the copies; slight behavior change on a few edges is intended):

- missing / empty / non-finite / `< 1` → default
- otherwise `Math.floor`, then clamp into `[minLimit, maxLimit]` when those options are set
- `offset = (page - 1) * limit`
- page is never upper-clamped here (skills already documents that as the caller's job once `totalPages` is known)

## Call sites to switch

Loader / client copies of the Math.max/Number dance:

- `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routes/settings.repositories._index.tsx` — `{ defaultLimit: REPOSITORIES_DEFAULT_LIMIT, maxLimit: 100 }`
- `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routes/projects._index.tsx` — `{ defaultLimit: PROJECTS_DEFAULT_LIMIT, maxLimit: 100 }`
- `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routes/plans._index.tsx` — package defaults (no max)
- `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routes/prompts._index.tsx` — package defaults (no max)
- `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routes/projects.$projectId._index.tsx` — `{ defaultLimit: PROJECT_TASKS_DEFAULT_LIMIT }`

Already-extracted app-local helpers to delete or thin:

- `routing/skills/utils/parse-skills-pagination.ts` (+ its spec) — import the package primitives instead; skills still clamps `page` to `totalPages` itself
- `routing/search/utils/parsers.ts` — `parseSearchParams` should delegate page/limit (`defaultLimit: DEFAULT_SEARCH_LIMIT, maxLimit: 100`) and keep `q` / `details`
- `routing/queues/utils/parse-queue-jobs-pagination.ts` — keep the URL wrapper; parse via `{ minLimit: QUEUE_JOBS_LIMIT_MIN, maxLimit: QUEUE_JOBS_LIMIT_MAX }` so `limit=1` still clamps to 10

Out of scope: `resources.queue-job-logs.tsx` is cursor-paged (`after` + `limit`, no `page`). Do not force it onto `parsePagination`.

## Non-goals

- Do not move `readSearchParam`
- Do not collapse route-specific default constants (`REPOSITORIES_DEFAULT_LIMIT = 10`, etc.) into the package default of 25 — pass them as `defaultLimit`
- Do not add a `maxPage` option; callers that slice client-side already clamp after they know `totalCount`

ot-worktree skill: portable worktree create/heal + single global worktree root
# Goal

Today worktree creation is OpenThrottle-monorepo-shaped: `scripts/create_worktree.sh`, `scripts/ensure_worktree.sh`, `scripts/setup_worktree.sh` and `scripts/worktree_ports.sh` live in this repo, are wired via `pnpm worktree:new` / `pnpm worktree:heal`, the nx `monorepo:ensure-worktree` target, the Claude `WorktreeCreate` hook (`.claude/settings.json`) and `.cursor/worktrees.json`. None of it travels — another GitHub repo gets nothing. And there is no removal path at all: a repo-wide grep finds no `git worktree remove` / prune / teardown anywhere, which is why orphan worktrees accumulate.

Because OpenThrottle skills are already mapped into any repo (`skills/` → `.agents/skills/` → `.claude/skills/` via `ot-skill-sync`), the worktree machinery belongs in a skill. Any repo that has the skill should then create, heal and destroy worktrees the same way.

## Three composable actions

The skill exposes exactly three verbs, each usable standalone and callable from the others:

| Action | Script | Entrypoint | Job |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **create** | `create.sh` | `pnpm worktree:new`, Claude `WorktreeCreate` hook, Cursor | Create the worktree, then provision it |
| **heal** | `heal.sh` | `pnpm worktree:heal`, nx `monorepo:ensure-worktree` | Lazily provision a worktree that was made outside the skill |
| **destroy** | `destroy.sh` | `pnpm worktree:remove` | Tear down and remove a worktree (net-new) |

They share `common.sh` (linked-worktree detection, name sanitization, target validation), `root.sh` (the root ladder), `provision.sh` and the teardown hook.

Two decisions were made up front and are NOT open for re-litigation during implementation:

1. **Single global worktree root, namespaced by repo:** `~/worktrees/<repo-name>/<worktree-name>`. This replaces the current per-repo default (a sibling `openthrottle-worktrees` directory). `OT_WORKTREE_ROOT` still overrides it, and a repo-level override is explicitly deferred (a later plan) — leave a seam, do not build it.
2. **Repo-specific provisioning stays in the repo.** The skill owns the generic mechanics (linked-worktree detection, hook-payload parsing, name sanitization, root resolution, `git worktree add`/`remove`, self-heal guard). It delegates to repo-provided provision/teardown hooks if they exist, and no-ops otherwise. OpenThrottle keeps `scripts/setup_worktree.sh` (pnpm install/build, `.env` reset, 6020–6026 port remap, docker compose override, service-account token sync) as ITS provisioner — none of that moves into the skill.

# Shape of the target

```
skills/ot-worktree/
  SKILL.md
  scripts/
    common.sh        # linked-worktree detection, logging, repo/name/target resolution
    root.sh          # resolve_worktree_root — the single global root ladder
    create.sh        # modes: CLI arg / hook stdin payload / provision-in-place
    heal.sh          # lazy self-heal guard (was ensure_worktree.sh)
    destroy.sh       # teardown + git worktree remove + prune (net-new)
    provision.sh     # find + exec the repo provisioner, or no-op
  references/
    contract.md      # the repo provision/teardown contract + env vars
```

Repo provisioner discovery order (first hit wins, all optional):
1. `$OT_WORKTREE_PROVISION` (absolute or repo-relative path)
2. `.worktree/provision.sh`
3. `scripts/setup_worktree.sh`  ← what OpenThrottle uses today, so this repo needs no new file

Teardown mirrors it: `$OT_WORKTREE_TEARDOWN`, then `.worktree/teardown.sh` (no `scripts/` fallback — no incumbent to preserve). Nothing found → log and no-op; a plain `git worktree add`/`remove` is a valid outcome in a repo with no setup needs.

Both hooks get: cwd = the worktree, `OT_SOURCE_REPO` = primary checkout, `OT_WORKTREE_NAME`, `OT_WORKTREE_PATH`, stdin closed. Port allocation (`scripts/worktree_ports.sh`) stays in this repo and stays owned by `setup_worktree.sh` — it is OpenThrottle's canonical-port concern, not a generic one.

# Root-resolution ladder (new)

Highest rung wins:
1. `OT_WORKTREE_ROOT` in the environment (one-off overrides; also how the BullMQ provisioner forwards the workspace setting).
2. `OT_WORKTREE_ROOT` in the primary checkout's `.env`.
3. **Default: `~/worktrees/<repo-name>`** where `<repo-name>` is the basename of the primary checkout.

Rungs 1 and 2 are absolute paths that already include their own namespacing — do NOT append `<repo-name>` to an explicitly configured root; that would silently relocate every existing configured setup. Only the default rung namespaces.

# Back-compat / callers to keep working

- `pnpm worktree:new <name>` and `pnpm worktree:heal` stay as the human entrypoints — thin wrappers onto the skill scripts. `pnpm worktree:remove` joins them.
- nx `monorepo:ensure-worktree` target (`package.json` nx block, wired via `targetDefaults.dev.dependsOn`).
- `.claude/settings.json` `WorktreeCreate` hook — MUST still print only the absolute worktree path on stdout.
- `.cursor/worktrees.json` provision-in-place mode (`cwd=$WORKTREE_PATH`, no args, no stdin).
- Server-side: `applications/openthrottle-server/src/services/worktree-root/worktree-root.resolver.ts` is the TS mirror of the shell ladder and is consumed by the settings page, `worktree-discovery.service.ts`, `plan-run-worktree-provision.service.ts` and `discovered-worktrees.resolver.ts`. Its `DEFAULT_WORKTREE_ROOT_DIRECTORY_NAME = 'openthrottle-worktrees'` default must change in lockstep or discovery will look in the wrong directory.
- Existing worktrees under the old sibling `openthrottle-worktrees` directory must keep working. They are already registered in `git worktree list`, so nothing needs moving; discovery just needs to not lose them.

# Non-goals

- Repository-level root override (deferred; leave the seam only).
- Moving port allocation, `.env` handling, or docker compose isolation into the skill.
- Auto-migrating existing worktrees to the new root.
- Server-side / UI wiring of the destroy action (a follow-up once the script exists).
Extract worktree create/heal into a portable `ot-worktree` skill, add a net-new destroy action (three composable actions), and move every repo to a single global worktree root (`~/worktrees/<repo>/<name>`), with repo-specific provisioning and teardown delegated to hooks.

Recharts 3.10.1: Bar and Pie shapes do not render
## What

With `recharts@3.10.1`, the data shapes in `SimpleBarChart` and `SimplePieChart` do not render:

- **Bar**: Recharts emits one `.recharts-bar-rectangle` group per datum, each containing an empty `.recharts-inactive-bar` group and **no** `rect`/`path`.
- **Pie**: `.recharts-pie` contains an empty layer and zero `path` elements.

Everything around them works — the SVG surface sizes correctly (512x256), axes render with the right scale and tick labels, grid, legend and tooltip are all fine. So the charts look plausible while the data is invisible.

`SimpleLineChart` and `SimpleAreaChart` are **unaffected** (1 curve path and 2 area paths respectively).

## Why it went unnoticed

jsdom cannot exercise Recharts geometry — the ResizeObserver no-op means no measurement, so no shapes. The package's 225-file / 472-test Vitest suite passes green. This was only visible once the components rendered in a real browser, via `applications/openthrottle-workbench` (plan c84d753c, task 56d7df54).

## Reproduce

```bash
pnpm nx run openthrottle-workbench:dev
```

Open `Components/SimpleBarChart → Default` and `Components/SimplePieChart → Default`, then inspect:

```js
document.querySelectorAll('.recharts-bar-rectangle path, .recharts-bar-rectangle rect').length; // 0
document.querySelector('.recharts-pie').outerHTML; // empty layer
```

The affected stories carry a `⚠️ KNOWN ISSUE` block pointing here.

## Not yet established

Root cause is open. Candidates worth checking in order:

1. **Version regression.** The catalog pins `recharts: ^3.6.0` and resolution landed on 3.10.1. Try pinning 3.6.x and see whether the shapes return — that would isolate it to a Recharts change.
2. **Component misuse.** Both failing components pass a `fill`/shape through in a way Line and Area do not. `SimpleBarChart` passes `fill={`var(--color-${valueKey})`}` and a `radius` tuple; check these against the Recharts 3.10 API.
3. **React 19 interaction.** The workspace is on React 19.2.4; confirm Recharts 3.10.1 supports it fully.

## Done when

- Bars and pie sectors render in the workbench for the existing stories, with no story changes required.
- The fix is verified in the browser (not only by unit tests, which cannot see this).
- Whatever regression guard is practical is added — note that a jsdom assertion cannot cover it, so this may mean pinning a version with a comment rather than a test.
- The `⚠️ KNOWN ISSUE` blocks are removed from `SimpleBarChart.stories.tsx` and `SimplePieChart.stories.tsx`.

## Related

Also documented while building the stories, and NOT a bug: `ChartContainer` wraps Recharts' `ResponsiveContainer`, which sets `width`/`height: 100%` **inline** — so sizing it with a `className` is silently ignored and it measures to zero. It needs a sized parent. This is already noted on the `Chart` stories.
RESOLVED — NOT A BUG. Root cause is requestAnimationFrame starvation in the hidden browser tab used to inspect the workbench, not recharts and not the components. Recharts animates chart geometry from t=0 via rAF; browsers never fire rAF when document.visibilityState is 'hidden', so Rectangle/Sector stay zero-sized and return null. SimpleBarChart and SimplePieChart render correctly unmodified once rAF runs (verified by screenshot under an rAF shim). The report's claim that Line/Area were unaffected was also wrong — they are equally starved, they just emit paths that draw zero length (stroke-dasharray "0px N px"), so counting DOM nodes reported them healthy. No code fix made; disabling animation or pinning recharts would have degraded working code. Shipped: the misleading KNOWN ISSUE blocks removed, and the rAF/hidden-tab trap documented in applications/openthrottle-workbench/AGENTS.md.

Make external skills read-only (UI + write API)
## Problem

`/skills/:slug` lets any discovered skill's SKILL.md be edited in place. For **external** skills (installed from an upstream source, e.g. `/skills/create-cli`) an in-app edit silently forks the file from upstream: the next `skill-sync` / lockfile install either clobbers the edit or leaves the repo permanently diverged from the source. OpenThrottle-authored skills (e.g. `/skills/ot-loop`, real directories under the repo's `skills/` tree) are the only ones we own and the only ones that should be editable here.

Provenance is already derived and surfaced — `discoverRepoSkills` sets `RepoSkillEntry.source` to `'openthrottle'` when the skill folder's realpath resolves under the authored `skills/` tree and `'external'` otherwise (`applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routing/agents/data/discover-repo-skills.server.ts`), the index has a Source column + filter, and `useSkillDetail` already computes `isOpenThrottle`. Nothing consumes it for write gating.

## Current write path (the only one)

There is **no GraphQL mutation** that writes SKILL.md. The single write surface is the developer app's route action:

- `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routes/skills.$slug.tsx` → `action` → `writeSkillFileBySlug(slug, content)`
- `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routing/skills/data/write-skill-file.server.ts` — resolves the monorepo root, re-discovers by slug, realpath-containment-checks the path, re-validates frontmatter, then `writeFileSync`.

So "API level" for this plan means that route action + `writeSkillFileBySlug`. That server helper is the authoritative gate: the UI gate is a courtesy, the helper must refuse regardless of what the client posts.

## Goal

1. **API:** `writeSkillFileBySlug` refuses with a structured error when the discovered entry's `source !== 'openthrottle'` — checked after slug discovery (so provenance comes from disk, never from client input) and before frontmatter validation / any write.
2. **UI:** on `/skills/:slug` for an external skill, the Edit button is disabled with a tooltip explaining the upstream-sync reason (distinct from today's "needs a local checkout" tooltip), and edit mode is unreachable.

## Explicit non-goals

- **Record-level tags stay editable** for external skills. `project_skills.tags`, add/remove tag, orphan removal, and skill-availability rules are database rows, not SKILL.md content — none of them drift from upstream. Do not gate them.
- **Running** an external skill stays allowed.
- The in-app IDE / any generic file editor is out of scope; this plan gates the skills surface only.
- No schema/migration work — provenance is already available on the entry.

## Key files

- `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routing/skills/data/write-skill-file.server.ts` (+ `__tests__/write-skill-file.server.test.ts`)
- `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routes/skills.$slug.tsx`
- `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routing/skills/hooks/useSkillDetail.tsx`
- `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routing/skills/components/SkillDetailEditControls.tsx`, `SkillIntroduction.tsx`, `SkillDetailTabs.tsx`
- `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routing/skills/data/data.copy.ts` (`SKILL_DETAIL_COPY`, `SKILL_WRITE_COPY`, `SKILLS_SOURCE_COPY`)

`pnpm nx run openthrottle-developer:lint`, `:typecheck`, `:test`. Live browser verification of authed pages is blocked without a permissioned seeded user — cover the gate with render-level Vitest instead.
