Rollout v1: feature-flagging system (@openthrottle/nestjs-rollout + /settings/rollout UI)
## What

Introduce **"rollout"** — OpenThrottle's feature-flagging system — as a new `@openthrottle/nestjs-rollout` package plus an admin CRUD UI at `/settings/rollout` in `openthrottle-developer`. It integrates with `@openthrottle/nestjs-rbac` from day one.

> Terminology: **rollout** = the feature-flagging system (this plan). **clutch** = the Agentic Chat & harness (a *separate* system, unrelated to this plan — noted only to avoid naming collisions).

## v1 scope (locked)

- **Flag model — global + role targeting.** A flag = `key` (unique, kebab/dotted string), `description`, `enabled` (bool), `targetRoles` (string[] of RBAC role names). Evaluation: a flag is ON for an actor when `enabled === true` AND (`targetRoles` is empty ⇒ everyone, else the actor holds ≥1 of `targetRoles`).
- **Consumption — server service + GraphQL query.** `RolloutService.isEnabled(key, principal)` for server-side code, plus a `myFeatureFlags` GraphQL query returning the evaluated flag set for the current actor.
- **RBAC integration.** New `flags:read` / `flags:write` permissions added to `@openthrottle/nestjs-rbac`. Admin mutations are gated by the app's `GqlPermissionsGuard` + `@Permissions(...)`. Role targeting resolves the actor's roles via `RolesService` (from `@openthrottle/nestjs-repositories`), exactly as `GqlPermissionsGuard` does.

Out of scope for v1 (candidate v2): percentage/bucketed rollout, per-user overrides, environment/segment targeting, audit history, SDK/edge caching.

## Architecture boundary (mirrors the existing roles precedent)

The **package owns the domain**: the TypeORM entity, `RolloutFlagsModule` (`TypeOrmModule.forFeature`), and `RolloutService` (CRUD + evaluation; depends on `@openthrottle/nestjs-repositories` `RolesService` and `@openthrottle/nestjs-auth` `AuthPrincipal`). The **GraphQL resolver lives in the app** (`applications/openthrottle-server/src/graphql/rollout/`) because it must use the app-local `GqlPermissionsGuard` (the app depends on packages, not the reverse). This is precisely how `RolesService` (in `nestjs-repositories`) pairs with `RolesResolver` (in the app).

## Conventions confirmed by research (apply throughout)

- **Package**: `NX_ISOLATE_PLUGINS=false pnpm nx g @tools/generators:package --type=nestjs --organization=@openthrottle --name=nestjs-rollout`. Source-first (`main`/`types` → `src/index.ts`); may own its own `*.entity.ts` (autoloaded via the `*.entity.js` glob in `nestjs-typeorm`); `synchronize` is OFF → schema comes from migrations, not entity sync. Generator auto-runs install + `pnpm nx sync`.
- **Migrations**: next free numbers are `084` / `085` under `databases/migrations/`. Idempotent DDL (`CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`, `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS`, `DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS … ; CREATE TRIGGER …`), `gen_random_uuid()` PKs, `TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE … DEFAULT NOW()`, reuse the shared `update_updated_at_column()` trigger, and mandatory `COMMENT ON TABLE`/`COMMENT ON COLUMN`. Apply with `pnpm database:migrate`. Reference: `082_create_scheduled_agent_jobs.sql`, `034_create_roles_and_permissions_tables.sql`.
- **GraphQL**: code-first. `app.module.ts` import order **==** schema field order — add `NestjsRolloutModule`/`RolloutGraphqlModule` in the alphabetical slot inside the `isApiLike` GraphQL block; never reorder. Object types `implements` the entity `*Data` type; Result wrappers are hand-written per-domain `…ResultObject` classes (there is no generic factory). After changes: boot the server once to regenerate `applications/openthrottle-server/schema.gql`, then `NX_ISOLATE_PLUGINS=false pnpm nx run openthrottle-developer:codegen-graphql`. Commit `schema.gql` + `app/__generated__/*`.
- **Developer UI**: React Router flat-routes. Mirror the workspace CRUD pattern — `settings.rollout._index.tsx` (list + create), `settings.rollout.$flagId._index.tsx` (view), `settings.rollout.$flagId.edit.tsx` (edit), each with a colocated `*.tsx.graphql`. Loaders/actions use `executeGraphqlWithAuth`. Add a nav item in `app/global/data/data.navigation.ts` (`Settings` array). The `/settings` prefix already auth-gates via `PROTECTED_PATH_PREFIXES`. Retire skill-tag-overlays.json: ingest first, tag on records
Flip skill tagging from a committed overlay file to post-ingest annotations on project_skills rows.

## Problem

`skill-tag-overlays.json` is a human-maintained skill→tag map. Every authored or vendored skill must have an entry (empty tags still required). CI (`check-skill-tag-vocabulary` via `check-agent-assets-ssot`) fails on missing or stale keys. Ingest (`openthrottle-ingest-agent-assets` → `toProjectSkillInputs` → `reconcileProjectSkills`) merges overlay tags onto rows and **overwrites** `project_skills.tags` on every run. Deleting a folder under `skills/` is not graceful: overlay CI breaks until a human edits the JSON, and reconcile **hard-deletes** the DB row (and its tags).

Tags never live in SKILL.md frontmatter in this monorepo (vendored skills must stay byte-identical to upstream). The overlay exists only so OT can classify skills for availability (rung 2 tagAllow/tagDeny) and plan-relevance (skill.tags ∩ plan domain tags). Cursor/Claude do not read this file.

There is no mutation or UI to tag a skill record. Vocabulary management exists (`skillTagVocabulary`, `SkillTagVocabularyManager`); per-skill tagging does not. Plan/task/project tags already have add/remove mutations — skills should follow that pattern.

## Desired model

1. **Bring skills in first, untagged.** Keep walking `.agents/skills/` into `project_skills` (slug, description, source, sourcePath, disable-model-invocation). Do **not** require tags at ingest. Do **not** write tags from a file.
2. **Tag the records afterward.** Tags are OT's idea of the skill, stored on the `project_skills` row (or an equivalent join), edited via GraphQL + `/skills` UI, validated against the caller's domain vocabulary. Ingest must **preserve** existing tags on upsert (never clobber).
3. **Delete `skill-tag-overlays.json`** and the overlay parser/CI coverage gate. No more "add an overlay entry when you add a skill."
4. **Graceful missing skill.** Deleting `skills/<slug>/` (or a vendored skill vanishing) is not a CI failure and must not auto-delete the DB row. Reconcile reports orphans: "was ingested, isn't on disk now — suggest remove." UI/MCP surfaces that and offers an explicit remove. Availability/plan-relevance skip or warn on orphans rather than crashing.

## Out of scope

- Do **not** remove agent-asset ingest into `custom_prompts` / embeddings. That path is independent.
- Do **not** put tags back into SKILL.md frontmatter for this monorepo. External workspace repos may still declare frontmatter tags; this repo's tags are record-owned.
- Phase tags still never attach to skills.

## Current overlay → records

One-shot: copy today's overlay tag lists onto existing `project_skills` rows so curated classification is not lost, then delete the file. New/untagged skills stay `{}` until someone tags them in the product.

## Key code

- Overlay: `skill-tag-overlays.json`, `packages/openthrottle-skills/src/skill-tag-overlays.ts` (`parseSkillTagOverlayFile`, `mergeSkillTags`)
- CI: `scripts/check-skill-tag-vocabulary.ts`, `scripts/check-agent-assets-ssot.sh`
- Ingest: `scripts/openthrottle-ingest-agent-assets.ts` (`reconcileDogfoodProjectSkills` overwrites tags; DELETE of stale slugs), `toProjectSkillInputs`, `ProjectSkillsService.reconcileProjectSkills`
- Consumers: `resolveSkillAvailability` rung 2, `plan-context-availability.service.ts` (`matchedPlanTags`), `/skills` merge (`mergeRepoSkillsWithProjectSkills` — disk is the list, DB wins for tags; DB-only orphans are currently invisible)
- Precedent for record tagging: `addPlanTag` / `addTaskTag` / `addProjectTag` in `tags.resolver.ts`

Fix & improve the Add-folder Browse flow (native + in-app server directory picker)
## Problem

On `/settings/workspace`, the "Add a folder" dialog's Browse control does not feel like folder selection. Today (`applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routing/settings/components/WorkspaceAddFolderDialog.tsx`, `.../hooks/useWorkspaceAddFolderDialog.tsx`, `.../actions/workspace.ts` → `browseDirectory`, server `applications/openthrottle-server/src/graphql/workspace-settings/workspace-folders.{resolver,service}.ts`):

- The Browse control is a **text input**: the user must type an absolute server-host path before anything happens, then click "Browse" to list immediate subdirectories.
- Navigation is **drill-down only** — no seed/default path, no breadcrumb, no "up one level", and no way to add the folder you are currently *inside* (only its listed children).
- Entries carry **no signal** for which are git repositories or already registered.
- The whole Browse block is visually secondary, buried under discovered folders and the manual-path escape hatch.

## Key constraint (design-defining)

Workspace folders live on the **openthrottle-server host**, not the browser. Browser folder pickers (`<input type="file" webkitdirectory>`, `window.showDirectoryPicker()`) intentionally **do not expose absolute filesystem paths** — only folder names / relative subpaths — so they cannot produce a usable server path even on localhost. Therefore the "native OS folder dialog" path must be a **server-side** OS picker (macOS `osascript -e 'choose folder'`, Linux `zenity --file-selection --directory` / `kdialog`, Windows PowerShell `FolderBrowserDialog`) that returns the chosen absolute host path, gated behind a **same-machine / localhost** capability check. When the server is remote (or headless / no display), fall back to the improved in-app server-side directory picker.

## Chosen direction (user decision)

**Both, with fallback:**
1. **Native path** — server-side OS folder dialog when server==same machine as the browser; the dialog opens on the user's own screen and returns an absolute host path that flows straight into `addWorkspaceFolder`.
2. **In-app fallback** — a real interactive directory picker built on the existing `browseDirectory` infra: seeded from configured workspace roots (or home), breadcrumb + up-navigation (allowlist-guarded), select-the-current-folder, and per-entry `isGitRepo` / `alreadyRegistered` annotations.

## Constraints & conventions

- Code-first GraphQL in `openthrottle-server`; after schema changes run the server to regenerate `applications/openthrottle-server/schema.gql`, then `pnpm nx affected --target=codegen-graphql,codegen-react-router --parallel` and commit `__generated__`.
- Reuse the existing allowlist guard in `browseDirectory` (must resolve under `OPENTHROTTLE_WORKSPACE_ROOTS`); keep the same path-safety posture (`realpathSync`, absolute-path + NUL checks, symlink-resolved root containment) on any new resolver.
- Native picker resolver must never hang the request: bounded timeout, clean cancel (user dismisses dialog → no error toast, just no-op), and hard-disable when headless / no display / not same-machine.
- Permissions: read capabilities under `SETTINGS_READ`; the native pick + `addWorkspaceFolder` remain `SETTINGS_WRITE`.
- UI from `@openthrottle/react-router-shadcn`; keep the component/hook split (component-primitive-shape R6/R7) and section comments; copy in `data.copy.ts`.
- Tests: server service/resolver Vitest; client hook + dialog render tests using `component` + `userEvent`. Gate with typecheck + lint + test + build on `openthrottle-developer` and `openthrottle-server`.

## Out of scope

- Electron/desktop-shell native dialogs (no desktop shell today).
- Clone-repo flow changes (separate surface).
- Multi-select add.
Rework the /settings/workspace "Add a folder" Browse flow so the Browse button actually launches folder selection — a native OS folder dialog when openthrottle-server runs on the same machine as the browser, falling back to an improved in-app server-side directory picker (seeded roots, breadcrumb + up-navigation, select-current-folder, git-repo/already-registered annotations) otherwise.

Fix plan/task status contract drift (DB enum ↔ GraphQL ↔ MCP) and establish a single source of truth
## Context

While counting OT plans, an agent queried `listPlansByStatus` with `["cancelled","draft","archived"]` and got a generic "The request was rejected as invalid" error, then wrongly concluded those statuses don't exist. Investigation revealed the real cause is status-vocabulary drift across four layers of the stack, none of which agree, and none of which is introspectable by a caller.

## Ground truth (DB)

Postgres enum type `plan_task_status`, defined in `databases/migrations/028_plan_task_status_enum.sql` and extended by `029_add_queued_status.sql`:

- `BACKLOG`, `BLOCKED`, `CANCELED`, `COMPLETED`, `IN_PROGRESS`, `PENDING`, `QUEUED` (plans-only), `SKIPPED`
- Note: `CANCELED` is **single-L**. `FAILED`, `DRAFT`, `ARCHIVED` are **not** members.
- `plans.status` and `tasks.status` are columns of this enum type.

## The drift

1. **Entity vs DB** — `packages/nestjs-repositories/src/modules/plans/plan.entity.ts:59` declares `@Column({ default: 'pending', name: 'status', type: 'text' })`. The ORM believes the column is free `text`, not the `plan_task_status` enum, and the default `'pending'` is lowercase while the enum labels are uppercase. Same likely applies to the task entity.
2. **GraphQL** — `applications/openthrottle-server/schema.gql` exposes `status: String!` on every plan/task type and `statuses: [String]` on `ListPlansByStatusInput`. No enum, so consumers cannot introspect the valid set. Input descriptions in `applications/openthrottle-server/src/graphql/plans/plan.input.ts` are inconsistent and partly wrong: line ~452 says "COMPLETED, CANCELLED, or FAILED" (double-L + `FAILED` doesn't exist in the enum); line ~486 says "COMPLETED, IN_PROGRESS, PENDING, QUEUED".
3. **MCP** — `ListPlansByStatusInputSchema()` in `packages/openthrottle-mcp/src/__generated__/schemas.ts` generates `statuses: z.array(z.string().nullable()).nullish()` (no enum), and the tool description in `packages/openthrottle-mcp/src/tools/plans.ts:75` only lists `pending`/`in_progress`/`completed`.
4. **Resolver** — `PlansResolver.listPlansByStatus` (`applications/openthrottle-server/src/graphql/plans/plans.resolver.ts:548`) uppercases and filters `status IN (...)` with **no validation**. An unknown value reaches Postgres → `invalid input value for enum plan_task_status: "CANCELLED"`. The MCP error mapper (`packages/openthrottle-mcp/src/utils/errors.ts:58`) then flattens this to the generic `validation` message "The request was rejected as invalid. Check the provided arguments and retry." — losing the actual reason. (`BLOCKED` "worked" only because it's a valid enum value returning 0 rows.)

## Goal / desired contract

- One canonical, code-level source of truth for the status vocabulary (shared const, ideally derived from or asserted against the DB enum).
- GraphQL exposes it as a **real enum** (or a query returning the valid set) so it is introspectable; deprecate `String` gradually per the repo's no-break-schema rule (`@deprecated`, migration plan) rather than hard-swapping.
- MCP types + tool descriptions regenerate from the GraphQL enum automatically (no hand-maintained status lists).
- Entity column type corrected to the enum with an uppercase default.
- Resolver validates status input up front and returns a **clear, actionable** error listing valid values, instead of leaking a raw Postgres enum error through the generic MCP sanitizer.

## Constraints / gotchas

- Code-first GraphQL (`autoSchemaFile`); after any schema change follow the codegen flow in CLAUDE.md (boot server to regen `applications/openthrottle-server/schema.gql`, then `codegen-graphql,codegen-react-router`, commit `__generated__`). CI fails on codegen drift.
- No new TS `enum`s — use an `as const` object per `.cursor/rules/`. A GraphQL enum can be registered from an `as const` map via `registerEnumType`.
- Never break existing fields without a migration/deprecation plan.
- `QUEUED` is plans-only; task status set is the 7 non-QUEUED values. The canonical model must capture that distinction.
- The UI already has status vocab in `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routing/plans/config/status-options.ts` and related components — reconcile so the UI consumes the same source.

Plan authored 2026-08-11.
The valid plan/task status set has drifted across four layers, so callers can't know the real values and unknown statuses fail with an opaque error. Ground truth is the Postgres enum plan_task_status = {BACKLOG, BLOCKED, CANCELED, COMPLETED, IN_PROGRESS, PENDING, QUEUED (plans-only), SKIPPED} (databases/migrations/028,029; CANCELED is single-L). But: (1) plan.entity.ts declares the column as `type: 'text'` with a lowercase default 'pending' — TypeORM thinks it's free text, not the enum, and the lowercase default doesn't match the uppercase enum labels; (2) schema.gql exposes `status: String!` with no enum, so consumers can't introspect valid values, and input descriptions cite inconsistent/nonexistent sets ("COMPLETED, CANCELLED, FAILED" — double-L + FAILED doesn't exist; elsewhere "COMPLETED, IN_PROGRESS, PENDING, QUEUED"); (3) the openthrottle-mcp tool schema is auto-generated to z.array(z.string()) with no enum and its description only lists pending/in_progress/completed; (4) listPlansByStatus does `status IN (...)` with no validation, so an unknown value reaches Postgres and throws "invalid input value for enum plan_task_status", which the MCP maps to the generic "The request was rejected as invalid" — which is exactly what bit an agent that guessed `cancelled`/`draft`/`archived`. Goal: define one canonical status source of truth, expose it as a real GraphQL enum (or introspectable const), regenerate MCP types/docs from it, fix the entity, and validate input at the resolver with a clear error instead of leaking a raw Postgres enum error.

Port `docs/marketing/scripts/10-notes.md` to a recorded flow in the openthrottle-developer demo pipeline (`applications/openthrottle-developer/tests/demo/`).

**This plan opens BLOCKED.** The notes half of the short is recordable today. The search half — which is the entire payoff and the whole reason the short exists — is not.

## Gate 1: notes are not in the semantic index (beats 0:32, 0:41, 0:50)

The short's promise is "search for the symptom, months later" → "There it is. And your agents query the same index before they start work."

`search._index.tsx.graphql` runs `search(input:)` and reads back `chunks` whose fields are `planId`, `planTitle`, `taskId`, `taskTitle`, `source`, `sourcePath`, `sourceRepo`, `sourceSha`. There is no `noteId`. The schema's own `getDocument` description enumerates the backing tables: *"UUID from plan_embeddings, task_embeddings, or documentation_embeddings"*. The migrations in `databases/migrations/` create `plan_embeddings` (004), `task_embeddings` (005), `documentation_embeddings` (020), `code_embeddings` (052) and `custom_prompt_embeddings` (037). **There is no note_embeddings table**, and `scripts/seed-demo.ts` truncates `task_embeddings, plan_embeddings` without ever writing a note embedding.

So the note will not come back from `/search`, and the closing claim that agents query the same index for notes is not true today. Recording it would put a false product claim on camera — the thing the publish checklist exists to prevent.

Two ways forward, and the first is real product work that deserves its own plan rather than being smuggled into a screencast:

- Index notes. A `note_embeddings` table, ingestion on note create/update, a `note` source in the search resolver and a note branch in the results UI. This is the feature the short is selling; if the channel wants this short, the product needs this.
- Re-cut the short around what notes actually do today — captured, listed, readable, linkable — and drop the search payoff. That is a materially weaker video and the title ("capture context your agents can actually find") stops being accurate, so it likely wants a new script rather than an edit.

## Gate 2: notes have no title (beats 0:08 and 0:18)

The script separates "type a title" from "type two sentences of body text". `NoteForm.tsx` renders a single `Label htmlFor="content"` over one `content` field; `notes.create.tsx` submits `{ input: { content: parsed.data.content } }`; and `CreateNoteInput` in `notes.create.tsx.graphql` is `{ content: String!, author: String }`. There is no title anywhere. `NotesTable` derives its row label from the content itself via `notePreviewLabel`.

Two beats collapse into one, and eight seconds of the script's runtime have nothing to show.

## What already exists and needs no work

- `/notes` (`NotesTable`, `NoteCard`), `/notes/create` (`NoteForm`) and `/notes/:noteId` all render, and `NoteCard` renders Markdown so a note with structure reads well in frame.
- `scripts/seed-demo.ts` already inserts `DEMO_NOTES` — four fictional notes whose voice fits "something you learned": "429 vs 503", "Antimeridian", "Tile cache invalidation", "Deploys and the tile cache". The 04 plan already vetted these on camera and found "429 vs 503" the strongest.
- `/search` renders and is exercisable; it is the *contents* of the index that are wrong for this short, not the route.

## Constraints

- 68 spoken words is the budget in the script frontmatter; collapsing the title beat and re-cutting the payoff will move it substantially. Re-validate against `scripts/validate-video-scripts.ts` and the `short` budget in `docs/marketing/format.json`.
- The script's frontmatter says `blockedOn: []`, which is wrong and is a deliverable of this plan.
- Notes render free-form user content, which per the 04 plan's scan task is one of the pipeline's higher-risk leak surfaces. Only ever record the fictional seeded notes.
- A flow may not invent a step the script does not describe, and a script may not describe UI that does not exist.
- Produce, do not publish. Uploading needs the channel credentials and the owner's decision.

BullMQ plan-run defaults: always worktree, verbose logging, workspace bound to the worktree
## Goal

Programmatic (BullMQ) plan runs must default to a **cursor** backend running in a **dedicated git worktree that OpenThrottle creates itself**, with **verbose agent logging**, and with the run's **workspace bound to that worktree** (working directory, `plan_runs.checkout_id`, and `run_config_snapshot.workspace`). Today only the backend default (`cursor`) is right; the rest default to "no worktree, no verbose, run in whatever cwd the server process has".

`cursor` stays the default backend deliberately: Claude requires a different payment model for this kind of unattended programmatic invocation, so the queue must not silently route to it.

## Decision (settled 2026-08-20)

**Option A — OpenThrottle creates the worktree.** The server provisions the worktree via the single sanctioned entrypoint `pnpm run worktree:new <name>` (`scripts/create_worktree.sh`) and passes the resulting absolute path as the run's `workingDirectory`. The agent CLI's `-w` / `--worktree` flag stays **off** for queued runs, so there is exactly one worktree per run and the path is known up front — which is what checkout registration, `.env` provisioning, and per-path agent-CLI MCP approval all require. Option B (let the agent CLI create it and discover the path afterwards) is rejected.

Second decision from the same conversation: **centralize where worktrees live.** `scripts/create_worktree.sh:115` currently hardcodes `BASE_DIR="$(dirname "$REPO_ROOT")/openthrottle-worktrees"`. That root becomes configurable so every agent (Claude, Cursor, OT Loop, the BullMQ worker) puts its worktrees in one predictable, user-chosen place. See the dedicated task for the precedence chain and the in-repo-vs-sibling trade-off.

## Decisions settled by task 1 (2026-08-20)

Recorded in full in `docs/openthrottle/plan-run-worktrees.md`.

- **Naming** — `plan-<first 8 chars of the plan UUID>` (e.g. `plan-5e172b67`), so the branch is `openthrottle/plan-5e172b67`. Deterministic (survives a plan retitle), collision-free, already within the `[A-Za-z0-9._-]` set `create_worktree.sh` sanitizes to, and short enough to read in `git branch` and a PR.
- **Lifecycle** — one worktree per **plan**, reused across runs. OT Loop runs are iterations of the same work landing as one branch and one PR; reuse preserves branch history and keeps disk flat, where per-run worktrees would multiply ~2 GB `node_modules` trees per iteration.
- **Cleanup** — no automatic removal. Removal stays manual (`git worktree remove`) until a dedicated sweep lands as a follow-up; safe automatic removal requires a clean tree, no unpushed commits, no active run, and an age floor. Ceiling: one worktree per plan that has ever run programmatically.
- **Failure policy** — fail the run fast, with the provisioner's stderr in the plan output stream. A fallback to the process cwd silently drops the agent into the primary checkout, which is the bug this plan fixes.
- **Timing** — at job start in the orchestrator, not at enqueue: a run queued for hours should not hold a worktree, and it keeps `validateWorkingDirectory`'s existence check honest (the enqueue payload carries a worktree *name*; only an explicit caller-supplied `workingDirectory` is existence-checked).
- **Concurrency** — idempotent provisioning (reuse an existing linked worktree at the target path) plus per-path serialization in-process. The plans worker is `concurrency: 1`, so this guards re-runs after a stall and multi-instance deployments.

## Current state (verified in-repo)

- `packages/openthrottle-plan-config/src/plan-run-config-storage.constants.ts` — `DEFAULT_PLAN_RUN_PLAN_RUN_RUNNER = 'cursor'`. No worktree/debug defaults exist.
- `packages/openthrottle-plan-config/src/plan-run-config-storage.defaults.ts` — `getDefaultPlanRunConfigPlanRunV1()` returns `debugCli: 'omit'`, `worktreeCli: 'omit'`, `worktreeName: ''`, `worktreeBase: ''`, `skipWorktreeSetup: false`; `workspace` is all-empty (`checkoutId`, `repositoryId`, `workingDirectory`).
- `applications/openthrottle-server/src/graphql/plans/enqueue-plan-plan-run-tuning.ts` — `parseEnqueuePlanRunTuning` only forwards what the caller sent; `resolvePlanRunDriver` falls back to `'cursor'`. Nothing injects worktree or debug when the caller omits them, so **API / scheduled-agent-job / rule-driven enqueues get no worktree and no verbose**, regardless of what the developer UI shows.
- Every queued run is now `runKind: 'orchestrator'` (in-process, no nested `plan-runner` spawn) — see `applications/openthrottle-server/src/queues/plans/plans.types.ts`. The legacy `WORKTREE_TARGETS` pooled-worktree path in `plans.processor.ts` is dead commentary.
- `applications/openthrottle-server/src/queues/agentic-loop/agentic-loop-orchestrator.service.ts` computes `configCwd = getWorkflowConfigCwd(jobData.workingDirectory, process.env)` and calls `maybeRegisterWorktreeCheckout({ filesystemPath: configCwd })`. When the agent CLI creates its own worktree via `-w`, `configCwd` is the **parent repo**, not the worktree — `RepositoryInspectionService.scan()` reports `isLinkedWorktree: false` and registration is skipped, leaving `plan_runs.checkout_id` NULL. This is the core "workspace isn't bound to the worktree" bug.
- Worktree is currently a passthrough agent-CLI flag: `context.worktree` / `worktreeBase` / `skipWorktreeSetup` → `iterationRunner.run()` → `runIterationAsync` → `-w` on `cursor-agent` (`tools/workflows/src/utils/plan-run-worktree-cli.ts`). The orchestrator never learns the resulting path, and `agentCwd` is unchanged.
- `scripts/create_worktree.sh` already handles three invocation modes (CLI arg, Claude `WorktreeCreate` hook payload on stdin, provision-in-place), prints ONLY the absolute worktree path on stdout, allocates a deterministic port block via `scripts/worktree_ports.sh`, and provisions through `scripts/setup_worktree.sh`. The server-side provisioner consumes exactly this contract — it does not reimplement it.

## Target behavior

1. **Worktree by default.** A run enqueued with no explicit worktree config gets one, created by OpenThrottle, with a deterministic collision-free name derived from the plan/run.
2. **Verbose by default.** `debugCli: 'verbose'` in stored defaults *and* injected at enqueue when the caller omits it, so `--verbose` reaches the agent CLI and the run output stream.
3. **Workspace = the worktree.** The orchestrator's `agentCwd`, the registered `repository_checkouts` row, `plan_runs.checkout_id`, and `run_config_snapshot.workspace.workingDirectory` all point at the worktree this run created.
4. **Defaults are server-side, not UI-side.** Every enqueue path (GraphQL mutation, scheduled agent jobs, tag-action rules, OT Loop CLI handoff) inherits them; the developer UI just reflects the same shared defaults.
5. **One configurable worktree root** shared by every agent and by the BullMQ worker.

## Known traps (from prior work)

- A fresh worktree path needs its own agent-CLI MCP approval and a valid `.env`; a stale `.env` shows up as a password prompt. See the recent `make scheduled agent runs reach their MCP servers` / `warn when a provider cannot reach workspace MCP` commits — the new default multiplies how often this path is hit.
- `pnpm run worktree:new` is the ONE provisioning entrypoint; a bare `git worktree add` only self-heals on first `:dev`.
- Existing plans already have persisted `run_config` JSON. New defaults must apply to new plans and to omitted fields, without silently rewriting a plan the user deliberately configured.
- Worktrees accumulate on disk; unbounded creation per run is a real cost.
- Moving the worktree root does not relocate existing worktrees — `git worktree` stores absolute paths in `.git/worktrees/<name>/gitdir`. Changing the root affects new worktrees only.

## Out of scope

- Changing the default backend away from `cursor`.
- Interactive chat runs (`react-router-chat`) — this plan is the BullMQ/programmatic path only.
- Any worktree pooling / `WORKTREE_TARGETS` revival.
- Migrating or relocating worktrees that already exist under `../openthrottle-worktrees`.
- An automatic worktree-cleanup sweep (deferred per the task-1 cleanup decision).

Alphabetize GraphQL document fields (automated)
Ensure GraphQL selection-set fields (and fragment field lists) are alphabetized as much as we can automate, matching the monorepo's "alphabetize when order doesn't matter" convention.

## Motivation

Consumer GraphQL documents (e.g. `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routes/skills.$slug.tsx.graphql`) often list fields in ad-hoc order. Alphabetical field order makes diffs quieter, reviews faster, and keeps documents consistent with our TS/object-key alphabetization rule.

Example target shape — fragment fields ABC'd:

```graphql
fragment SkillDetailUsageBySkill on SkillUsageBySkillObject {
  abandonedCount
  avgDurationMs
  count
  errorCount
  lastUsedAt
  outcomeCount
  scope
  skillName
  successCount
}
```

Today that file is *not* fully alphabetized (`skillName`, `scope`, `count`, …).

## Scope (in)

- GraphQL **documents**: `*.graphql` co-located with routes, package operation docs (developer, admin, website, email, mcp, agentic-loop, vscode-openthrottle, etc.).
- Selection sets inside queries, mutations, subscriptions, and fragments (including nested selections).
- Lint/CI enforcement so new documents cannot regress.
- Optional autofix (ESLint `--fix`, Prettier plugin, or a dedicated sort script) preferred over manual-only cleanup.

## Scope (out / explicit non-goals unless a later task says otherwise)

- NestJS code-first **schema** field declaration order on `@ObjectType` / `@InputType` (decorator order can be domain-intentional; `schema.gql` is generated).
- Reordering operation **arguments** or variable definitions only if the chosen tool supports it safely; prefer fields first.
- Changing runtime behavior or codegen output shapes beyond field order in source documents.

## Approach (investigate → choose → enforce → sweep)

1. Inventory all `*.graphql` document roots and current lint/format pipeline (no `@graphql-eslint` today).
2. Pick automation: prefer existing ecosystem (`@graphql-eslint` custom/community alphabetize rule, Prettier GraphQL plugin + sort, or a small Nx/workspace script using `graphql` AST) that can **lint + autofix**.
3. Wire into monorepo lint (shared ESLint flat config and/or an Nx target) so `pnpm nx affected --target=lint` / CI catches violations.
4. Autofix + commit sweeps per app/package (start with `openthrottle-developer` route docs as the exemplar).
5. Document the convention in coding rules (point at GraphQL documents) so agents/humans know the expectation.

## Acceptance

- A lint/format check fails when selection-set fields are out of alphabetical order.
- Autofix (or a documented one-command sort) brings documents into compliance.
- `openthrottle-developer` route `.graphql` files (including `skills.$slug.tsx.graphql`) pass.
- Other document-owning projects either pass or are listed with a tracked follow-up if intentionally deferred.
- Short rule/docs note: GraphQL selection sets are alphabetized when order does not matter.

# Page title audit + cleanup across openthrottle-developer routes

## Problem

`document.title` across `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routes` was never curated. Titles were emitted by the `@tools/generators:react-router` route template and mostly left as generated, so several routes ship raw PascalCase scaffold identifiers straight to the browser tab. The reported example:

- `app/routes/settings.appearance.tsx` → `SettingsAppearance | OpenThrottle`

That is not a one-off. A sweep of all 191 route files (79 with a `meta` export) found four distinct defect classes plus a root cause.

## Root cause

`tools/generators/src/generators/react-router/files/route/__name__.tsx:24`:

```ts
export const meta = (_args: Route.MetaArgs) => {
  return [{ title: `<%= namePascal %> | ${SITE_TITLE}` }];
};
```

The template interpolates `namePascal` — the flat-route filename converted to Pascal case — as the human-facing title. Every route scaffolded and not hand-edited inherits a machine identifier as its tab title. Fixing the routes without fixing the template guarantees the defect returns with the next generated route.

## Inventory of defects

Baseline: `SITE_TITLE = 'OpenThrottle'` (`app/global/config/settings.ts:4`); root fallback is `Welcome | OpenThrottle` (`app/root.tsx:290`). Most routes wrap meta in `mergeRouteModuleMeta` from `@openthrottle/react-router-utils`.

### Class A — raw scaffold identifiers (4 routes)

| Route | Current title |
| --- | --- |
| `settings.appearance.tsx` | `SettingsAppearance` |
| `notifications._index.tsx` | `NotificationsIndex` |
| `personas.create.tsx` | `PersonasCreate` |
| `plans.temp.tsx` | `TEMP` |

Per-repository keyed concurrency for scheduled agent jobs
# Per-repository keyed concurrency for scheduled agent jobs

Follow-up from OT plan ef4b5c75 (repository targeting for /schedule), which landed the prerequisite but deliberately left concurrency alone.

## Problem

`SCHEDULED_AGENT_JOBS_CONCURRENCY = 1` (`applications/openthrottle-server/src/queues/scheduled-agent-jobs/scheduled-agent-jobs.constants.ts`) exists because two agent CLIs sharing one cwd fight over the git index. Every scheduled job in the system therefore runs strictly serially, even when the jobs target completely unrelated checkouts.

ef4b5c75 made per-repository targeting real: a schedule now names a `repository_checkout_id`, and every run records the exact `resolved_cwd` it executed in. That makes >1 *conceivable* — but NOT safe on its own, which is why it was left at 1 with a comment saying so. Two schedules can still target the SAME checkout, so simply raising the number reintroduces the original git-index race.

## Goal

Allow genuinely-independent scheduled runs to overlap, while still serialising any two runs that would land in the same directory.

## Design sketch

- The concurrency key is the run's **resolved cwd**, not the checkout id: a schedule with a legacy explicit `cwd` and a schedule targeting a checkout can resolve to the same directory, and the id-based key would miss that. `resolveScheduledAgentJobRunCwd` already centralises this resolution.
- Investigate BullMQ's grouping / rate-limit-by-key facilities against the version pinned here; a group key per resolved cwd with a per-group concurrency of 1 is the shape. If groups are unavailable in the OSS version, the fallback is an application-level advisory lock (a Redis key per resolved cwd) taken in the processor before `runner.run`, releasing in the `finally` block — with a TTL so a crashed worker cannot deadlock a directory forever.
- The processor resolves the cwd BEFORE claiming its run row today, so the key is available early enough to gate on.
- `settings.worktree` runs are already isolated per run; consider whether they should bypass the lock entirely (their effective cwd differs from the checkout path).

## Acceptance

- Two schedules targeting different checkouts demonstrably run concurrently (verified by overlapping run timestamps).
- Two schedules targeting the same checkout — including one via a checkout and one via a legacy `cwd` resolving to the same path — still serialise.
- A worker killed mid-run does not permanently block that directory.
- The concurrency constant and the comment left by ef4b5c75 are updated to describe the new mechanism.
Give the scheduled-agent-jobs worker a per-repository concurrency key derived from each run's resolved cwd, so SCHEDULED_AGENT_JOBS_CONCURRENCY can exceed 1 without two CLIs fighting over one git index.

Screencast pipeline polish found producing 04-mental-model
Filed from plan 09b88bff-036a-4bae-bae6-0b86b43d2538 (the 04-mental-model short). None of these blocked that video; all three affect every flow, so they are their own work rather than comments in a flow file.

## 1. The portrait pass lays out as desktop, wasting most of the Short frame

`runner/run.ts --portrait` records at 1080x1920. 1080 CSS pixels is ABOVE the app's mobile breakpoint (768), so the app renders its desktop layout — sidebar and all — and on a content-light route roughly 60% of the frame is empty background below the content. Verified on the 04-mental-model 9:16 master.

Options: record the portrait pass at a genuinely mobile viewport (e.g. 540x960 at deviceScaleFactor 2, which still downsamples to 1080x1920) so the app's mobile layout fills the frame; or keep the viewport and have the assembler scale the content region up. The first is closer to what a viewer would actually see on a phone.

Not a publish blocker — the captured text is legible either way — but it is the difference between a Short that looks composed for the format and one that looks like a cropped desktop.

## 2. A missing region-of-interest selector costs 30 seconds per step, silently

`sampleRegion` in `runner/run.ts` calls `page.locator(selector).first().boundingBox()` and `.catch(() => null)`. A selector that does not match burns Playwright's 30s default timeout, the error is swallowed, and because nothing is added to `sampledBeats` it retries on EVERY subsequent step of that beat.

One wrong selector turned a 54-second recording into 264 seconds with no error and no warning — the run "succeeded". Give the call a short explicit timeout (a region either exists now or does not) and log loudly when a declared region never resolves. A silent 5x inflation is worse than a failure.

## 3. Dev-only server metrics are in frame on every beat

Both 04-mental-model masters carry a "Server metrics — RSS 286.2 MB · Heap 205.49 MB · CPU 5,533 ms" footer across the bottom of every shot. It is real UI rather than a leak, so `video-scan` passes it, but it is developer diagnostics on a marketing video and the numbers change every take.

The runner already hides the editor deep-link buttons for recording; this belongs in the same list, or behind whatever flag the footer should have had.
Three pipeline-wide issues surfaced while producing the mental-model short; none blocked it, all affect every future video.

Configurable privacy levels for skill-usage capture (future / paid-feature track)
## Origin

Spun out of the **Skill usage tracking** plan (OT d3759118). That plan ships skill-usage capture with a FIXED default privacy level (truncated args) but deliberately funnels args through a single `applyPrivacy(level, args)` seam. This plan turns that seam into a real, user-configurable control — a natural productizable / paid-tier feature (fine-grained telemetry governance is something orgs pay for).

**Depends on** OT d3759118 shipping the `applyPrivacy` seam + persistence first. Do not start until at least Phases 1–2 of that plan exist.

## Levels to support (draft)

- `off` — capture nothing (skill not recorded at all).
- `name-only` — skill name + metadata (session, cwd, branch, scope, timestamp); NO args.
- `truncated` — name-only + args truncated/redacted (the fixed default from the base plan).
- `full` — full args verbatim (heaviest privacy/retention burden; likely gated behind explicit opt-in).

## Dimensions to think through (design task should settle these)

1. **Config scope & precedence** — global default vs per-project vs per-skill override. Where does the setting live (settings.json? OT rollout flags — see OT 184a4971? server-side org policy)? Likely a hybrid with a clear precedence order.
2. **Enforcement point** — client-side (hook redacts before it ever leaves the machine — strongest privacy guarantee) vs server-side policy. Client-side redaction should be the floor so raw args never transit when a lower level is set.
3. **Retention** — different retention windows per level (e.g. `full` args auto-expire faster). Ties into a retention/TTL job.
4. **Paid-feature gating** — which levels / which granularity (per-skill overrides, org policy enforcement, audit log) sit behind a paid tier. Reuse the rollout/feature-flag package (OT 184a4971) rather than bespoke gating.
5. **Auditability** — an org admin should be able to see/prove what level is in effect and that lower levels actually redact.

## Not now

This is a design-first, future track. No implementation until the base capture plan is live and there's real demand signal. Keep it on the roadmap, not in the current build queue.

# Settings › Setup: per-model enable/disable + favorite models

## Context — this is a follow-up
Builds directly on **"Settings › Setup: agent CLIs as an actionable table + per-user enable/disable"** (OT plan `84d4a42b-ead1-4944-9bb0-6a171d39c427`), which introduces the compact `SettingsSetupTable`, per-user **agent-level** on/off persistence, and the downstream gate (hide from chat/model pickers + block new runs). Do not start until that plan's persistence + table land; this plan extends the same seams rather than inventing new ones.

## Goals
1. **Per-model enable/disable.** Extend the per-user enable/disable state from the agent (backend) granularity down to individual **models** within an agent. Row expansion in `SettingsSetupTable` reveals per-model toggles; an agent-level toggle remains a bulk control over its models. Semantics to settle: does disabling every model imply the agent is off, and does an agent-off hard-override individual model state?
2. **Favorite models.** Let a user star/favorite specific models. Favoriting is cheap to add once model-level rows exist (same per-user, per-(backend,model) store). Favorites float to the top of / are highlighted in chat model pickers and run selection.
3. **Surface downstream.** Chat/model pickers and run/scheduled-job selection consume per-model enabled + favorite state (ordering + filtering), reusing the gate wired at agent granularity in the base plan.

## Design questions to resolve first
- Storage shape: extend the base plan's per-user disabled-agents store to a per-(user, backend, model) table, or a superset store keyed by (user, backend, model?) with a null model meaning "whole agent".
- Precedence between agent-level and model-level state (override vs. union).
- Whether favorite implies enabled.
- Model identity stability: models come from `discoverAgentClis` probing and can change between scans — key favorites/toggles by (backend, model-id string) and tolerate models that disappear.

## SHIPPED BY BASE PLAN 84d4a42b (actual seams to extend — verified in code)
- **Persistence**: table `user_disabled_agent_clis (id, user_id, backend, created_at)` — **presence-as-disabled** (a row = disabled; absence = enabled; empty table = default all-enabled). Migration `databases/migrations/091_create_user_disabled_agent_clis.sql`. NOTE: this is a DISABLED-set, not an enabled-set — extending to models likely means adding a nullable `model` column (null = whole agent) with a partial/overloaded unique key, OR a sibling table; decide precedence there.
- **Service**: `AgentCliPreferencesService` in a NEW package module `@openthrottle/nestjs-repositories` → `modules/agent-cli-preferences/` (NOT under `graphql/agent-setup/*`). API: `getDisabledBackends(userId): Set<string>`, `isEnabled(userId, backend)`, `setEnabled(userId, backend, enabled)`.
- **Mutation**: `setAgentEnabled(backend, enabled): SetAgentEnabledResult` on `AgentSetupResolver` (SETTINGS_WRITE, isDriverId-validated). A per-model variant would live alongside it.
- **Query surface**: `enabled: Boolean!` is on `AgentCliOptionObject` (the `discoverAgentClis` agents), resolved per-request by overlaying the caller's disabled set AFTER the shared discovery cache — NOT on `agentCliSetupConfig`. A per-model `enabled`/`favorite` would extend the model shape here (models are currently a `[String!]` list; per-model state needs an object type — a breaking reshape, so add-only/deprecate).

Chat tool cards: show the real tool name, not "name"
## Symptom

In a chat thread every tool card and every folded tool group renders `name` as its header (see the group header "name · 10 actions" with ten child rows all titled "name"). Expanding a row shows the truth: the arguments payload is `{"name": "view_file", "parameters": {…}}` — the real tool is `view_file`. The header is repetitive and carries zero information.

## Root cause

`packages/react-router-chat/src/turn-events.ts` derives the tool name by key-sniffing:

```ts
const extractToolName = (toolCall: unknown): string => {
  if (!isRecord(toolCall)) return 'tool';
  const name = Object.keys(toolCall).find(
    (key) => key !== 'toolCallId' && key !== 'hookAdditionalContexts',
  );
  return name === undefined ? 'tool' : name.replace(/ToolCall$/, '');
};
```

That heuristic was written for the cursor-agent shape (`{ toolCallId, readToolCall: {…} }`, where the first non-reserved key IS the tool). Every other driver in `packages/openthrottle-agentic-utils/src/utils/conversation-backend/*/events.ts` emits a different shape, and the heuristic misreads all of them:

| driver | metadata shape | header today | should be |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| cursor-agent | `toolCall: { toolCallId, readToolCall: {…} }` | `read` ✅ | `read` |
| gemini | `toolCall: { name, parameters }` | **`name`** | `view_file` |
| antigravity | `toolCall: { name, parameters }` / result `{ error, name, output, status }` | **`name`** | `view_file` |
| claude | `metadata.name` (no `toolCall` key at all) | **`tool`** | `Read` |
| opencode | `metadata.tool` + `metadata.toolPart` | **`tool`** | the part's tool |

So four of five backends render a useless header; only cursor-agent is accidentally correct. Same defect hits `toolLabelFromMetadataJson`, used for the one-line activity marker, and it flows through both the live stream (`turn-events.ts`) and the persisted path (`map-persisted-messages.ts`) since both go through `parseChunkMetadata`.

Secondary: the antigravity/gemini call payload is double-wrapped — `toolCall: { name, parameters: payload.tool_info }` where `tool_info` is itself `{ name, parameters }` — which is why the expanded Arguments block shows `name`/`parameters` twice.

## Direction

1. Drivers emit a canonical, explicit `metadata.toolName` (string) at the chunk boundary — the client should never have to guess.
2. The client prefers explicit fields (`toolName`, then `name`/`tool`) and keeps the key-sniff only as a legacy fallback for already-persisted cursor-agent conversations. Old rows must keep rendering correctly.
3. Rendering stays as-is otherwise: mono, truncating, `event.name` in `ChatToolCall` and `activeToolOf(...).name` in `ChatToolCallGroup`.

## Files

- `packages/react-router-chat/src/turn-events.ts` (`extractToolName`, `normalizeMetadata`, `toolLabelFromMetadataJson`)
- `packages/react-router-chat/src/components/ChatToolCall.tsx`, `ChatToolCallGroup.tsx` (display only)
- `packages/openthrottle-agentic-utils/src/utils/conversation-backend/{claude,cursor-agent,gemini,antigravity,opencode}/events.ts`
- Tests: `packages/react-router-chat/src/__tests__/turn-events.test.ts`, `map-persisted-messages.test.ts`, and the per-driver event tests

## Done when

A thread run against each driver shows real tool names (`view_file`, `Read`, `edit`, …) on both the group header and every child card, with no `name`/`tool` placeholders for any driver that reports one, and persisted (reloaded) conversations render identically to live ones.
Tool-call headers in chat threads render the literal string "name" (or the generic "tool") because the client sniffs the first key of the toolCall payload instead of reading the tool name. Make each driver emit a canonical toolName and make the client prefer it.

Target a repository for scheduled agent job (/schedule) runs
# Target a repository for /schedule runs

## Problem

A scheduled agent job (`/schedule` in openthrottle-developer, `scheduled_agent_jobs` in Postgres) has no notion of *which repository* it runs against. The only targeting knob is a free-text `cwd` column:

- `databases/migrations/082_create_scheduled_agent_jobs.sql` — `cwd TEXT NULL`, "Process cwd for the agent CLI; null falls back to WORKSPACE_ROOT ?? process.cwd()".
- `applications/openthrottle-server/src/queues/scheduled-agent-jobs/scheduled-agent-jobs.constants.ts` — `resolveScheduledAgentJobCwd()` (explicit cwd → `WORKSPACE_ROOT` → `process.cwd()`).
- `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routing/schedule/components/ScheduleForm.tsx` — a bare `Working directory (optional)` text input, placeholder "Defaults to the workspace root".

Consequences: the user must know and hand-type an absolute host path; the path is never validated or ownership-checked; it is not host/container aware; nothing ties a run to a repository for provenance; and every schedule silently defaults to the one canonical checkout (which is also why `SCHEDULED_AGENT_JOBS_CONCURRENCY = 1` — two CLIs in one cwd would fight over the git index).

The streaming chat path already solved exactly this. `StartConversationStreamInput.repositoryId` (`applications/openthrottle-server/src/graphql/conversation-stream/conversation-stream.input.ts`) takes a registered repository checkout id, and the resolver (`conversation-stream.resolver.ts` ~L476-500) resolves it via `repositories.findByIdForUser(repositoryId, userId)` → `toContainerPath(repository.filesystemPath)`, requires a repository in production, and keeps a `DEV_CWD_ENV` escape hatch for development. **/schedule should adopt that same model.**

## Goal

Let a scheduled job target a registered repository checkout by id, resolve the cwd server-side from that checkout (ownership-checked, container-path-aware), snapshot the resolved path on each run for provenance, and replace the free-text working-directory input with a repository picker — without breaking existing rows that only carry `cwd`.

## Design

**Data model** (`repository_checkouts` from migration 078 is the target; `workspace_local_repositories` is the deprecated view over it):

- `scheduled_agent_jobs.repository_checkout_id UUID NULL REFERENCES repository_checkouts (id) ON DELETE SET NULL` + index. Nullable so existing rows lift cleanly.
- `cwd` stays, re-commented as the legacy/explicit-path fallback, and is deprecated in GraphQL (`@deprecated`, never removed — CLAUDE.md schema rule).
- Runs get provenance: `scheduled_agent_job_runs.repository_checkout_id UUID NULL` (ON DELETE SET NULL) and `resolved_cwd TEXT NULL`, so a run's history survives a later schedule edit or checkout deletion. Sibling of the existing `settings_snapshot` column from migration 087.

**Resolution precedence** (one shared helper, documented in one place):
1. `repository_checkout_id` → checkout `filesystem_path` → `toContainerPath(...)` (from `@openthrottle/openthrottle-agentic-utils`; identity on host-run flows, mount-aware under a containerized server — mirrors `workspace-editor-config.service` and the chat resolver).
2. explicit `cwd` (legacy rows / power users).
3. `WORKSPACE_ROOT` → `process.cwd()` (today's behavior, kept so nothing regresses).

**Where resolution happens.** The BullMQ payload is a self-contained snapshot built at scheduler-upsert / run-now time (`buildScheduledAgentJobPayload` in `scheduled-agent-job-scheduler.service.ts`), so it must carry both `repositoryCheckoutId` and the resolved `cwd`. Because a scheduler payload can be arbitrarily stale (a checkout can move or be removed months after upsert), the processor re-resolves from `repositoryCheckoutId` when present and treats the payload path as fallback — one indexed read per run, and a moved checkout keeps working.

**Ownership.** Resolve against the schedule's `owner_user_id` (already on the row) using the same `findByIdForUser` check the chat path uses, and validate at write time in the GraphQL service so a bad or foreign checkout id fails at create/update rather than at 3am.

**Concurrency.** Note (do not change) that `SCHEDULED_AGENT_JOBS_CONCURRENCY = 1` exists because of shared-cwd git-index contention. Per-repository targeting makes raising it *possible*, but that needs per-repo keyed concurrency — explicitly out of scope, captured as a follow-up.

## Non-goals

- Raising worker concurrency or per-repository queue partitioning.
- Auto-provisioning a worktree per run (`settings.worktree` already exists; untouched).
- Removing `cwd` from the schema or GraphQL.
- Repository targeting for OT Loop plan runs (tracked separately with the run-provenance work).

## Acceptance

- A schedule can be created and edited with a repository picked from the user's registered checkouts; no path typing required.
- The agent CLI actually spawns in that checkout's directory (verified in run output).
- Existing `cwd`-only schedules keep running unchanged.
- A run row records the repository and the exact resolved cwd; the run detail page shows both.
- Picking a foreign or unknown checkout id is rejected at write time with a clear message.
- `pnpm run check:local` green; `schema.gql` + `__generated__` committed.
Let a scheduled job target a registered repository checkout by id instead of a hand-typed cwd: FK on scheduled_agent_jobs, server-side ownership-checked + container-aware cwd resolution, per-run provenance snapshot, and a repository picker in ScheduleForm. Mirrors the chat path's repositoryId model.

Fix cursor-agent first-chat startup failures (cold session mint)
## Problem

The `cursor-agent` chat backend intermittently fails on the **first** chat of a session/conversation. It is a cold-start / first-invocation symptom: switching to another agent (claude/codex/opencode), sending one chat, then switching back to cursor usually makes cursor work.

## Current architecture (as of this plan)

- `packages/openthrottle-agentic-utils/src/utils/conversation-backend/cursor-agent/cursor-agent.ts`
  - `createCursorAgentSession()` spawns `cursor-agent create-chat`, accumulates stdout, and returns **`stdout.trim()` verbatim** as the session id.
  - `streamCursorAgent()` spawns a second process: `--print --output-format stream-json --stream-partial-output --workspace <cwd> --trust --resume <sessionId> [-- prompt]`.
  - Both children run under `buildScrubbedEnv()` - an allowlist of exactly `CURSOR_API_KEY, HOME, LANG, LC_ALL, LOGNAME, PATH, TERM, TMPDIR, USER`.
- `applications/openthrottle-server/src/graphql/conversation-stream/conversation-stream.service.ts:260`
  - On the first cursor turn (`sessionId` null/empty) it publishes a keepalive, then awaits `mintCursorSession()`. A throw becomes a terminal `Failed to start a cursor-agent session: ...` chunk. **No retry.**
  - The minted id is persisted to `conversation.metadata[cursorSessionId]`.
- Timeouts (`cursor-agent/teardown.ts`): `resolveSessionCreateTimeoutMs()` default **30_000 ms** (`OPENTHROTTLE_AGENT_SESSION_TIMEOUT_MS`); per-agent idle 120s, wall-clock 900s.

## Findings — task 1 evidence gate (COMPLETE)

Full raw capture is on the plan output stream. Verdicts, re-ranked:

1. **(NEW, reproduced) Cold startup does unbounded blocking network work and the child does not exit promptly.** With `~/.cursor/statsig-cache.json` moved aside, the turn reported `outcome=success duration_ms=15150` yet the process had still not closed **4+ minutes later**; warm baseline for the same sequence is **result → close = 3021 ms**. Cold startup does MCP OAuth discovery over the network (`needsAuth` / `Unauthorized`) and runs Claude-plugin hooks at 1–4 s each, some firing *after* the turn ends. cursor also leaks a `worker-server` grandchild that inherits our stdout pipe and outlives the run (observed alive 2:44 later) — and `terminateChild()` signals only the direct child, never the process group.
2. **H3 env allowlist — PARTIALLY CONFIRMED.** Not the trigger on this machine (none set), but provably wrong: `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` (selects the config dir, so our child can use a *different chat store* than the user's terminal), `AGENT_CLI_CREDENTIAL_STORE` (`file`|`memory`|`default`; `default` on darwin = macOS login keychain), `HTTPS_PROXY`/`HTTP_PROXY` (dropped = no network behind a corporate proxy). Also read by cursor: `CURSOR_AUTH_TOKEN`, `CURSOR_DATA_DIR`, `SHELL`, `NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED`, `CI`.
3. **(NEW) Keychain auth from a daemon-spawned child.** Mechanism and exact error strings captured (`Authentication required. Please run 'agent login' first…`, `⚠ Warning: The provided API key is invalid.`, both exit 1 with ANSI on stderr; keychain osStatus 36/44/45 mapped by cursor). Unconfirmed as the trigger.
4. **H1 (banner poisons the id) — DISPROVEN as the failure cause.** `handleCreateChat` is local-only and `console-io` writes the id to stdout and *everything else* to stderr; ~10 runs (cold, fresh workspace, concurrent) gave byte-identical clean output. Decisively, **`--resume` accepts any string** — resuming with a never-minted UUID and with the literal `"Update available!  1.2.3"` both produced full successful turns. Survives re-scoped: a polluted id silently starts a *fresh, disconnected* chat, losing multi-turn continuity while appearing to work.
5. **H4 (poisoned persisted id = dead end) — DISPROVEN.** Resume never rejects an id, so there is no "chat not found" signal. **Task 6's re-mint-on-resume-failure half has no trigger and must be dropped or re-scoped;** the retry-on-mint-failure half stands.
6. **H2 (cold token mint in `create-chat`) — DISPROVEN.** Local-only (`randomUUID()` + SQLite store), no network, no auth, 2.0–2.6 s warm *and* cold, clean under 4-way concurrency — ~12× headroom against the 30 s budget.

**Task 2 (structured logging) is now the critical path**, not merely standalone-valuable: naming which failure the user actually hits needs server-side evidence.

## Scope

In scope: the cursor-agent backend adapter, the mint call site in `ConversationStreamService`, its timeouts/retries, and the composer-facing error copy. Out of scope: other CLI backends (except where a shared helper is the right home), and any change to cursor's own model/flag surface.

## Success criteria

- A cold-start reproduction is captured with raw stdout/stderr bytes (task 1) and the failure mode is named. ✅
- First cursor chat in a fresh session succeeds without the switch-to-another-agent workaround.
- A bad mint is recoverable: bounded retry on the mint. (Re-mint-on-resume-failure is moot — see H4.)
- A minted id is validated so a conversation can never silently fork into a disconnected chat.
- Teardown reaps the whole process group, so `worker-server` grandchildren do not accumulate.
- Failures the user cannot fix (auth expired, cursor-agent not installed) surface as distinct, actionable composer copy — ANSI-stripped, never a raw exit code or a silent hang.

## References

- `docs/openthrottle/agentic-cli-chat-backends.md`
- `docs/openthrottle/agentic-cli-backend-compatibility-guide.md`
- `docs/openthrottle/cursor-agent-stream-json-schema.md`

💰 CI cost reduction: free-tier runners, cache egress, and run volume
## Context

Measured on 2026-08-18 against `OpenThrottle/monorepo`:

- **Repo visibility: PUBLIC** (`gh repo view` → `"visibility":"PUBLIC"`, 47 MB). Standard GitHub-hosted runners (`ubuntu-latest`, 4 vCPU / 16 GB) are **free with unlimited minutes on public repos**. Larger/managed runners are not.
- **Every job runs on `blacksmith-4vcpu-ubuntu-2204`** — `changes`, `build`, `ci-success`, `nx-dependency-graph` in `continuous-integration.yml`, plus both jobs in `vercel-deploy.yml`. Same 4 vCPU count as the free GitHub box, with *less* RAM (GitHub's standard runner is 16 GB).
- **Live spend is essentially one workflow.** `openthrottle-docker.yml`, `vercel-deploy.yml`, `secret-scan.yml`, `daily-merged-prs-summary.yml`, `dependency-graph-scheduled.yml`, `docs-watch.yml` are all already `if: false` or dispatch-gated. The 💰 markers throughout show this ground has been worked; the remaining wins are structural, not more disabling.
- **Volume is the multiplier.** 100 workflow runs in an 8-hour window (2026-08-17 23:40 → 2026-08-18 07:47), of which 26 were Continuous Integration. Extrapolates to ~78 CI runs/day ≈ ~2,300/month. Per-job timing over the last 12 CI runs: `build` avg **5.3 min** (ran 6 of 12 times; the draft/docs gate correctly skipped the rest), while `changes` and `ci-success` each spin a **separate billed runner** — so even a docs-only or draft PR pays two runner startups, and a real build pays three.
- **GCS Nx cache**: `gs://openthrottle-staging-nx-cache` is 2.19 GB, US multi-region, 90-day lifecycle. Storage is pennies; the cost is **egress**. GitHub-hosted runners are on Azure, so every cache read is billed GCS internet egress (~$0.12/GB) plus Class B ops, on every one of those ~2,300 runs/month. Meanwhile `.github/actions/node-setup` **already** caches `.nx/cache` via `actions/cache` — a free layer duplicating a paid one.

## Strategy

Do not trade away correctness or the CREEP-safe (CVE-2025-36852) cache model. Every change here is either "same guarantee, $0 instead of $" or "delete work that gates nothing".

Ordered by expected saving per unit of effort:

1. Move compute to the free tier the public repo already entitles us to.
2. Stop paying egress for a cache layer we duplicate for free — and note that GitHub Actions cache scoping (a PR branch reads its base branch's caches but cannot write into them) reproduces the current trusted-`main`-writes / PRs-read-only model *by construction*.
3. Cut run volume at the source (agentic per-task pushes).
4. Stop re-running full-tree checks whose result cannot have changed.

## Non-goals

- Re-enabling any currently disabled workflow.
- Removing test coverage or lint/typecheck gates to save minutes.
- Nx Cloud DTE (see `nx-audit-plan` — already decided against).

## Baseline to beat

~2,300 CI runs/month; ~7 billed job-minutes per real build (5.3 build + 2 satellite runners), ~2 per skipped run; ~2,300 GCS cache-read sessions/month of egress.
Cut GitHub Actions / CI spend for a budget-limited OSS monorepo. Headline lever: OpenThrottle/monorepo is a PUBLIC repo, so standard GitHub-hosted runners are free and unlimited — yet every job runs on paid blacksmith-4vcpu-ubuntu-2204. Second lever: the paid GCS Nx remote cache duplicates a free actions/cache layer that is already wired. Third lever: run volume (~78 CI runs/day observed) from agentic per-task pushes.

Squash "workspace is out of sync" (@nx/js:typescript-sync gate) for frictionless worktrees
# Goal

Permanently stop the recurring `NX  The workspace is out of sync … [@nx/js:typescript-sync] … Run 'nx sync'` hard-fail that blocks `pnpm nx run <proj>:{typecheck,test,lint}` in non-interactive shells (fresh worktrees especially), so a worktree is usable immediately without a manual `nx sync` dance. This is a sibling to OT c9545bb0 (tool-agnostic worktree *provisioning*); that plan fixes stale `.env`, this one fixes the Nx sync gate.

# Root cause (verified 2026-08-07)

1. The custom Nx plugin `tools/nx-plugins/package-typecheck.ts:126` re-attaches `syncGenerators: ['@nx/js:typescript-sync']` to the `typecheck` target (it owns the target because `@nx/js`'s built-in typecheck is disabled). So the sync gate fires on `typecheck` for every `{applications,packages,tools}/*` project.
2. `nx.json` has only `sync: { applyChanges: true }` — no `disabledTaskSyncGenerators`. `applyChanges` auto-applies **only in an interactive TTY** (and silently in CI); a plain Bash/worktree shell has no TTY, so Nx errors out *before running the target*.
3. The generator's output cannot be trusted: on Nx 22.7.4 it injects phantom cross-references BETWEEN the 4 React Router apps (developer/website/admin → email, admin → developer) — `type: static` graph edges backed by NO import / tsconfig ref / paths entry, unstable across runs. Upstream defect: https://github.com/nrwl/nx/issues/36297. Applying them writes bogus refs into the apps' `tsconfig.json` and BREAKS their `typecheck`. So `nx sync` is never a safe remedy for this workspace.

Net: the sync generator provides negative value here (it can only produce noise or breakage), yet it gates every typecheck. The durable fix is to stop letting it gate targets, reconcile the small set of REAL tsconfig-reference drifts by hand one time, and replace auto-sync with a non-blocking check + manual discipline.

# Recommended approach

**Disable the `@nx/js:typescript-sync` task-sync generator globally** via committed `nx.json`:

```json
"sync": {
  "applyChanges": true,
  "disabledTaskSyncGenerators": ["@nx/js:typescript-sync"]
}
```

Critical distinction: `disabledTaskSyncGenerators` disables ONLY the tsconfig-reference sync gate. It does **NOT** touch `@nx/js.analyzeSourceFiles`, so the project-graph edges that drive `nx affected` and build ordering remain intact. This is fundamentally different from the previously ruled-out `analyzeSourceFiles: false` (which drops ~85 real edges). This exact edit has been used repeatedly as an *uncommitted temporary* workaround with no side effects — this plan makes it permanent and cleans up the fallout it papered over.

Trade-off accepted: tsconfig `references` are now maintained manually (they already are, de-facto — policy is already "NEVER run nx sync"). We compensate with a one-time reconcile of real drift + an optional non-gating check so genuine drift is still visible without blocking work.

# Out of scope
- Worktree `.env` / DB seeding (OT c9545bb0).
- Upgrading Nx past the bug (large, uncertain; revisit only if the bug is fixed upstream).

Fix agentic-hooks bundle targets: undeclared dependency on nodejs-utils dist
Found while validating CI sharding on a fat affected graph (plan `b19377d1`, task `befc47c3`). **Pre-existing and independent of sharding** — reproduced locally with no matrix involved.

## Symptom

`@openthrottle/agentic-hooks:bundle-hooks-check` fails on a clean checkout:

```
✘ [ERROR] Could not resolve "@openthrottle/nodejs-utils"
    packages/agentic-hooks/src/adapters/cursor/payload.ts:9:25
  The module "./dist/src/index.js" was not found on the file system:
    packages/agentic-hooks/node_modules/@openthrottle/nodejs-utils/package.json:13:16
```

Observed on CI run `32198879567` (all three shards). Reproduced locally with:

```bash
rm -rf packages/nodejs-utils/dist
pnpm exec nx run @openthrottle/agentic-hooks:bundle-hooks-check --skip-nx-cache
```

Restoring `packages/nodejs-utils/dist` makes it pass again.

## Root cause

Two gaps that only fail together:

1. **`bundle-hooks` and `bundle-hooks-check` declare no `dependsOn`** (see the `nx.targets` block in `packages/agentic-hooks/package.json`). They esbuild-bundle `packages/agentic-hooks/src/**`, which imports `@openthrottle/nodejs-utils`, so they need that dependency materialized — but Nx is never told, and so never schedules it.
2. **`@openthrottle/nodejs-utils` has no target that emits `dist/src/index.js`.** Its `exports` map points at `./dist/src/index.js` / `./dist/src/index.d.ts`, but its `nx.targets` are `__build: {}` / `__build-package: {}` (prefixed, i.e. disabled) plus `lint`/`test`/`typecheck`. `typecheck` runs `tsc --emitDeclarationOnly`, producing the `.d.ts` but **not** the `.js` esbuild needs.

## Why nobody noticed

The failure is masked from both directions:

- **On CI:** `bundle-hooks-check` is `cache: true`, and its `inputs` do not include the dependency's `dist`. Once the target hash was recorded as passing, every later run cache-hits and the command never executes. It only ran for real on the fat-graph run above because an unrelated `nx.json` edit invalidated the hash.
- **Locally:** dev machines carry a stale `packages/nodejs-utils/dist` from some earlier build, so esbuild resolves it and the check passes.

Sharding did not cause this and did not fix it — the shard run simply happened to be the first real execution in a long time. Worth noting that project sharding *would* have surfaced it eventually anyway: with the dependency on a different box, co-scheduling can no longer accidentally satisfy it.

## Work

1. Decide the resolution shape. Either (a) give `@openthrottle/nodejs-utils` a real `build` target so its dist-pointing `exports` are honest, or (b) make `nodejs-utils` source-first (`main`/`exports` → `./src/index.ts`, like `@tools/dotfiles`) so esbuild bundles from source and no dist is needed. Note the constraint from prior work: packages the **server** imports need top-level exports resolving to `dist` for Docker type-stripping, so check whether `nodejs-utils` is server-consumed before choosing (b).
2. Add the missing `dependsOn` (`^build`, or whatever step 1 settles on) to **both** `bundle-hooks` and `bundle-hooks-check`.
3. Fix the cache correctness that hid this: the `inputs` for both targets must cover whatever the bundle actually reads, so a missing or changed dependency invalidates the hash instead of serving a stale pass.
4. Audit for siblings — any other `nx:run-commands` target that bundles or imports workspace packages without a `dependsOn` has the same latent bug.

## Success

`rm -rf packages/nodejs-utils/dist && pnpm exec nx run @openthrottle/agentic-hooks:bundle-hooks-check --skip-nx-cache` passes from a cold cache, because Nx builds what the bundle needs rather than relying on a leftover artifact.
Superseded — fixed by later merged work, closed 2026-11-14. nodejs-utils went source-first (main/types/exports → ./src/index.ts) in f4d2c0d10 (#540), so esbuild bundles from source and no dist is needed. bundle-hooks and bundle-hooks-check now declare dependsOn ["^build"] and include ^production in their inputs. Verified on main: with packages/nodejs-utils/dist removed, `pnpm exec nx run @openthrottle/agentic-hooks:bundle-hooks-check --skip-nx-cache` succeeds. The sibling audit (work item 4) was not re-run.

🔀 Enable GitHub merge queues on Continuous Integration
## Why

Today every PR is validated against the `main` it branched from, then merged with no re-validation. That is the classic semantic-conflict hole: two PRs that are individually green can break `main` together. A merge queue closes it by building each entry against `main` + the entries ahead of it, and only fast-forwarding when that build is green.

The plumbing is already half-built and currently inert:

- `.github/workflows/continuous-integration.yml:30` already declares `merge_group: types: [checks_requested]`.
- `docs/monorepo/NX.md:27` explicitly records the state: *"The `merge_group` trigger is still wired but inert — there is no merge queue enabled."*
- Line 245 of the workflow reasons about shard behavior with the note "No merge queue on this plan, so the ready PR is the gate" — that comment becomes wrong the moment the queue is on.

So this plan is mostly **configuration + verification + doc/agent-workflow reconciliation**, not a workflow rewrite. The hard parts are the traps, listed below.

## Current repo state (measured, 2026-08-18)

Two overlapping protection surfaces on `main`, which is itself something this plan must reconcile:

- **Classic branch protection** (`/branches/main/protection`): `required_status_checks.contexts = ["ci-success"]`, `strict: false`, `require_code_owner_reviews: true`, `required_approving_review_count: 0`, `enforce_admins: false`.
- **Ruleset `main` (id 14604876)**, enforcement `active`: rules `deletion`, `non_fast_forward`, `required_linear_history`, `pull_request` with `allowed_merge_methods: ["rebase"]` and `required_approving_review_count: 0`. **No** `required_status_checks` rule, **no** `merge_queue` rule, no bypass actors.
- Repo merge settings: `allow_squash_merge: true`, `allow_rebase_merge: true`, `allow_merge_commit: false`, `allow_auto_merge: true`, `delete_branch_on_merge: true`, `squash_merge_commit_title: PR_TITLE`, `squash_merge_commit_message: COMMIT_MESSAGES`. Repo is **public**.

`ci-success` is the only required context, and it is a stable non-matrix job (`continuous-integration.yml:520`) that already aggregates the 3 build shards. That is exactly the shape a merge queue wants — no work needed there.

## The traps (why this is a plan and not a checkbox)

1. **Every required check must fire on `merge_group`, or the queue stalls.** A required context whose workflow has no `merge_group` trigger simply never reports inside the queue; GitHub waits out `check_response_timeout_minutes` and dequeues the PR. Right now only `ci-success` is required and only `continuous-integration.yml` has the trigger, so we are safe *today* — but `secret-scan.yml`, `openthrottle-docker.yml`, `terraform-validate.yml`, and `vercel-deploy.yml` are all PR-triggered and none carry `merge_group`. Anyone who later marks one required silently arms a stall.
2. **`required_linear_history` + `allowed_merge_methods: ["rebase"]` constrain the queue's own merge method.** The queue has an independent merge method (`MERGE`/`SQUASH`/`REBASE`); `MERGE` is incompatible with linear history. Whichever we choose has to preserve conventional-commit titles and the `Plan-Id:` / `Task-Id:` footers that the OT work ledger and traceability depend on.
3. **The merged SHA is not the PR branch SHA.** Queue entries build (and merge) a rewritten commit. Any agent flow that assumes "the SHA I pushed is the SHA on `main`" — notably `record_artifact` of the merged squash on the work ledger — must read the SHA back from `main` after the merge lands, not from the local branch.
4. **`gh pr merge` stops being synchronous.** With a queue on, merging enqueues; the actual merge happens minutes later and can *fail out of the queue*. OT Loops, the `github-pull-request` skill, and any "merge then continue" automation need to either use `--auto` and stop waiting, or poll to completion.
5. **CI runs roughly double** (PR run + merge-group run, and the existing `push: main` trigger fires a third time after the fast-forward). Free on a public repo — see `docs/monorepo/ci-cost.md` — but the `push: main` run is now largely redundant re-validation of a commit the queue just validated, and is worth an explicit keep/drop decision rather than drift.
6. **Concurrency.** `continuous-integration.yml:56` groups on `github.ref` with `cancel-in-progress` for everything except `refs/heads/main`. Merge-queue refs are `refs/heads/gh-readonly-queue/main/pr-N-<sha>` — unique per entry, so cancellation is a no-op in practice, but the reasoning in that comment block needs to be checked and restated rather than assumed.
7. **`nx affected` base resolution inside the queue.** `nrwl/nx-set-shas` derives `NX_BASE` from the last successful run on the default branch. Its behavior on a `merge_group` event must be confirmed empirically, not assumed — a wrong base means the queue build silently checks *less* than the PR build did, which is a green-but-untested failure mode this repo has explicitly designed against elsewhere (`changes` job fails closed, partitioner self-validates).
8. **The `changes` doc-only gate already handles it.** `continuous-integration.yml:124` short-circuits every non-`pull_request` event to `run/deps/graph=true`, so merge-group entries always run the full build. Verify, don't change.

## Scope

In: queue configuration on `main`, `merge_group` correctness of the CI workflow, required-check hygiene across the other workflows, an end-to-end live validation, docs, and the agent-workflow changes in trap 3/4.

Out: adopting Nx Cloud DTE (unrelated, still not adopted — `docs/monorepo/NX.md`), changing the sharding factor, and enabling any currently cost-gated workflow.

## Definition of done

A PR merged through the queue on `main`; a `merge_group` CI run visible in Actions and reporting `ci-success`; conventional-commit title and `Plan-Id:`/`Task-Id:` footers intact on the resulting `main` commit; a documented rollback; and `docs/monorepo/NX.md` no longer claiming the trigger is inert.
Turn on a GitHub merge queue for `main` and make `.github/workflows/continuous-integration.yml` a correct, trustworthy `merge_group` gate — including the agent workflows (auto-merge, work-ledger SHA capture) that change shape once merges stop being instantaneous.

## Goal

Stand up a library of high-impact **recurring** agent jobs that continuously improve this monorepo without a human driving each run. Deliverable is 10 prompt files in `.agents/prompts/`, each runnable standalone via OT Loop `--prompt-file` (layer-1 prompt delivery) or an OT scheduled job.

## Decisions (locked)

1. **Output contract = OT plan + tasks.** Every job is *read-only on source code*. It never edits, fixes, or refactors. Its single side effect is creating one OpenThrottle plan (with prioritized, self-contained tasks) via the `openthrottle-mcp` MCP — the same posture as the `improve` skill. Nothing merges without a human starting that plan.
2. **Fully self-contained prompts.** No shared preamble file, no new skill. Each prompt repeats the shared rules so it works alone when passed to any agent CLI via `--prompt-file`. ## Conventions

- Location: `.agents/prompts/` (flat, SSOT; ingested into `custom_prompts` by `packages/openthrottle-skills`).
