Editor integration settings: design + layout refresh
## Why

`applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routing/settings/components/SettingsWorkspaceEditorsForm.tsx` has all the right *information* and none of the right *shape*. One entity — an editor — is fragmented across three stacked blocks that each re-enumerate the same three editors:

1. `WorkspaceEditorMultiSelect` — a combobox dropdown for a fixed set of **three** options. The user must open a popover to discover what OpenThrottle even supports.
2. `WorkspaceEditorPresenceHints` — a separate "On this machine" bullet list restating those editors with a detected/not-detected line.
3. `WorkspaceEditorAffiliateLinks` — a third block of "Don't have Cursor yet?" paragraphs, again per editor.

So "is Cursor on? is it installed? where do I get it?" requires reading three disjoint lists and mentally joining them. The fix is a join in the UI: **one row (card) per editor**, carrying its toggle, its presence badge, and its acquisition link together.

Secondary gaps worth closing in the same pass:

- `editorPresence.scannedAt` and `editorPresence.trusted` are fetched by the loader and thrown away. `trusted` is the signal that separates "we probed the host and did not find it" from "we are guessing"; it should be visible, quietly.
- The Save button is always enabled, even with zero changes, and there is no dirty indicator.
- `WORKSPACE_EDITOR_OPTIONS` carries only `{ label, value }` — no icon, no one-line description, no docs link — so every surface that renders an editor invents its own presentation.

## Invariants that must survive (non-negotiable)

- **Presence never gates.** A `NOT_FOUND` editor must still be enableable and still submit; the save button must never disable because of detection. This is the whole point of commit f27d2c55 and is asserted by an existing test.
- **`UNKNOWN` renders no claim.** A containerized server cannot see the user's filesystem; silence stays the correct output.
- **A failed presence probe is invisible.** The loader already `.catch(() => null)`s it; the redesigned form must degrade to "no badges", never to a broken layout or an error.
- The form still posts `intent=updateProfile` with `worktreeRoot`, `contactDisplayName`, `contactEmail` hidden alongside `enabledEditors[]`, because the shared action tolerates no partial payload.
- The single FTC affiliate disclosure stays exactly one, page-level — not repeated per card.

## Target shape

A responsive grid (1 col mobile / 2–3 col at `md`) of editor cards inside the existing `OpenThrottleFieldset`. Each card:

- editor mark + label ("Claude Code", "Cursor", "Visual Studio Code")
- a one-line description of what OpenThrottle writes for it
- a presence `Badge` — `Detected` (success-ish) / `Not detected` (muted) / nothing at all for `UNKNOWN` or a failed probe
- a `Switch` for enablement, with the card itself selectable (whole-card click target, selected state via ring/border, `aria-pressed` semantics or a real label-wrapped switch)
- a "Get Cursor" affiliate link inline, shown when an affiliate URL exists — most valuable precisely on a not-detected card

Below the grid: the FTC disclosure, the `scannedAt`/`trusted` footnote, the action error, and a dirty-aware Save.

## Available primitives (use these, do not hand-roll)

`packages/react-router-shadcn`: `Badge`, `Card` (+ `CardHeader`/`CardContent`/`CardFooter`), `Switch`, `Tooltip`, `Separator`, `Label`, `Button`, `Empty`, `InlineErrors`. `packages/react-router-ui`: `OpenThrottleFieldset` (keep it — it is the section chrome for the whole settings page).

## Constraints

- Generators first: `NX_ISOLATE_PLUGINS=false pnpm nx g @tools/generators:react-router --subGenerator=component --application=openthrottle-developer --folder=app/routing/settings/components --name=...`. Keep the generated section comments, even empty.
- One component per file; lists/copy live in `routing/settings/data/data.copy.ts`, editor metadata in `routing/settings/config/workspace-editors.ts`.
- No `as` casts, no enums, `import type` for types, explicit return types, alphabetized props/keys.
- Tests use `component` (not `screen`) and `userEvent`.
- Component line cap is checked **after** prettier runs.

## Validation

`pnpm nx run openthrottle-developer:typecheck`, `:lint`, `:test`, `:build`, then a live visual pass at `/settings/workspace` against the built server with the seeded `developer-e1e878@atlasworks.example` user (that user has admin; a fresh user has zero perms and cannot reach the page).
Rebuild SettingsWorkspaceEditorsForm from a dropdown + three stacked footnote blocks into one per-editor card grid that carries selection, presence, and the affiliate CTA on the same row.

Rich per-run metadata for scheduled agent jobs: model, settings, token usage & cost
## Goal

Each scheduled-agent-job RUN should record and display richer execution metadata than it does today. On the run detail route (`applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routes/scheduled-jobs.$jobId._index.tsx` and the per-run `RunDetail.tsx`) we want to see, per run:

- **Model** — already stored on the run row, just needs surfacing more prominently.
- **Settings snapshot** — the effective run settings at execution time (driver, model, reasoning tier, permission mode, any run-config), captured on the run row so later edits to the schedule don't rewrite history.
- **Token usage** — input / output / cache-read / cache-write / reasoning / total tokens.
- **Estimated cost** — costUsd for the run.

## Current state (from codebase audit)

- **Table:** `scheduled_agent_job_runs` (`databases/migrations/082_create_scheduled_agent_jobs.sql:57-93`). Has `driver_id`, `model`, `status`, `exit_code`, `error_message`, timestamps. **No** settings snapshot, token, or cost columns.
- **Entity:** `packages/nestjs-repositories/src/modules/scheduled-agent-jobs/scheduled-agent-job-run.entity.ts`.
- **GraphQL:** `ScheduledAgentJobRunObject` (`applications/openthrottle-server/src/graphql/scheduled-agent-jobs/scheduled-agent-job.object.ts:90-146`), mapper `scheduled-agent-jobs.mapper.ts:36-52` (`toScheduledAgentJobRunObject`), resolver `scheduled-agent-jobs.resolver.ts` (`scheduledAgentJobRuns`, `scheduledAgentJobRun`).
- **Execution path:** processor `applications/openthrottle-server/src/queues/scheduled-agent-jobs/scheduled-agent-jobs.processor.ts` (`process()` 106-183, `claimOrCreateRun()` 189-216); persistence `packages/nestjs-repositories/src/modules/scheduled-agent-jobs/scheduled-agent-jobs.service.ts` (`createRun` 159-171, `markRunStarted`, `markRunFinished` 199-212).
- **Design gap:** `runAgentPrompt` (`packages/openthrottle-drivers/src/run-agent-prompt/index.ts:90-96`) returns only `{ driverId, exitCode, model, output, status }`; `DriverChunk` carries raw text only. Structured usage is NOT threaded through the scheduled-job path today — it must be parsed from the buffered raw `output`.

## Reuse (do NOT reinvent)

- **Normalizer:** `packages/agentic-token-usage/src/usage.ts` — `normalizeUsage`, `sumUsage`, `hasUsageCounts`, `formatTokenCount`, `formatUsageCost`, type `NormalizedTokenUsage`. Handles claude/cursor/codex/grok/opencode/openai shapes and tolerates partial input.
- **Persistence pattern:** `agent_token_usage` table (migration 083) + `agent-token-usage.service.ts` (`recordTurnUsage`). Mirror its column shape on the run row.
- **Server wiring reference:** `conversation-stream.service.ts` `persistTurnUsage()` (547-581) — filters usage events, folds via `sumUsage(acc, normalizeUsage(...))`, gates on `hasUsageCounts`, persists. Imitate this in the processor.
- **GraphQL usage models to copy:** `applications/openthrottle-server/src/graphql/token-usage/`.

## Approach

Store the usage counts + costUsd + a `raw_usage` jsonb + a `settings_snapshot` jsonb directly on the run row (denormalized, run-scoped) rather than joining to `agent_token_usage` — scheduled runs aren't conversation/message scoped. Parse usage from the buffered CLI `output` in the processor after `runAgentPrompt` returns, reusing the normalizer.

## Out of scope

- Cross-run aggregation / cost dashboards (belongs with OT a55b76ba Usage-route work; can follow later).
- Enriching the driver `onChunk` pipeline to emit structured usage events (bigger refactor; parse-from-output is the pragmatic v1).

## Validation

`pnpm nx run openthrottle-server:dev` to regen `schema.gql`; `pnpm nx affected --target=codegen-graphql,codegen-react-router --parallel`; `pnpm nx affected --target=lint,typecheck,test`. Commit schema.gql + all `__generated__`.

Onboarding-in-a-modal: surface the FeatureOnboarding pitch via a modal=onboarding GlobalFeatureOnboardingModal when lists are populated
## Why

Builds directly on **f599b238** (onboarding empty-states). Today the rich `GlobalFeatureOnboarding` "teach-me-fast" block only renders when a list is **empty AND unfiltered** (`isNewUser`). Once a user has any Rules / Schedule jobs / Plans, that onboarding content vanishes — there's no way to re-read "what is this, what's it for, how do we use it."

We want the **same onboarding content** to remain reachable when the list is populated, surfaced inside a `GlobalFeatureOnboardingModal` built on our base modal (`GlobalModal` → shadcn `Dialog`), driven consistently by `?modal=onboarding` across all three routes. A single copy object per feature drives BOTH the inline empty-state block AND the modal — no duplicated copy.

## Current state (verified 2026-08-15, on branch openthrottle/loop-plan-onboarding-empty-states)

- `packages/react-router-ui-global/src/components/GlobalFeatureOnboarding.tsx` — presentational `Card` block. Props: `{ className?, content: GlobalFeatureOnboardingContent }`. Renders eyebrow/icon + title + tagline, "What it is", "How we use it internally", "What you could use it for", numbered "Quick start", and CTA(s). Exported from the package barrel along with the `GlobalFeatureOnboardingContent` / `GlobalFeatureOnboardingLink` types and `GLOBAL_FEATURE_ONBOARDING_SECTION_COPY`.
- `GlobalModal.tsx` — thin wrapper over shadcn `Dialog`/`DialogContent`, open-state bound to a URL search param via `useUrlSyncedOverlay({ param, openValue })`. `DialogContent` is already `max-w-5xl max-h-svh overflow-y-auto`.
- `GlobalMetricsInfoModal.tsx` + `GlobalMetricsInfoTrigger.tsx` — the reference pattern: a trigger sets `modal=<KEY>` (URL is the single source of truth; trigger and dialog share no React state), a modal wraps `GlobalModal`. Both hang a `.key` off the component.
- `useUrlSyncedOverlay.tsx` — hook returning `{ open, onOpenChange, setOpen }`; `setOpen(true)` sets the param preserving others, close deletes it. Scroll-preserving by default.
- Routes render onboarding inline gated on `isNewUser` (empty && !filtered): `rules._index.tsx`, `plans._index.tsx`, `schedule._index.tsx`. Header components: `RulesIntroduction`, `PlansIntroduction`, `ScheduleIntroduction` (Schedule's was added in f599b238). Copy objects: `RULES_ONBOARDING`, `PLANS_ONBOARDING`(via plans `data.copy.ts`), schedule `data.copy.ts` onboarding const.

## Design decisions (locked)

1. **One shared modal param value: `modal=onboarding`**, identical across Rules / Schedule / Plans. Each page renders at most one onboarding modal, so the value is unambiguous per-page and consistent across the app. Export a single `GLOBAL_FEATURE_ONBOARDING_MODAL` constant (`{ param: 'modal', value: 'onboarding' }`) from the package and use it in both the modal and the trigger — no stringly-typed drift.
2. **New primitive `GlobalFeatureOnboardingModal`** in `react-router-ui-global`: `props { content: GlobalFeatureOnboardingContent; className? }`. Internally `<GlobalModal param="modal" value="onboarding">` wrapping the onboarding content. Hang `.key = 'onboarding'` off it, matching the existing convention.
3. **Dialog-aware rendering, single-sourced markup.** Add ONE optional prop to `GlobalFeatureOnboarding`: `renderAs?: 'block' | 'dialog'` (default `'block'`, preserving today's behavior). In `'dialog'` mode it (a) drops the outer `Card`/`CardContent` chrome (the `Dialog` surface is already the card), and (b) renders its title/tagline row using shadcn `DialogTitle`/`DialogDescription` so Radix's required-accessible-title invariant is satisfied without duplicating a header. All body sections + CTAs stay identical. This keeps the teaching markup in ONE component; the modal is a thin shell.
4. **New primitive `GlobalFeatureOnboardingTrigger`** (mirrors `GlobalMetricsInfoTrigger`): a labeled button (default label e.g. "How it works" — expose a `label?` prop, default from package copy) that calls `setOpen(true)` on `modal=onboarding`. URL is the source of truth; trigger and modal need no shared state.
5. **Wiring per route.** Each route renders `<GlobalFeatureOnboardingModal content={X_ONBOARDING} />` unconditionally (cheap; only mounts a Dialog that's closed unless the param is set), and each `Introduction` header renders a `GlobalFeatureOnboardingTrigger`. The existing inline `isNewUser` block is unchanged. Net effect: empty+unfiltered → inline pitch (as today); populated/filtered → same pitch on demand via the header trigger + `?modal=onboarding`.
6. **No GraphQL / schema / codegen** changes. Purely presentational + URL state.

## Out of scope

- Auto-opening the modal on first visit, or any "seen it" persistence/preference. v1 is trigger-driven only.
- Fanning the trigger+modal out to routes beyond Rules / Schedule / Plans (Prompts, Queues, Personas, …) — a follow-up, same as f599b238's rollout follow-up.
- Restyling the underlying `GlobalModal` / base Dialog.

## Validation

- `pnpm nx run openthrottle-developer:lint,typecheck,test` green; `pnpm nx run react-router-ui-global:lint,typecheck,test` green.
- Package unit tests: `GlobalFeatureOnboarding renderAs="dialog"` emits an accessible `DialogTitle` and no `Card`; `GlobalFeatureOnboardingModal` renders its content only when `?modal=onboarding`; trigger sets the param.
- Route render tests: with a populated list the header trigger is present and `?modal=onboarding` reveals the onboarding content (assert on a stable test-id + CTA href); the inline empty-state path still works when empty+unfiltered.

Whole-take narration with word timestamps (Fish Audio stream-with-timestamp)
## Why

`packages/openthrottle-showroom/src/narrate/narrate.ts` renders **one TTS request per sentence**, concatenates the clips, measures loudness once across the take, and applies that single gain to every clip. Per-sentence was chosen so a re-record of one line does not invalidate a whole take, and `narrate/render-cache.ts` later exploited it so a one-word edit only re-buys the sentences that changed.

The cost of that choice is tonal: the model never sees more than one sentence, so it has no run-on context, no paragraph-level arc, and it re-picks pitch and pace at every full stop. NARRATION.md's own bake-off measured loudness range (LRA) as the proxy for prosody — that is exactly the axis a whole-take render should move.

Fish Audio's `POST https://api.fish.audio/v1/tts/stream/with-timestamp` returns an SSE stream where each event carries `audio_base64`, `content`, `chunk_seq`, `chunk_audio_offset_sec`, and an `alignment` object with **word-level** `segments` (`text`, `start`, `end`, relative to chunk start) plus `audio_duration`. That is the missing piece: with word timings we no longer need one file per sentence to know where each sentence starts — we can render one take and slice it.

The premise this plan takes as given: caching is nice, but at Fish's pricing (~$15/M UTF-8 bytes; a full 24-script Season 1 pass ≈ $0.17) the savings are noise, while consistent tone across a take is the thing that actually shows up in the video.

## Settled before the work starts

These are decisions, not open questions:

- **Fish Audio is the default backend.** Done in task 0 — `narrate.ts` defaults to `fish-audio`, and NARRATION.md, `docs/marketing/pipeline.md`, `publishing.md` and `catalogue-rebuild.md` say so. Piper is the on-box path (`--backend piper`), required for any text not going into a published episode. macOS `say` stays a rehearsal backend.
- **ElevenLabs is out of scope.** `backends/elevenlabs.ts` is left exactly as it is — no `renderTake`, no comparison renders, no edits beyond a stale comment already corrected. It won the 2026-08 listen and was not adopted; Fish won on cost, pay-as-you-go billing, open-weight escape hatch, and having a word-timestamp endpoint at all.
- **The currently pinned Fish voice is the voice.** `DEFAULT_FISH_AUDIO_VOICE` in `backends/fish-audio.ts`. A swap is expected within days, so no task may hardcode or assume the id — read the constant, and let every take keep recording the voice it used.
- **Season 1 is unshipped, so Season 1 is the testing ground.** The old "frozen on Piper, repinning means re-rendering everything published" rule protected published episodes; nothing is published. It starts applying at publication. Until then the plan iterates on the real 24 scripts, and re-rendering the season is a ~$0.17 pass.

## What changes

- `TtsBackend` gains an **optional** whole-take capability alongside `render`. Backends that do not implement it (Piper, macOS `say`, ElevenLabs) keep the per-sentence path untouched.
- Fish Audio implements it against the with-timestamp endpoint.
- Word timings are mapped back onto sentence boundaries, and the take is sliced into the same `NNN-<beat>.wav` files with the same `timings.json` shape, so `assemble/timeline.ts` and `assemble/captions.ts` are unchanged.
- The loudness rule from NARRATION.md gets simpler on this path, not different: one measurement per take, one gain — the take already exists as a single file, so measure it, apply the gain, then slice.
- The render cache moves to take granularity rather than being deleted.

## What must not change

- `timings.json` shape and the per-sentence `.wav` file layout; downstream stages are not rewritten for this.
- `backends/elevenlabs.ts`.
- Captions keep using the **written** form, not the spoken (lexicon-substituted) form.
- The privacy line, now that the default path is off box: hosted backends render script text intended for publication. Season 1 narration is written to be published, so it qualifies. Drafts, experiments and anything not going into an episode render through `--backend piper`, explicitly.

## The unknown worth answering first

Fish's `chunk_length` (100–300 chars, default 300) means the service internally re-chunks long text. If prosody resets at those seams, the tonal win is smaller than the hypothesis assumes and `chunk_length` becomes a tuning knob rather than a detail. Listen at a seam on a >300-character take before building the slicing logic.
Rolled up into plan 02393bbe-e62f-4749-8eda-402f27bca1ad on 2026-11-21 (narration tasks at sortOrder 13000–21000). Work it there, not here. Task 0 (Fish default backend) stays COMPLETED here as history.

**Data model** — `tag_action_rules` (migration 065, +072 title) is user-owned and carries a scope ladder: `project_id` (reserved, see above), `environment` (NULL = all; `ci|interactive|plan-run`), `status` (NULL = any plan status), `tag_all` (AND semantics over the plan's effective tag set). Guarantee all six .demo-workstation.local fields on every setup
## Problem

After nuking the repo, Docker images, and volumes and re-running `./scripts/setup.sh` on a second machine, the generated `.demo-workstation.local` was missing `OPENTHROTTLE_MCP_AUTH_TOKEN`. The file must ALWAYS contain all six fields:

- `OPENTHROTTLE_ADMIN_URL`
- `OPENTHROTTLE_BOOTSTRAP_USER_EMAIL`
- `OPENTHROTTLE_BOOTSTRAP_USER_PASSWORD`
- `OPENTHROTTLE_DEVELOPER_URL`
- `OPENTHROTTLE_MCP_AUTH_TOKEN`
- `OPENTHROTTLE_WORKER_GRAPHQL_AUTH_TOKEN`

## Root cause

The six fields come from two bootstrap scripts writing the same git-ignored file via `scripts/local-secrets-file.ts` `upsertLocalSecrets`:

- `scripts/bootstrap-default-user.ts` writes the 4 non-token fields **unconditionally** (lines 128-133) — these always appear.
- `scripts/bootstrap-service-account-credentials.ts` writes the 2 token fields **only in the mint-and-print branch** (`mintBootstrapCredential`, `upsertLocalSecrets` at line 148). It does NOT write the file in the other two `provisionAccount` branches:
  - **Skip branch** (`mintBootstrapCredential`, `activeCount > 0`, lines 119-129): service account already has an active credential -> returns `skipped`, no file write. Because only a bcrypt hash is stored, the plaintext token cannot be re-derived, so the file legitimately cannot be repopulated with the existing value.
  - **Env-provided branch** (`upsertBootstrapCredentialFromEnv`): when `OPENTHROTTLE_MCP_AUTH_TOKEN` / `OPENTHROTTLE_WORKER_GRAPHQL_AUTH_TOKEN` is already set in the environment, the credential is upserted from that env value but the file is never written.

The observed asymmetry (worker token present, MCP token absent) means on the affected box the `openthrottle-mcp` service account already had an active credential when setup ran (Postgres named volume survived a `docker compose down` without `-v`, OR `database:bootstrap-service-accounts` ran twice — e.g. once during an earlier `server:dev` boot and once from `setup.sh`, OR `OPENTHROTTLE_MCP_AUTH_TOKEN` was set in `.env` from the Cursor MCP config), so it hit a non-mint path while `plan-runner` was freshly minted.

## Goal

Make bootstrap self-healing so `.demo-workstation.local` ends up with all six keys after `./scripts/setup.sh`, regardless of which `provisionAccount` branch each account takes — plus a loud final invariant that fails setup if any field is missing, and a documented recovery path for the box that is broken right now.

## Design decisions to lock before implementing

1. **Skip branch recovery.** When the env var is unset AND the target key is absent from `.demo-workstation.local` but an active credential already exists, the old plaintext is unrecoverable. Preferred fix: treat this as "need a usable token" and self-heal by rotating (revoke existing active credential(s) + mint a fresh one), then write the new value to the file. This is safe for local bootstrap accounts. Confirm rotate-vs-warn with the owner before implementing.
2. **Env-provided branch.** When the token comes from the environment, that plaintext IS known, so write it into the file so the durable copy stays complete.
3. **Final invariant.** Add a verification step (either at the tail of the service-account script or a small standalone check wired into `setup.sh`) that asserts all six keys are present and non-empty, failing loudly with remediation guidance otherwise.

## References

- `scripts/bootstrap-service-account-credentials.ts`
- `scripts/bootstrap-default-user.ts`
- `scripts/local-secrets-file.ts`
- `scripts/setup.sh` (steps 4 and 4b)
- `scripts/verify-openthrottle-mcp-env.sh`, `AUTH.md` runbook (from the stale-in-session OT MCP plan)

Editor presence detection: hint which editors are installed, never gate on it
## Why

`/settings/workspace` offers Claude Code, Cursor and VS Code with no signal about which are actually installed. Enabling one you do not have produces a button whose deep link silently does nothing when clicked — the OS has no handler for the scheme. Observed live: VS Code enabled on a machine without it.

There is **no browser-side way** to detect this, and that is deliberate on the browsers' part:
- `navigator.registerProtocolHandler` registers, it cannot query.
- `getInstalledRelatedApps()` is Chrome-only and scoped to PWAs tied to your own origin.
- Navigate-and-detect-blur is unreliable and fires an OS prompt regardless.

Scheme-handler enumeration is a fingerprinting vector, so no engine exposes it. Detection therefore has to happen **server-side**, and OT already has that pattern.

## The hard constraint: this is a HINT, never a gate

The server is not guaranteed to be running on the user's machine. `WorkspaceEditorConfigService` already handles this via `toContainerPath`, which is identity when the bridge env (`OPENTHROTTLE_HOST` / `CONTAINER_WORKSPACES_DIR`) is unset — i.e. every host-run flow — and translates when the server runs in a container. **A containerized server probing its own filesystem would confidently report "VS Code not installed" about a Mac it cannot see.**

So the result is **three-state, not boolean**:

| State | Meaning | UI |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `installed` | probe found it | quiet confirmation |
| `not_found` | probe ran on the host and found nothing | advisory "we couldn't find this" |
| `unknown` | probe could not be trusted (containerized, unsupported OS, probe error) | say nothing at all |

**Detection must never auto-disable, auto-enable, or block saving an editor.** Stored `enabledEditors` stays authoritative. A user on a container-backed server, or one whose editor lives somewhere unusual, must still be able to turn an editor on and have it work. Collapsing `unknown` into `not_found` and greying out the checkbox would break exactly those users — do not do it.

## Editors are NOT the agent CLIs (do not conflate)

Tempting shortcut, wrong answer: reuse `discoverAgentClis`. The drivers registry's `cursor` is `cursor-agent` (the CLI) and `claude` is `claude-code` (the CLI) — **not** the Cursor and Claude Code desktop apps that register `cursor://` and `claude://`. Someone can have the CLI without the app, or the reverse. Editor detection needs its own probe table keyed by `WorkspaceEditorId`, even though it borrows discovery's machinery.

## `code` in PATH under-detects (the macOS trap)

Probing for a `code` binary is the obvious approach and it is wrong on macOS: VS Code ships the `code` shell command **opt-in** ("Shell Command: Install 'code' command in PATH"), so a large fraction of real installs have the app and no CLI. A PATH-only probe reports `not_found` for a working editor — worse than no detection, because it is confidently wrong.

Detection is therefore per-platform:
- **macOS** — look for the `.app` bundle (`/Applications/…`, `~/Applications/…`); consider `mdfind`/Launch Services for non-standard locations. Bundle ids, not binary names.
- **Linux** — `.desktop` entries and/or PATH.
- **Windows** — registry / known install paths.

Ship whichever platforms are actually supported and return `unknown` for the rest. **Never guess.** That is the same rule the plan-toolbar deep links landed on: a confidently wrong answer beats no answer only in the sense that it is worse.

## Reuse, do not rebuild

`AgentDiscoveryService` is the template and is already solved for the expensive-probe problem: `StaleWhileRevalidateCache`, a soft TTL (`AGENT_DISCOVERY_CACHE_TTL_MS`, default 60s) serving fresh, a hard TTL (default 600s) past which a call blocks rather than serve indefinitely-stale data, and a single coalesced background refresh. Filesystem probes are cheaper than the 3–5s CLI spawns, but they still should not run per page load. Mirror the knobs and naming.

Security: probe an **allowlist only**, derived from the editor vocabulary. Never spawn or stat a caller-supplied path.

## Relationship to plan 4d6bdf92

This adds a per-editor detection table — another exhaustive `Record<WorkspaceEditorId, …>`. It must be built on whatever [[exhaustive-vocabularies]] settles, not as a fourth hand-maintained editor list. If 4d6bdf92 has not landed, still express the table as an exhaustive Record so it fails typecheck when an editor is added.

## Out of scope

- Installing editors from the UI (agent CLIs have `installEnabled`; editors are GUI apps, different problem).
- Detecting editor *versions* or capabilities.

Surface in-progress worktrees on /settings/repositories from the configured worktree root
## Problem

`/settings/repositories` renders a two-level tree (`buildRepositoryRows`, `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routing/settings/repositories/utils/rows.ts`): a repository's `kind='primary'` checkout is a parent row and its `kind='worktree'` checkouts hang off it as children. Those child rows only exist when a `repository_checkouts` row exists, and today that happens in exactly two places:

- `PlanRunWorktreeCheckoutService` -> `RepositoryCheckoutsService.upsertWorktreeCheckout` (server-provisioned plan runs), and
- `workspace-folders.service.ts:557`, when a user explicitly adds a folder whose inspection says `git.isLinkedWorktree`.

So every worktree created outside the server — `pnpm run worktree:new <name>` run by hand, by a Claude/Cursor session, or by the ot-claude-loop — is invisible on the page even though it is the worktree the user is actively working in.

Migration 097 added `user_workspace_settings.worktree_root`: "the one directory every agent creates git worktrees under", already surfaced on `/settings/workspace` (`SettingsWorkspaceWorktreeRootForm`) and already forwarded to `scripts/create_worktree.sh` as `OT_WORKTREE_ROOT` by `PlanRunWorktreeProvisionService`. That gives us a reliable place to look, so the page can show what is actually on disk.

## Goal

`/settings/repositories` shows every worktree that exists on disk for the user's repositories, whether or not OpenThrottle created it, with an honest activity signal, and lets the user register one with a single action. Read-only with respect to git: v1 never creates, prunes, or deletes a worktree.

## Design decisions (settled — implement these, don't re-litigate)

**1. Two discovery sources, unioned and deduped by resolved real path.**

- *Per-repository, authoritative:* `git worktree list --porcelain` from each registered primary checkout. The parser already exists (`RepositoryInspectionService.parseLinkedWorktrees`, surfaced as `inspection.git.linkedWorktrees`) but that snapshot is a cache keyed on `scannedAt` and goes stale; discovery must run live rather than read the cached snapshot.
- *Root scan, catches the rest:* shallow (depth 1) scan of the resolved worktree root for immediate child directories whose `.git` is a **file** pointer (the `isLinkedWorktree` test the inspection service already uses). For each hit, `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` resolves the owning repository so it can be attached to the right parent row — this is what catches worktrees whose base checkout is not registered, or whose primary lives outside the workspace roots.

Dedupe on `realpathSync` so a symlinked root and a direct path are one row, matching how `browseDirectory` already resolves roots.

**2. Root resolution is a single shared ladder.** `scripts/create_worktree.sh` resolves the root as: `OT_WORKTREE_ROOT` env -> `OT_WORKTREE_ROOT` in the primary checkout's `.env` -> sibling `openthrottle-worktrees` directory. The settings value feeds rung 1 via the provisioning service. Extract that ladder (settings value included) into ONE resolver consumed by both `PlanRunWorktreeProvisionService` and the new discovery service, so the page can never disagree with where the script actually writes. Any divergence here is the bug this plan is most likely to introduce.

**3. "In progress" is defined, never inferred from a directory existing.** Each discovered worktree gets one activity state:

- `RUNNING` — an `IN_PROGRESS` `plan_runs` row whose `checkout_id` resolves to this path *and* whose `heartbeat_at` is inside the staleness cutoff (the liveness contract from the heartbeat/staleness work — a stale IN_PROGRESS row is dead, not running).
- `DIRTY` — no live run, but `git status --porcelain` is non-empty or the branch is ahead of its upstream/base.
- `IDLE` — clean, no live run.

A worktree with no `repository_checkouts` row is additionally flagged `unregistered`; that flag is orthogonal to activity (an unregistered worktree can be DIRTY).

**4. Bounded and non-fatal.** Depth-1 scan only; per-path `git` calls get an explicit timeout and `maxBuffer`; a hard cap on discovered worktrees with the overflow reported rather than silently truncated; every failure becomes a warning on the payload (the pattern `RepositoryInspectionService` already uses), never a thrown resolver error. Discovery must not be able to make the page hang or 500 — if the root is missing or unreadable, the table renders exactly as it does today plus a warning.

**5. Path containment.** `browseDirectory` refuses paths outside the configured workspace roots. The worktree root is frequently a sibling *outside* those roots, so discovery is allowed to read the resolved root — but only the resolved root, never a client-supplied path. No new user-controlled path parameter is introduced.

**6. Scope.** In: discovery, activity classification, GraphQL surface, table rows/badges, "register this worktree" via the existing `addWorkspaceFolder` mutation, refresh, docs. Out: creating a worktree from the UI, `git worktree prune`, deleting a worktree directory (destructive — separate plan), and any change to how runs pick their worktree.

## Verification

Unit tests at every layer (mocked `execFile`/`fs` for discovery, fixture rows for the UI). Live browser verification of authed settings pages is blocked in this workspace (fresh users have zero permissions and login needs a password), so the UI gate is render-level Vitest on the table plus a `check:local`-parity run, not a Playwright pass.
Discover git worktrees from the workspace worktree_root (migration 097) plus `git worktree list`, classify each as running/dirty/idle, and show them as children in the /settings/repositories table — including ones OpenThrottle never provisioned.

Pre-Hooks props unpack: agent rule + ESLint
Capture and enforce a Component body convention that agents currently miss: unpack `props` (and anything taken from those bindings) at the top of the function, before `// Hooks`. Derived/narrowed values stay under `// Setup`. This is **one abstract contract** that both authored components (`FooProps`) and route default Components (`Route.ComponentProps`) must persist — not two one-off rules.

## Why this exists

Exemplar (already applied locally, not yet the house rule):

`applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routes/settings.repositories.$repositoryId._index.tsx` and `settings.repositories._index.tsx`.

Before: `const { loaderData } = props` and `const { repository } = loaderData` sat after `// 🔌 Short Circuit`, immediately above `return`. After: those identity unpacks sit between the signature and `// Hooks`. On the list route, `'error' in actionData` narrowing stayed in `// Setup` — that split is the rule.

The same split applies to authored components: `const { className, repository } = props` (and `const { id, name } = repository` when `repository` came from props) belongs in the pre-Hooks block; a formatted label or `'x' in y` narrowing belongs in `// Setup`. Route.ComponentProps is just a specific props shape (`loaderData` / `actionData` / `params` / `matches`), not a different convention.

The written contract already hints at the first line only:

- Component R3 (`docs/monorepo/component-primitive-shape.md`): optional `const { … } = props` between the signature and `// Hooks`.
- Route R2 (`docs/monorepo/route-primitive-shape.md`): same sentence for the default Component — currently a fork of that sentence, not a pointer.
- Route generator already emits `const { actionData: _a, loaderData: _l, matches: _m, params: _p } = props;` in that slot.
- Component generator currently comments out `// const {  } = props` and binds `_props`.

Gaps:

1. Nested unpack (`const { repository } = loaderData` or `const { id } = item` from a prop) is unspecified, so agents treat it as Setup or dump it with the return.
2. Unpack vs derive is unspecified — identity destructure vs `'x' in y` / mapping / formatting.
3. ESLint `openthrottle/component-primitive-shape` and `openthrottle/route-primitive-shape` only check marker presence, order, and blank lines. They do not look at statement placement. The after-Short-Circuit dump is the common anti-pattern (still in `settings.workspace._index.tsx`, `settings.repositories.$repositoryId.edit.tsx`, `settings.rollout.$flagId.edit.tsx`, and many others).
4. Agent rules (`.agents/rules/coding/frontend-design-openthrottle.mdc` and siblings) mention the six markers but not the pre-Hooks unpack block, so agents will keep writing the anti-pattern even after docs change unless the rule files say it.
5. The two ESLint files already duplicate `MARKERS` / `checkMarkers`. A third copy of unpack logic would drift; the checker must be shared.

## The convention (normative, one idea)

Inside **any** render function that follows the six-marker shape (authored component or route default `Component`):

1. **Pre-Hooks unpack block** (between `{` and `// Hooks`, one blank line before the marker):
   - `const { … } = props;` (unused keys prefixed `_`).
   - Immediate nested identity destructure of those bindings: `const { repository } = loaderData;`, `const { slug } = params;`, `const { id, name } = item;` when `item` came from props.
   - No derived/narrowed values here.
2. **`// Setup`**: derived values from those bindings (discriminated-union narrowing like `actionData && 'error' in actionData ? actionData.error : null`, maps, formatters).
3. **Never** place `const { … } = props` (or nested unpack from a props-derived binding) after `// Hooks`, and especially not after `// 🔌 Short Circuit`.

Hooks stay first after the unpack so Rules-of-Hooks order remains stable; Setup can then use both unpacked props and hook results.

## Architecture — pull the idea out, wire it into both

Do **not** implement a route-only check and a component-only check. The abstract rule is “identity ObjectPattern unpack of `props` and of bindings taken from `props`, before `// Hooks`." Route keys (`loaderData`, …) fall out of that walk; they are not a special case.

- **Docs:** Component R3 owns the unpack-block contract (SSOT). Route R2 says the default Component follows component R3 including that block, then shows a route-shaped example (`loaderData` → `repository`). Do not fork the rule text.
- **Agent rules:** One bullet covering both surfaces.
- **ESLint:** Extract a shared helper (e.g. `tools/dotfiles/src/rules/pre-hooks-unpack.ts`) that, given a function body + source, reports identity unpacks after the first `// Hooks` marker. Both `component-primitive-shape` and `route-primitive-shape` call it. Unit-test the helper; each RuleTester still has a valid/invalid fixture for its surface.
- **Warn-first on both rules.** Inventory routes *and* authored components. Graduate to error later, independently if the tails differ, same rollout as route-shape R4.

## Enforcement details

- Flag a `VariableDeclarator` whose init is Identifier `props`, or an ObjectPattern destructure of a binding previously taken from `props`, if it appears after the first `// Hooks` marker in the same function body.
- Do **not** flag ordinary `const` in Setup (narrowing, mapping) — only identity ObjectPattern unpack from props-derived names.
- Message should point at the pre-Hooks slot and component R3 (route reports can still link route R2, which points at R3).
- Autofix is optional and not required.
- Keep the generator as SSOT: route template already correct; component template currently comments out `const { } = props` — uncomment/normalize so template, docs, and rule cannot drift.

## Out of scope

- Mass-migrating every violating route or component in this plan (inventory + a few exemplars; bulk fix is a follow-up once warn-first is live).
- Requiring unused `_a` / `_l` / `_m` / `_p` keys — generator style, not this rule.
- Changing marker order or the Short Circuit early-return contract.
- Deduplicating the existing `MARKERS` / `checkMarkers` copies (nice-to-have, not this plan) — only the new unpack checker must be shared.

# Generic scheduled agent jobs

## Why
Every recurring agent job today requires a bespoke, code-defined queue + processor + `*-repeatable.service.ts` (there are 5 cron services). There is **no way for a user to create a scheduled agent job at runtime**: no persistence, no create-repeatable mutation (only `repeatableJobs` list + `removeRepeatableJob`), and the only agent worker (`PlansProcessor`) is hardwired to the OT Loop orchestrator + a single Cursor iteration runner.

We want a **generic** scheduled job: give it a **prompt + provider/model/settings**, pick a **cron schedule**, and it runs on BullMQ's built-in repeatable machinery — one shared queue, no new queue per job — usable with any agent framework/CLI.

## Approach (locked)
- **Runner primitive lives in `openthrottle-drivers`** — that's our choke point and most of it already exists (`ALL_DRIVERS`/`getDriver`, `AgentDriver.buildShellCommand`, `DriverInvocationConfig`, `runDriverAsync`/`runDriverSync` engine across claude/codex/cursor/grok/opencode). The design must **inventory what already exists there first** and extend/expose a single provider-agnostic "run once with {prompt, driverId, model, settings, cwd, signal, onChunk}" entrypoint rather than reinventing invocation in the server.
- **Server adds ONE generic queue + processor** (modeled on `PlansProcessor`: heartbeat, AbortSignal cancellation, output logging, stalled recovery) that decodes `{scheduleId, prompt, driverId, model, settings}` and calls the drivers entrypoint. Decoupled from OT Loop/plans.
- **BullMQ repeatable jobs** provide the scheduling (reuse `REPEATABLE_JOB_OPTIONS`; evaluate legacy `repeat` vs newer `upsertJobScheduler`). No dedicated queue per user job.

## Net-new
- Persistence for user-defined schedules (no table exists today).
- A create/update/delete/enable/run-now GraphQL surface (only list/remove repeatables exist).
- Reconciliation between persisted schedules and BullMQ schedulers.
- A generic driver-invocation worker (current one is OT Loop/Cursor-specific).
- Developer UI to author schedules (prompt + provider/model/settings + cron) and view run history/live logs.

## Design-first
Task 1 is an architecture design doc (under `docs/`) that must resolve: the drivers-package entrypoint API, the generic queue payload + naming, persistence schema (schedule + runs), legacy `repeat` vs `upsertJobScheduler`, DB↔BullMQ reconciliation, where run output/logs live (reuse `queueJobLogs`/work-ledger?), role-slicing, and the GraphQL contract. Implementation tasks follow the doc.

## Key anchor files
- `packages/openthrottle-drivers/src/{types,drivers,registry,engine}/index.ts`
- `packages/nestjs-bullmq/src/modules/nestjs-bullmq.module.ts`, `applications/openthrottle-server/src/queues/repeatable-job.options.ts`
- Reference services: `.../queues/doc-ingestion/doc-ingestion-repeatable.service.ts` (env-driven cron), `.../queues/work-ledger-sweep/work-ledger-sweep-repeatable.service.ts`
- Reference worker: `.../queues/plans/plans.processor.ts`; enqueue path `.../graphql/plans/plan-enqueue.service.ts`
- Dynamic-queue caveat: `.../graphql/queues/queues.service.ts` `createQueue` makes a producer-only queue (no processor) — a generic job needs a statically-registered processor.
Design-first feature: let users create scheduled agent jobs from a prompt + provider/model/settings that run on a cron schedule via BullMQ's built-in repeatable jobs, WITHOUT a dedicated queue per job. The provider-agnostic run-once primitive stays in openthrottle-drivers (the choke point — runDriverAsync/engine already exists); the server adds one generic queue + processor, persistence, reconciliation, GraphQL, and a developer UI.

🪝 Overlay agentic hooks into child repositories — options and direction
# Hook overlay for child repositories — direction E (plugin + spawn-time injection)

**Status:** DIRECTION SET — option **E** chosen by the owner, 2026-08-18. Implementation tasks below.

**Related plans:** `d3a30314` (foreign-workspace skill injection, DONE), `21f150c6` (`@openthrottle/agentic-hooks` package, DONE), `96bfd217` (agentic lifecycle hooks, PENDING), `d3759118` / `91679bbf` (skill usage tracking, PENDING), `60c8e0b8` (agentic-hooks bundle target dependency fix, PENDING — **blocks distribution work**).

**Docs:** `docs/monorepo/foreign-workspace-skill-injection.md`, `docs/monorepo/agent-editor-folders.md`.

---

## Problem

`@openthrottle/agentic-hooks` authors a tool-neutral core in TS and esbuild-bundles per-tool adapters into committed, self-contained `.cjs` under each tool's hook folder — five under `.claude/hooks/`, one under `.cursor/hooks/`. Those bundles are wired up by **this repo's** `.claude/settings.json` and `.cursor/hooks.json`, so they only ever fire inside the OpenThrottle monorepo.

~99% of real work happens in **child repositories** — foreign checkouts OT drives agents against, plus repos humans open directly. None of them get hooks. Skills already solved their half of this (`d3a30314`); hooks are the unsolved half.

Hard constraint from the owner: **never override or clobber a user's own hooks.**

## The key asymmetry — this is NOT the skills problem again

Skill injection was forced to materialize into the target working tree because *no* agent CLI exposes an out-of-repo skills directory (§2 of the injection decision record). Hooks are different — `claude --help` confirms:

| escape hatch | effect |
| --- | --- |
| `--settings <file-or-json>` | loads **additional** settings for the session; merges with project/user settings |
| `--plugin-dir <path>` | loads a plugin (hooks + skills + MCP) from a directory or `.zip`; repeatable |
| `--plugin-url <url>` | fetches a plugin `.zip` for that session only |
| `/plugin install` (marketplace) | durable, per-machine; hooks merge additively — Claude Code never rewrites the user's `settings.json` |

Claude Code merges hooks from user settings, project settings, local settings, and every installed plugin. They are **additive by construction** — which is why the no-clobber requirement is satisfied by *mechanism* rather than by careful merge logic.

Counterweight that killed option C: skills are one directory per skill, so collision handling is trivial. Hooks live in a **single user-owned JSON file** with no fragment-include mechanism, so anything writing into it inherits merge, restore, and corruption risk the skill materializer never had.

---

## Decision — option E

**Ship both legs against one shared artifact:**

- **Leg A — plugin.** An OpenThrottle Claude Code plugin (`.claude-plugin/plugin.json` + `hooks/hooks.json` referencing `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/*.cjs`), published to a marketplace and installed once per machine. This is the durable, human-facing path: it applies in every repo the user opens, writes nothing into their checkout, and can later carry skills and the OT MCP server too.
- **Leg B — spawn-time.** `@openthrottle/openthrottle-drivers` appends `--plugin-dir` to the Claude CLI invocation so OT-orchestrated runs never depend on the user having installed anything. Zero disk mutation in the target repo: no ledger, no teardown, no `.git/info/exclude` block.

**Unifying design:** the plugin directory is built **once**, as a first-class Nx artifact produced by the existing `bundle-hooks` pipeline. Leg A publishes that directory; leg B points `--plugin-dir` at it in place. One payload, two delivery paths, one drift gate — this is what makes E cost barely more than either leg alone.

### Rejected

- **C (extend foreign-skill-injection to hooks)** — rejected. Reuses shipped machinery but requires a managed-block merge into a user-owned `settings.json`, with restore-on-teardown and real corruption risk, to reach somewhere the CLI already offers a first-class out-of-repo flag for. May only be revisited if the capability matrix proves a non-Claude CLI has *no* out-of-repo hook config and parity becomes a v1 requirement.
- **D (server-side transcript derivation)** — not chosen as the mechanism, but retained as the **fallback for non-Claude CLIs** until they grow real hook support, and as the degraded path when no hook can run.

---

## Open questions still owned by this plan

1. **Multi-CLI capability matrix** — what hook/plugin surface codex, cursor, opencode, and grok expose, and whether any accepts out-of-repo config. E covers Claude fully; this decides what the other four get (likely D). Cursor reads `.cursor/hooks.json` in-repo and we already ship one adapter there.
2. **Child-repo scoping and privacy contract** — the hooks phone home to the OT GraphQL API. Which server, how a foreign repo is identified and scoped, behavior when no server is reachable (core is already fail-open), and the privacy default for a repo the OT operator does not own. Overlaps `91679bbf`.
3. **Scope of the overlay** — telemetry-only in v1 (just skill-usage) versus a general hook channel (`96bfd217` would add more). Telemetry-only is far easier to justify installing into someone else's repo; recommend v1 stays telemetry-only.
DIRECTION SET (owner, 2026-08-18): **option E — plugin (A) + spawn-time injection (B)**. Both legs are additive by construction, so "never clobber a user's hooks" is met by mechanism, not merge logic. Option C (extending foreign-skill-injection into the target's settings.json) is explicitly rejected. Unifying design: build the Claude plugin directory as ONE Nx artifact — A publishes it to a marketplace, B points `--plugin-dir` at it. Key precedent: unlike skills, hooks have first-class out-of-repo escape hatches (`--settings`, `--plugin-dir`, `--plugin-url`, marketplace) so nothing is ever written into a child repo.

Chat auto-scroll: only on user send and first response
## Problem

The chat message list scrolls to the bottom on *every* new message, which is jarring during streaming.

Root cause (confirmed in code): the auto-scroll effect in [`packages/react-router-chat/src/components/ChatThread.tsx:65`](packages/react-router-chat/src/components/ChatThread.tsx) has dependency array `[messages]` (line 82) and calls `endRef.current?.scrollIntoView({ behavior: 'smooth' })` on every change of the `messages` array identity. In the true-streaming path (developer + admin apps) `messagesView` returns a **new array on every stream chunk** (see `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routing/home/demo/useAgenticChatTurn.tsx` `messagesView` memo, ~lines 132-148), so the smooth scroll re-fires on every streamed token — continuous, jarring motion.

## Desired behavior

Scroll to bottom only at two moments:
1. **User sends a message** — a new `role: 'user'` message is appended.
2. **First response token of a turn** — the in-flight assistant message transitions from empty/`pending` to its first non-empty content (streaming start). Fire once per assistant turn, not on subsequent tokens.

Bonus (already partially present, keep it): if the user has scrolled up (more than `NEAR_BOTTOM_THRESHOLD_PX` = 64px from the bottom), do not yank them back — respect their scroll position for the response scroll.

## Why this is a one-file change

Every chat surface renders the single shared `ChatThread` and passes `messages` (streaming `messagesView` or non-streaming appended array): developer home (`HomeComposer`), developer header (`useHeaderChatController`), admin app parity copies, and the packaged `ChatDialog` (non-streaming `useChatTurnFetcher`, which appends the whole assistant message once on completion). The scroll decision is entirely internal to `ChatThread` via refs (`isNearBottomRef`, `hasRenderedRef`) — no props. Changing the effect logic fixes all surfaces at once.

## Design (self-contained in ChatThread — start simple)

Replace the `[messages]`-identity trigger with event detection derived from `messages`, using refs to compare against the previous render:

- **New user message:** track the last message / user-message identity; when a newly appended message has `role: 'user'`, scroll to bottom **always** and set `isNearBottomRef.current = true` (we just jumped to the bottom).
- **First assistant content:** keep a `firstResponseScrolledIdRef`. Find the latest assistant message; when it first has non-empty `body`/`events` (i.e. `pending` cleared / streaming started) **and** its `id !== firstResponseScrolledIdRef.current`, scroll (respecting `isNearBottomRef`) and record its id. Subsequent tokens grow the body but the id already matches → no re-scroll.
- **Keep** the first-paint jump (`behavior: 'auto'` on `!hasRenderedRef.current`) for bulk history hydration, the empty-thread early return, and the existing `handleScroll` near-bottom detection.

This satisfies both required scroll points and gives the "respect user scroll" bonus for free via the existing `isNearBottomRef`. It also covers the non-streaming `ChatDialog` path: user append → scroll; whole assistant message appears with content → first-response scroll fires once.

## Rejected / deferred alternative

Threading explicit `onUserSubmit` / `streamingStarted` signals down from `useAgenticChatTurn` into `ChatThread` as props. More precise but touches both apps' hooks and both surface controllers — deferred; the ref-derived approach keeps the blast radius to one component and its test.

## Key files

- `packages/react-router-chat/src/components/ChatThread.tsx` — the effect (lines 65-82) + refs (44-47) + `handleScroll` (52-60). Primary change.
- `packages/react-router-chat/src/components/__tests__/ChatThread.test.tsx` — asserts current scroll-on-change behavior (lines ~151-176); must be updated.
- `packages/react-router-chat/src/types.ts` — `ChatMessage` (`role`, `body`, `events`, `pending`) is the signal source.
- Integration check surfaces: `applications/openthrottle-developer` home + header, `applications/openthrottle-admin` parity, packaged `ChatDialog`.
Stop the chat thread from smooth-scrolling on every streamed token/array change. Scroll to bottom only when the user sends a message and when the first assistant token of a turn arrives; keep the existing near-bottom guard so a user who has scrolled up is not yanked back. Change is centralized in packages/react-router-chat ChatThread — all surfaces inherit it.

Showroom demo fixture: sanitized snapshot of the real workspace
## Why

`packages/openthrottle-showroom/src/fixtures/demo-content.ts` seeds 8 tables of hand-written fiction; the developer app reads ~30. Measured against the dev database on 2026-08-27, the gap is an order of magnitude on every surface (tasks 5194 vs 16, work ledger 4558/4087/4216 vs 0, conversations 376/121 vs 0, tags 5697+928 vs 0, …) and most episode surfaces render empty states. Episodes 07, 09, 13, 14, 16, 17, 19 and 21 cannot be recorded honestly against the current seed.

An earlier revision of this plan proposed a deterministic PRNG-generated background calibrated to the measured distributions. **That approach is dead.** Generated fiction has to imitate a real workspace; we already have a real workspace. This repo is open source and the workspace is expected to eventually be exposed publicly as a read-only "watch us build it" instance, so the content itself is not the secret — credentials, personal data and machine details are.

## Approach: export → sanitize → commit → load → verify

1. **Export** the last `n` days (default 30; ~208 plans, ~1,400 tasks measured 2026-08-27) of the real dev database by walking the FK graph (restored in migration 099) from time-windowed root tables (`plans`, `agent_conversations`, `scheduled_agent_job_runs`, `daily_stats`, `skill_usage_events`). Parents of windowed rows always come along (users, projects, repositories, tags); children come along within the window. Embedding vectors export with their rows — episode 07 works for free because the embedded text is unchanged. Output is JSONL per table in FK-topological order.
2. **Sanitize best-effort, fail loud where it counts.** A committed column manifest classifies every exported `(table, column)` as `keep | scrub | drop`; an unclassified column (i.e. any new migration) fails the export naming the table and column — schema drift breaks the export, not the take. Deny-listed tables (`mcp_connector_connections`, anything credential-adjacent) never export. A secret detector (known key shapes + high-entropy strings) stops the export on a hit rather than silently redacting. Identity scrub (emails, home paths, machine names) applies inside free text. Free text is otherwise **kept** — accepted residual risk: recordings are reviewed carefully before publishing, nothing goes live automatically.
3. **Commit** the sanitized snapshot to the package. Refreshing it is a PR, so leak review is code review, and the existing `scan/rules.ts` leak rules run over the snapshot itself in CI.
4. **Load** the snapshot idempotently into the demo database alongside the existing hand-authored hero rows (which keep their `d0d0d0d0-` ids and byte-identical content — existing flows deep-link them). Imported rows keep their real ids: a re-export is stable, and a deep link shown on camera can later match the public instance. Timestamps are rebased to the existing minute-offset-from-seed-time convention so the snapshot stays visually fresh.
5. **Verify like an E2E suite.** Each episode declares `dataRequirements` asserted against the freshly seeded database; a missing row names the video it breaks. The videos become a byproduct of a passing run.

## Out of scope (deliberately)

Hosted deployment of the platform and the public read-only guest instance are separate future plans. This plan must not block on them, but the column manifest and deny list built here are their first draft.

## Non-negotiables carried forward from PIPELINE.md

Demo database name contains `demo`; seed idempotent under re-run and `--reset`; every seeded run stays `COMPLETED` (stale-sweep reconciles `IN_PROGRESS` runs and changes badges between takes); output chunk timestamps strictly increasing and unique per plan.
Replace hand-written demo fiction with a time-windowed, sanitized snapshot of the real dev database, loaded deterministically for recordings and asserted per episode like an E2E suite.

Skill usage drill-down: link Top skills to /skills/$slug and surface per-skill stats
## Problem

The /usage route's "Top skills" leaderboard (`UsageSkillUsage.tsx`, heading copy `SKILL_USAGE_COPY.leaderboardHeading`) is a dead end: every row is plain text. A developer who spots a skill that is heavily used, slow, or erroring has no way to jump to that skill, and `/skills/$slug` — which today loads only the on-disk SKILL.md (`readSkillFileBySlug`) — shows no usage signal at all. Usage analysis and skill authoring are the same loop, split across two disconnected screens.

## Primary user

Human developer in the openthrottle-developer app (skill author/maintainer). Secondary: agent operator judging whether an authored skill is actually being invoked and succeeding.

## Outcome

1. Each "Top skills" row links to `/skills/$slug` when a matching on-disk skill exists.
2. `/skills/$slug` renders a new usage component with that skill's stats over the last 30 days.

## Key constraints discovered during scoping

- **Not every usage row has a detail page.** `skillName` on skill_usage events includes third-party/plugin-namespaced ids (e.g. `vercel:deploy`); `/skills/$slug` slugs come from disk discovery (`discoverRepoSkills` → frontmatter `name` or folder name) under `.agents/skills`, `.claude/skills`, `.opencode/skills`. Link ONLY names that match a discovered slug; unmatched rows stay plain text (no hopeful links into 404s). Slugs containing `:` must be `encodeURIComponent`-ed in the `to`.
- **No per-skill server query exists.** `skillUsage(start, end, scope, gitBranch, cwd)` returns whole-range aggregates. Filtering client-side would give the detail route a bySkill row but no per-skill daily series — add an optional `skillName` arg to the existing query instead of a new query.
- **`/skills/$slug` has no GraphQL today** — its `.graphql` document file is empty and the loader is filesystem-only. The `skillUsage` query is guarded by `SETTINGS_READ`; a user without that permission must still get the SKILL.md view (degrade to a notice, never a 500).
- **Load order matters.** The detail route already streams `runOptions` as a naked promise so the shell paints immediately; per-skill usage should follow the same deferred pattern.
- Recharts renders no geometry under jsdom (see `UsageSkillUsageChart`) — tests assert wrapper/markup, not ticks.

## Non-goals (v1)

- Per-skill filters (branch/cwd/scope) on the detail route — the /usage route keeps ownership of filtering.
- Range picker on the detail route; fixed 30-day window matching /usage.
- Backfilling usage for skills that no longer exist on disk.
Make the /usage "Top skills" leaderboard clickable through to /skills/$slug, and add a per-skill usage stats component on the skill detail route (same aggregates as the leaderboard, plus last-used and a 30-day series), backed by a new optional skillName filter on the skillUsage GraphQL query.

Tighten checkout selector search matching
## Problem

The chat composer's checkout/repository selector (`ChatCheckoutSelector` in `packages/react-router-chat`) is great overall, but its search is too loose: typing `visormatt` should return only the `visormatt/*` checkouts, yet the whole list — `atlasworksinc/monorepo`, `atlasworksinc/atlasworks`, `atlasworksinc/nativeapps`, `atlasworksinc/native-apps` — stays visible.

## Diagnosis

Two compounding causes, both in `packages/react-router-chat/src`:

1. **cmdk's default filter is fuzzy subsequence scoring** (`command-score`). Each `CommandItem` is matched against `value + ' ' + keywords.join(' ')`, and a query matches if its characters appear *in order anywhere* in that haystack — not as a substring.
2. **The keyword haystack is deliberately wide.** `ChatCheckoutSelectorRow` passes `keywords={checkoutSearchTerms(checkout)}` (`utils/checkout-groups.ts`), which joins label, branch, **filesystem path**, project name, host, repo name and owner. Every local checkout lives under `/home/demo/…`, so the letters of `visormatt` (v-i-s-o-r-m-a-t-t) trivially subsequence-match across e.g. `atlasworksinc … main /home/demo/Development/…` for every row.

Wide keywords are the right call (they were added precisely so owner/path/project are searchable); the fuzzy scoring on top of them is what breaks precision.

## Fix direction

Supply a custom `filter` to the `<Command>` in `ChatCheckoutSelector` (cmdk supports `filter(value, search, keywords) => number`):

- Case-insensitive **substring** matching, not subsequence scoring.
- Tokenize the query on whitespace; every token must substring-match at least one search term (AND across tokens, OR across terms).
- Keep matching against the full `checkoutSearchTerms` set so `owner`, path and project searches keep working — `visormatt` matches only rows whose owner/path/label actually contains it.
- Optionally rank: term-prefix or label matches score higher than path matches, but any non-match returns 0.
- Extract the predicate as a pure util (e.g. `checkoutSearchFilter` next to `checkoutSearchTerms`) so it is unit-testable, and export it `@public` with JSDoc.

Note `CommandItem` `value` is `checkout.id` (a UUID) — the custom filter should ignore the value string and match keywords only, so UUID fragments don't produce ghost matches.

## Acceptance

- Searching `visormatt` in a list containing `visormatt/*` and `atlasworksinc/*` checkouts shows only the `visormatt` rows; group headings for empty groups disappear (cmdk handles this once items report 0).
- Searching `monorepo` still shows every `monorepo` checkout across orgs; searching `atlasworksinc mono` narrows to `atlasworksinc/monorepo`.
- Path (`Development`), branch (`main`) and project-name searches still match, as substrings.
- `No matching checkouts.` empty state still appears for garbage queries.

## Where

- `packages/react-router-chat/src/components/ChatCheckoutSelector.tsx` — pass `filter` to `<Command>`.
- `packages/react-router-chat/src/utils/checkout-groups.ts` (or a sibling util file per one-export-per-file conventions) — the pure filter function + tests.
- Source-first package: validate with `lint`/`typecheck`/`test`, then run `openthrottle-developer` as the integration check.
Searching the chat checkout/repository selector for `visormatt` matches every checkout (including all atlasworksinc repos). Replace cmdk's default fuzzy subsequence scoring with a strict, token-based substring filter over the checkout search terms so only genuinely matching checkouts survive.

Chat idle backstop aborts live claude turns (150s "no activity") — idle timers measure different signals
## Symptom
Chats via the "sonnet claude-code" backend in the developer chat UI intermittently fail with the terminal error: "The response timed out after 150s with no activity." Observed 3x in a row (8/10/26, ~1:23–2:16 PM). Reproduction just after showed healthy 8s turns, so this is intermittent/latency-triggered, not a hard break.

## Root cause
Two idle timers guard every turn and they measure DIFFERENT signals:
- CLI backend idle — packages/openthrottle-agentic-utils/src/utils/conversation-backend/claude/claude.ts:155 — 120s, resets on ANY stdout byte from `claude`.
- Server backstop idle — applications/openthrottle-server/src/graphql/conversation-stream/conversation-stream.service.ts:272 (withIdleTimeout) — 150s (resolveChatIdleTimeoutMs = agent idle 120s + 30s margin), resets ONLY when the backend YIELDS a mapped chunk.

The user sees the SERVER 150s message, not the CLI's own "idle timeout". That is only possible when `claude` emits stdout continuously (keeping the 120s CLI timer alive) while producing nothing the server counts as a chunk for 150s straight.

mapClaudeEvent (packages/openthrottle-agentic-utils/src/utils/conversation-backend/claude/events.ts:169) maps to NULL for:
- system/hook_started + system/hook_response (plugin SessionStart hooks — warp + vercel, 4 hooks, re-run every headless turn)
- system/status
- rate_limit_event

So during (a) slow/hanging startup hooks or (b) slow first-token / rate-limited API responses, `claude` is alive and emitting these null-mapped events; the CLI 120s idle never fires but the server 150s chunk-based idle does — killing a live turn. Empirically confirmed by reproducing the scrubbed-env spawn: a captured turn contained system/hook_*, system/status, and a rate_limit_event, plus heavy cache_creation_input_tokens (~28.6k) that lengthens time-to-first-token.

## Contributing amplifier
The claude backend spawns with the host's real HOME (ALLOWED_ENV_KEYS in claude.ts:35), so every chat turn re-runs the user's enabled plugin SessionStart hooks (warp@claude-code-warp + vercel@claude-plugins-official, verified in ~/.claude/plugins/installed_plugins.json) and injects a large Vercel CLAUDE.md — pure overhead on the critical path before the model answers.

## Fix direction
1. (Primary/code) Make the server idle backstop measure real backend liveness, not just mapped chunks. Either: emit a lightweight keepalive/status chunk (done:false) for currently-null system/*/rate_limit_event events so the server timer advances in lockstep with the CLI's stdout timer; OR reset withIdleTimeout on any raw stdout activity from the backend iterator. Add a regression test alongside packages/react-router-chat/src/__tests__/conversation-stream.test.ts (which asserts the 150s message) covering: null-mapped-but-alive stream must NOT trip the backstop.
2. (Mitigation/env) Server env knobs for headroom: OPENTHROTTLE_CHAT_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS (e.g. 300000), OPENTHROTTLE_AGENT_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS.
3. (Mitigation/isolation) Spawn headless `claude` with a dedicated CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/HOME that does not load user plugins, so chat turns stop re-running startup hooks and injecting plugin context every turn.

## Timeout math reference
DEFAULT_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS=120000, DEFAULT_CHAT_IDLE_MARGIN_MS=30000 → server backstop 150000ms. Defined in packages/openthrottle-agentic-utils/src/utils/conversation-backend/cursor-agent/teardown.ts.

## Note on scope
This blind spot is shared by all spawned CLI backends (grok/codex/cursor/opencode) that route through the same withIdleTimeout — any backend whose "alive" signals map to null is vulnerable. Fix should be evaluated at the orchestrator level, not only in the claude mapper.
Server-side chat idle backstop (150s) aborts claude CLI turns that are still alive because it only resets on *mapped* chunks, while null-mapped liveness events (system/hook_*, system/status, rate_limit_event) keep the CLI's own 120s stdout-based idle alive. Fix: make server idle measure real backend activity; reduce per-turn plugin-hook overhead from spawning with real HOME.

Persist fresh-setup bootstrap values to a git-ignored local file
## Problem

During a fresh `./scripts/setup.sh`, `scripts/bootstrap-service-account-credentials.ts` mints service-account bearer tokens (`OPENTHROTTLE_MCP_AUTH_TOKEN`, `OPENTHROTTLE_WORKER_GRAPHQL_AUTH_TOKEN`) and prints each **once** to stdout (bootstrap-service-account-credentials.ts:136-141). In the wall of setup output these scroll past and are frequently missed. Because the mint path *skips* any account that already has an active credential (bootstrap-service-account-credentials.ts:114-124), recovering a missed token is expensive: you must revoke the existing credential via admin GraphQL and re-mint. `scripts/bootstrap-default-user.ts` similarly echoes the seeded dev login (email/password) that a new machine needs.

## Goal

Write the bootstrap values to a **non-git-tracked file at the repo root** at mint time, so a user who misses the echoed stdout can recover them from disk WITHOUT having to expire/regenerate keys. The stdout echo stays; the file is an additional durable record.

## Approach

- Pick a root-level, git-ignored file (e.g. `.demo-workstation.local`) and add a `.gitignore` entry. Note `.env*` (`.gitignore:26`) already ignores any `.env*`-named file, so if the file is named under that pattern it's auto-ignored — but an explicit, clearly-named entry is preferred for discoverability.
- At mint time in `bootstrap-service-account-credentials.ts`, append/write each minted `ENV_VAR=token` line to the file (secrets only exist at mint time — cannot be re-derived later, so persistence MUST happen in the mint branch). Keep the existing one-time stdout echo.
- Persist the default-user login (email/password + login URLs) from `bootstrap-default-user.ts` to the same file for convenience.
- Idempotency: a re-run that mints nothing must not clobber a still-valid file. Decide overwrite-vs-append and de-dup behavior in the design task.
- Update `databases/README.md` and any "shown once" setup docs to point at the file.

## Non-goals

- No change to token minting/verification logic or the env-provided upsert path.
- Not a secrets manager — this is a local convenience file, kept out of git for the same reasons as `databases/seed.sql`.

## Key files

- `scripts/bootstrap-service-account-credentials.ts`
- `scripts/bootstrap-default-user.ts`
- `scripts/setup.sh`
- `.gitignore`
- `databases/README.md`

Settings → Appearance: regroup, prune, and componentize
# Settings → Appearance: regroup, prune, and componentize

## Context

`/settings/appearance` in `openthrottle-developer` is one flat `AppearancePanel` component (~205 lines) with four stacked, visually undifferentiated `<section>`s: Theme mode, Theme palette, Brand color, and a "CSS tokens affected by a custom brand" collapsible.

Files today:

- `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routes/settings.appearance.tsx` — thin route adapter. Its `loader` calls `getSettingsDiagnosticsLoaderData()` but nothing on the page consumes it (dead loader).
- `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routing/settings/components/AppearancePanel.tsx` — all markup and all handlers.
- `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routing/settings/config/appearance.ts` — just `THEME_DEFAULT_OPTION`.
- `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/global/data/atom.config.ts` — `configAtom` (`brand` / `theme` / `themeId`), localStorage-backed via `atomWithStorage`.
- `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routing/settings/components/SettingsOnboardingRestore.tsx` — written, tested, and **commented out** of the panel (`AppearancePanel.tsx:32,200`).

## Problems

1. **No grouping.** Three related-but-distinct concerns (color scheme, palette, brand) read as one undifferentiated stack. Nothing signals which controls interact.
2. **The CSS-token collapsible earns nothing.** It lists `--brand`, `--ring`, `--color-accent`, … — implementation trivia on a settings screen. Drop it.
3. **Palette picking is blind.** `THEMES` (OpenThrottle + the ported Cursor themes) renders as a name-only `<Select>`. You pick by reading a label, then eyeball the whole app.
4. **Stale copy.** The intro says "Diagnostics below mirror General settings" — there are no diagnostics on this route.
5. **Dead code shipped.** `SettingsOnboardingRestore` is commented out; the route loader is unused.
6. **Hard to change.** Adding, moving, or deleting a settings group means surgery inside one long JSX tree.

## Approach

Move from one long component to a **registry-driven set of small components**, so adding / reordering / deleting a group is a one-line data edit rather than JSX surgery.

- `AppearanceSection` — a shared card shell (title, description, optional aside, children). Every group renders through it, so spacing and heading treatment stay consistent for free.
- One component per control (`AppearanceThemeModeField`, `AppearancePaletteField`, `AppearanceBrandColorField`, …), each owning its own slice of `configAtom` and nothing else.
- `APPEARANCE_SECTIONS` in `routing/settings/data/data.appearance.ts` — an ordered array of `{ id, title, description, Component }`. `AppearancePanel` becomes a `.map()` over it. **Reorder = move an array entry. Remove = delete an entry. Add = append one.**
- Copy lives in `routing/settings/data/data.copy.ts` per the component/data-file boundary rule, not inline in JSX.

Proposed grouping:

| Group | Contains |
| --- | --- |
| **Color scheme** | Theme mode toggle (System / Light / Dark) |
| **Palette** | Palette swatch grid (replaces the name-only Select) + brand color override + "use theme default" |
| **Motion & effects** | Reduced-motion preference |
| **Guides & resets** | Restore dashboard onboarding + reset all appearance to defaults |

A live preview surface sits above the groups so palette + brand + mode changes are visible without leaving the page.

## What we're adding (and why)

**In scope — high value, low risk:**

- **Palette swatch grid.** Render each `THEMES` entry as a small multi-swatch chip drawn from its own `light`/`dark` token record. Picking a palette becomes a visual choice.
- **Live preview card.** A compact sample (buttons, badge, muted text, chart-color row, sidebar accent strip) rendered under the current selections. Answers "what does this actually do" — the honest job the CSS-token list was failing to do.
- **Reset appearance to defaults.** One control returning `configAtom` to `DEFAULT_APPEARANCE_CONFIG`; today you reset brand and palette separately and there's no way back to `system`.
- **Restore onboarding.** Uncomment `SettingsOnboardingRestore` into the "Guides & resets" group — it already exists and is already tested.
- **Reduced motion.** The app ships `GlobalAnimationMesh` / `GlobalAnimationWaves` / `GradientMesh` with no user control. A `reducedMotion: 'system' | 'always'` field on `configAtom` (default `system`, respecting `prefers-reduced-motion`) is a real accessibility win.

**Deliberately out of scope:**

- **UI density / font scale.** Genuinely useful, but it needs shared spacing/size tokens in `react-router-shadcn` before a toggle means anything. Worth its own plan.
- **Server-side persistence of appearance.** Stays localStorage-only here.

## Cleanup this plan owns

- Delete the CSS-token `Collapsible` block and its `APPEARANCE_BRAND_OVERRIDE_KEYS` / `APPEARANCE_THEME_COLOR_TOKEN_KEYS` imports from the panel.
- Keep those constants in `packages/react-router-utils/src/utils/theme.ts` — `buildBrandOverrideCss` (`theme.ts:204`) and `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routes/__tests__/settings.cusomization.test.tsx` still consume them. Only the UI listing goes away.
- Drop the unused `loader` from `settings.appearance.tsx`.
- Fix the stale "Diagnostics below mirror General settings" intro copy.

## Constraints

- Generators first: `NX_ISOLATE_PLUGINS=false pnpm nx g @tools/generators:react-router --subGenerator=component --application=openthrottle-developer --folder=settings --name=A,B,C` (comma-separated batch). Do not hand-write component files.
- Keep the generated section comments (`// Hooks` / `// Setup` / `// Handlers` / `// Markup` / `// Life Cycle` / `// 🔌 Short Circuit`) even when empty.
- One component per file; components export only the component + its props interface. Lists and copy go in the nearest `data/`.
- UI from `@openthrottle/react-router-shadcn` only. No new enums — `as const` objects. No `as` casts.
- Tests use `component` (not `screen`) and `userEvent`.
- Existing tests to keep green: `app/routing/settings/components/__tests__/AppearancePanel.test.tsx`, `app/routes/__tests__/settings.appearance.test.tsx`, `app/routes/__tests__/settings.cusomization.test.tsx`.

## Validation

```bash
pnpm nx run openthrottle-developer:lint
pnpm nx run openthrottle-developer:typecheck
pnpm nx run openthrottle-developer:test
```

Then a visual pass on `/settings/appearance` in light, dark, and System, across at least three palettes.

Regroup /settings/appearance into registry-driven sections, drop the CSS-token list, and add a palette swatch grid, live preview, reduced-motion, and reset controls.
