`cursor-agent --help` exposes `--approve-mcps` (auto-approve all MCP servers) and `--trust` (trust the workspace without prompting). Neither is emitted. In headless `-p` mode the project's `.cursor/mcp.json` servers require approval/trust, so `openthrottle-mcp` never attaches — the schedule fires an agent structurally incapable of the job it was given.

A grep for `approve-mcps|--trust|mcp-config` across `packages/openthrottle-drivers/src` and `tools/workflows/src` returns **zero hits**. This is a gap in **all five registered drivers** (`claude`, `codex`, `cursor`, `grok`, `opencode` — see `drivers/index.ts` `ALL_DRIVERS`), not just cursor. `claude.ts` likewise emits only `claude -p --permission-mode acceptEdits`.

The engine (`packages/openthrottle-drivers/src/engine/index.ts`) spawns with `shell: true` and the inherited server env — no MCP config or auth token is injected either, and a BullMQ worker's env is not a login shell's env.

**2 — Process exit code is treated as task outcome.**
`ScheduledAgentJobsProcessor.runStatusForAgentStatus` maps `RUN_AGENT_STATUS.ok` -> `succeeded`. Agent CLIs exit 0 when the model declines to act, so an aborted run is indistinguishable from a completed one. Every scheduled job depending on MCP has been silently green.

**3 — No token usage for cursor runs.**
`foldRunUsage` folds JSONL usage lines, but the cursor driver runs the default `--output-format text`, so there is nothing to parse — hence "No token usage was reported for this run." `cursor-agent` supports `--output-format stream-json`. Overlaps plan `2c9bd39e` (scheduled-run metadata); coordinate rather than duplicate.

## Blast radius — three surfaces, not one

`buildShellCommand` is shared by every agent invocation path:

- **scheduled jobs** — `applications/openthrottle-server/src/queues/scheduled-agent-jobs/scheduled-agent-runner.service.ts`
- **chat** — `packages/openthrottle-agentic-utils/src/utils/conversation-backend/agent-setup-executor.ts:220`
- **OT Loop** — `tools/workflows/src/bin/run-iteration.ts:109` (and `:125`)

A driver-level fix reaches all three for free, which is the point — but it also means the MCP flags change chat and OT Loop behavior, and `--trust`/`--approve-mcps` auto-approve every configured MCP server. That is the intent for an unattended scheduled run in a known repo; it may be a permissions widening for an interactive chat session. The chat/OT Loop regression task owns that decision.

## Scope

- **In:** root causes 1 and 2, across all five drivers, with the chat and OT Loop surfaces explicitly regression-checked.
- **Out:** token-usage persistence (root cause 3) — owned by `2c9bd39e`. Touch `--output-format stream-json` here only where the run-outcome signal needs a structured result event.

## Key files

- `packages/openthrottle-drivers/src/drivers/{cursor,claude,codex,grok,opencode}.ts`
- `packages/openthrottle-drivers/src/types/index.ts` (`DriverCapabilities`)

Follow-up: Parse & render structured skill arguments in the Run-skill modal
## Goal

Upgrade the Run-skill modal (from the "Run a skill from the /skills/:slug detail route" plan, id `0cd89ddc-158d-4ce1-8140-551ee7b2eeb7`) from a single free-text **Arguments** box to **typed, per-argument form fields** derived from the skill's own declaration. When a skill declares arguments, render one labeled field per argument (respecting type / required / description / default); when it declares none, fall back to the v1 free-text field.

## Important framing (spec reality)

The user's expectation was that arguments "would already be present" because OT skills follow the Agent Skills spec (https://agentskills.io/specification). **That spec does NOT define a first-class `arguments`/`inputs` field.** Its frontmatter is only: `name`, `description`, `license`, `compatibility`, `metadata` (an arbitrary string→string map), and experimental `allowed-tools`. So there is nothing typed to parse today.

This plan therefore has a **design decision as task 1**: pick the source of truth for argument declarations. Options (pick one, spec-compatible first):

1. **`metadata` convention (spec-compatible).** Store an args schema under a namespaced `metadata` key, e.g. `metadata.openthrottle-arguments` = a JSON/YAML string of `[{ name, type, required, description, default, enum }]`. Stays 100% within the spec (metadata is free-form string→string). Slightly awkward (stringified schema).
2. **OT frontmatter extension.** Add a top-level `arguments:` block to SKILL.md frontmatter and teach the OT parser to read it. Cleaner authoring, but a superset of the spec (non-portable; other tools ignore it).
3. **Parse from the body.** Heuristically extract an "Arguments"/"Inputs" section from the markdown body. Rejected as fragile unless a strict convention is enforced — note but don't build.

Recommendation to evaluate: option 1 (metadata convention) for spec-fidelity, with a small typed helper so authoring is still ergonomic. Confirm with the owner before building parser + UI.

## Scope

- Extend the skill frontmatter parser (`packages/openthrottle-skills/src/parse-skill-frontmatter.ts` — add a typed `arguments` field; no new enums, use `as const` for the arg-type union) and thread it onto `RepoSkillEntry` (`applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routing/agents/data/repo-skills-registry.ts`) and any GraphQL surface if the parsed args need to reach the client that way (the skill route loader is filesystem-based, so it can likely pass parsed args directly).
- Render dynamic fields in `RunSkillDialog` / `useRunSkillDialog`: one control per declared argument (text / number / boolean / enum-select), with required-validation feeding `submitDisabled`.
- Compose the invocation string from the structured values (define the encoding: positional vs `--flag value`; match how skills actually consume args at invocation — verify against the harness/skill-invocation path, not assumed).
- Keep the free-text fallback for skills with no declared arguments (v1 behavior).
- Add a couple of OT skills' declarations as reference/dogfood examples once the convention is chosen.

## Constraints / conventions

- Do not break the v1 modal contract — this is additive.
- Follow the same conventions as the base plan: generators-first for any new components, section comments, one-component-per-file, `@openthrottle/react-router-shadcn` controls, avoid `as`/`any`, `import type`, explicit return types.
- If a GraphQL type gains an `arguments` field, deprecate rather than break, run codegen, commit `__generated__`.
- Tests: parser unit tests (valid/invalid/absent declarations) + render-level Vitest for dynamic field rendering + required-validation + invocation-string composition.

## Dependencies

Blocked on the base plan `0cd89ddc-158d-4ce1-8140-551ee7b2eeb7` landing (needs the modal + `useRunSkillDialog` to exist).

Build the 05-connect-ot-mcp screencast flow
Port `docs/marketing/scripts/05-connect-ot-mcp.md` to a recorded flow in the openthrottle-developer demo pipeline (`applications/openthrottle-developer/tests/demo/`).

This is the first Season 1 short whose subject is not the product's UI. Six of its eight beats are a terminal and a text editor; only the 0:44 payoff is in the browser. Every flow recorded so far (01, 03, 04, 21) lives entirely inside the dashboard, so this one does not merely add beats — it asks the pipeline for a capability it does not have.

## Gate 1: the runner cannot record a terminal or an editor

`runner/actions.ts` implements exactly thirteen verbs — `click`, `dwell`, `highlight`, `hover`, `moveTo`, `navigate`, `press`, `scrollTo`, `select`, `type`, `waitFor`, `waitForUrl`, `zoomTo` — and every one of them drives a Playwright page. `runner/run.ts` launches `chromium` and captures a CDP screencast of that browser. There is no verb, and no capture surface, for a shell or for VS Code.

That is not an oversight to patch casually: the pipeline chose Playwright over screen capture precisely because macOS screen capture hangs on an interactive permission grant and records the whole desktop (see the spike README). Re-opening that decision for one short would re-open it for the whole channel.

Three ways out, and this must be decided before any flow is written:

- Type the terminal and the editor **in the browser**, the way captions and cards are already typeset there — an HTML surface styled as a shell and as an editor pane, driven by the existing `type` and `press` verbs. Consistent with the pipeline's existing "typeset it in the recording browser" precedent, and it makes the on-screen text scannable by `video-scan` for free.
- Reshoot the script around `/settings/mcp`, which already exists (`settings.mcp._index.tsx`, `settings.mcp.$connectorId.tsx`) and is a real product surface. Changes what the short teaches.
- Add a real terminal capture path. Highest cost, re-opens the settled recorder decision, and puts arbitrary desktop content in frame.

## Gate 2: the command's own output fails the leak scan

The 0:00 and 0:09 beats put the output of `pnpm run setup:mcp-instructions` on camera. `scripts/setup_mcp-instructions.ts` resolves the repo root with `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` and prints `${root}/scripts/run-openthrottle-mcp.sh`, and it names the client config files as `join(homedir(), '.claude.json')` and `join(homedir(), '.cursor', 'mcp.json')`.

Every one of those is an absolute `/Users/<name>/…` path, and `scan/rules.ts` rule `home-path` is `severity: 'error'` — "a home directory leaks a username and the shape of someone's machine". The single most important thing this short asks the viewer to copy is the exact string the publish gate is built to reject. This is not a scan tuning exercise; the frame genuinely should not ship a real machine's paths.

## Gate 3: the script's happy path does not happen on the recording machine

`setup_mcp-instructions.ts` checks whether the `openthrottle-mcp` node is already registered and, when it is, prints `✓ already installed, nothing to do.` instead of the install block. On any machine that can record this short, OT MCP is already installed — that is how the recording gets a seeded database in the first place. The beat as written cannot be captured by simply running the command.

## What already exists and needs no work

- The payoff surface: `/plans` (`plans._index.tsx`) renders the plans list, and the demo fixture seeds enough plans that a new one arriving at the top reads clearly.
- `scripts/setup_mcp-instructions.ts` is pure stdout with no side effects, so it is safe to run repeatedly while iterating.
- The `type` verb supports per-character pacing, which is what a believable terminal beat needs.

## Constraints

- 63 spoken words is the budget in the script frontmatter; any rewrite of a beat must re-validate against `scripts/validate-video-scripts.ts` and the `short` budget in `docs/marketing/format.json`.
- A flow may not invent a step the script does not describe, and a script may not describe UI that does not exist. Whichever gate resolution is chosen, the script and the flow end up agreeing before recording.
- Never point a flow at real data or a real machine's configuration.
- Produce, do not publish. Uploading needs the channel credentials and the owner's decision.

Layer OT curated skills into foreign workspaces (server-scoped, non-mutating)
## Problem

OT's real value downstream is its curated skill set (create-readme, ot-plans, the nx-*/openthrottle-* skills, etc.). But when OT drives an agent in a **foreign workspace** — any checkout outside the OT monorepo, e.g. `ssm-data-pipeline` in the reference screenshot — those skills are unavailable. Today the only foreign-workspace handling is a *prompt layer* (`buildForeignWorkspacePromptLayer`, packages/openthrottle-agentic-utils/src/utils/foreign-workspace-context.ts) that does the OPPOSITE of what we now want: it instructs the agent to NOT reference OT `/skills`, generators, or tooling. Result: "OpenThrottle MCP server and /create-readme skill are unavailable here."

## Goal

Make OT's curated skills a **layered, non-mutating, server-scoped** base that gets projected INTO the foreign repo while the OT server is running, reused across runs, and reconciled on shutdown/boot — extending the existing skill-sync SSOT/fan-out (`skills/<name>` → `.agents/skills/<name>` → per-agent dirs, driven by `skills/skill-sync/scripts/sync.sh`) to a third, external target.

## Locked decisions (visormatt, revised 2026-08-13)

These SUPERSEDE the 2026-08-12 decisions, which assumed run-scoped ephemeral injection and that Cursor/Grok had no skill mechanism. The latter was stale: Cursor 2.4+ and Grok Build CLI both read the SKILL.md standard. The former was reframed after confirming CLIs only discover skills from dirs inside the working tree (no out-of-repo `--skills-dir` pointer exists) and that visibility "while the server runs" is the desired property.

1. **Placement — in-repo, forced by CLI reality.** All five CLIs (claude/codex/opencode/cursor/grok) discover skills only from dirs inside the working tree; none exposes an out-of-repo `--skills-dir` flag or env override. Inject into **`.agents/skills/` + `.claude/skills/`** — the union of those two dirs covers all five (`.agents/skills` → claude/codex/opencode/cursor; `.claude/skills` → claude/cursor/grok). Reuse skill-sync's symlink/ownership semantics rather than reinventing them. (Global user dirs like `~/.claude/skills`, `~/.grok/skills` were considered and REJECTED: non-uniform across CLIs and permanently global — they would leak OT skills into every repo and every interactive session, overshooting "while the server runs.")
2. **Lifecycle — server-scoped, per-repo** (changed from run-scoped ephemeral). Materialize the layer lazily on the first foreign run that touches a given repo; keep it in place while the OT server runs; REUSE across all subsequent runs (no per-run setup cost). Teardown on server shutdown, plus a boot-time reaper for missed teardowns. This matches visormatt's stated preference: OT skills present and visible while the server is running.
3. **Non-mutation — symlinks + `.git/info/exclude` + ledger.** Injected links are made invisible to `git status` via the repo-local **`.git/info/exclude`** (NOT the tracked `.gitignore`, and NOT a global `core.excludesFile`, which would leak into every repo and risk masking real files). A per-repo LEDGER (JSON of every injected path) records exactly what was created. The target repo's tracked files are never modified; `git status` is clean at all times, not merely after a successful teardown.
4. **Recovery — ledger-driven boot sweep.** On startup, reconcile ledgers against live filesystem state and remove exactly the paths recorded (and only still-OT-owned symlinks/copies), covering missed teardowns after a server/run crash. Piggybacks on the existing STALE-run sweep lifecycle (heartbeat/cutoff, PlanRunsService.settleStaleRun).
5. **Precedence — target repo wins.** OT skills are a BASE layer that fills gaps; any skill name the target repo already defines is excluded from the manifest and never masked. Layering low→high: OT curated (`skills/`) < personal/experimental (per-user dir) < target repo.
6. **Container mode — copy, not symlink.** When workspace path-mapping is active (workspace-paths.ts host↔container bridge), symlink targets won't resolve across mount namespaces; materialize COPIES (or arrange a bind mount) in that mode. Host-run mode stays symlinks.
7. **Personal/experimental tier — per-user dir outside the repo.** A configured, opt-in per-user location (e.g. `~/.openthrottle/skills`), layered ABOVE OT curated but BELOW the target repo. It is a resolver SOURCE only — the materializer projects it into the repo like everything else; it does not depend on any CLI reading an out-of-repo dir. Unreleased skills never touch git and are never force-fed to other users.

## Approach (high level)

1. A layered skill-set RESOLVER that merges OT curated (`skills/`) + personal-user-dir into an ordered manifest, applying name-collision precedence and excluding target-repo-owned names, reusing skill-sync's symlink/ownership semantics.
2. A server/repo-scoped MATERIALIZER that, given a foreign repo, idempotently ensures the resolved layer exists in `.agents/skills/` + `.claude/skills/` (symlinks on host, copies under the container bridge), writes a per-repo ledger, and registers `.git/info/exclude` entries. Idempotent "ensure-materialized(repo)" — a no-op when already present. Teardown removes exactly and only the ledger-recorded paths.
3. WIRING into the foreign-workspace run path so ensure-materialized runs at run start (idempotent, reused across runs) and teardown runs on server shutdown — and RECONCILING `buildForeignWorkspacePromptLayer` so it no longer blanket-forbids the now-available OT skills (while still forbidding OT monorepo paths/generators), surfacing which skills were injected.
4. CRASH-SAFETY reaper: a boot-time (and/or periodic) ledger-driven sweep that removes stranded injected links even after a missed teardown, riding the existing STALE-run sweep lifecycle.
5. Container path-mapping awareness (toContainerPath/toHostPath, workspace-paths.ts) so injection works under the Docker host-execution bridge via copy mode, not just host-run.

Non-goal: changing how OT's in-repo skill-sync fan-out works. This adds an external consumer of the same SSOT.
Extend the skill-sync fan-out to reach into a downstream/foreign repo: layer OT's curated skills (plus an opt-in per-user experimental tier) into the target workspace's .agents/skills + .claude/skills. Materialized server-scoped/per-repo (lazily on first foreign run, reused across runs while the server is up, torn down on shutdown + boot reaper), non-mutating via symlink/copy + .git/info/exclude + a per-repo ledger so git status stays clean. Target repo's own skills win on collision.

We want this audit to behave like the linter: it must pass to successfully **commit**, not just to push.

## Goal

Add the strict component-shape audit to the **pre-commit** lifecycle so every commit (human or agent) is gated, keeping pre-commit / pre-push / CI in lockstep on the exact same command.

## Key facts (already verified)

- Command is fast enough for a commit hook: `pnpm run audit:component-shape:strict` runs repo-wide in ~1.35s.
- CI (line 201) and pre-push both run the SAME single command: `pnpm run audit:component-shape:strict` (the authored variant). Neither runs the `:shadcn:strict` variant — only `check:local:component-shape` runs both. **Decision: pre-commit mirrors CI/pre-push = authored strict only.** Do NOT add the shadcn variant to the commit gate (keep the three surfaces on one identical command).
- `.husky/pre-commit` currently runs only `lint-staged`. `.husky/pre-push` already runs the audit with a clear failure message; the new pre-commit block should reuse that exact wording/command.
- The script (`scripts/audit-component-shape.ts`) is **repo-wide** (`globSync`), not staged-file-scoped — same as pre-push/CI. It reads the working tree, so it can flag a violation in a file not part of the current commit. This matches existing pre-push behavior and is acceptable; do not attempt to scope to staged files (would diverge from CI and add fragility).
- Bypass is prohibited by CLAUDE.md: never `--no-verify` / never bypass Husky. Fix the violation instead.

## Non-goals

- Do not change what the audit checks or the R4/R5/R6/R7 rules.
- Do not scope the audit to staged files.
- Do not add the shadcn strict variant to the commit/push gate.

## Rollout note

This will start blocking commits that previously only blocked on push. Confirm the repo is currently green (`pnpm run audit:component-shape:strict` exits 0 on `main`) before enabling, so we don't hand agents/humans an immediately-broken commit gate.

## Problem / motivation

The skill-usage hook system already has the right *shape* — a tool-neutral core plus thin per-tool adapters — but the core is a hand-written CommonJS file (`.agents/hooks/skill-usage/lib.cjs`, ~25KB) that each adapter reaches by relative `require('../../.agents/hooks/skill-usage/lib.cjs')`. That's robust at runtime (no install/build needed) but has no TS authoring, no Nx lint/typecheck/test targets, and copy-me adapter duplication (`adapter.template.cjs`).

Additional agents/editors (Cursor and others) are landing **very soon**, each needing its own adapter + config wiring. Before that fan-out multiplies, promote the core to a real workspace package **without** regressing the two hard guarantees that make hooks safe: **fail-open** (never block a Skill call) and **zero runtime external-dependency resolution** (hooks run as bare `node x.cjs` in fresh checkouts and worktrees, where `node_modules`/pnpm-symlink resolution is exactly what breaks).

## Chosen approach (the "package + esbuild" middle ground)

- Author the neutral core in **TypeScript** in a new package `@openthrottle/agentic-hooks` (`packages/agentic-hooks`).
- Author each tool's adapter as a **TS esbuild entrypoint** in that package.
- An Nx **bundle** target runs esbuild (`platform:node`, `format:cjs`, node builtins external only, everything else inlined) to emit **self-contained committed `.cjs`** files into each tool's hook folder (`.claude/hooks/*.cjs`, `.cursor/hooks/*.cjs`, …). At runtime the hook `require`s nothing outside node builtins — same robustness as today.
- A **codegen-style drift check** (mirrors the `schema.gql` / graphql-codegen CI gate) regenerates bundles and fails on diff, so committed artifacts can't rot. This mirrors the existing skill-sync generated-file model (source of truth in package; generated artifacts committed + fanned out).

## Non-negotiable constraints (carry into every task)

- **Fail-open always**: swallow errors, `exit 0`, never block a Skill call. Behavior-preserving migration — no telemetry regression.
- **Zero runtime external deps**: bundled `.cjs` must resolve nothing outside node builtins. No `require('@openthrottle/...')` in shipped hooks. Verify against a checkout with `node_modules` absent.
- **Committed, tracked bundles** — NOT gitignored. Gitignored generated files are invisible to Nx input hashing and cause poisoned-cache bugs (see prior GCS cache poisoning from gitignored `__generated__`). Bundle outputs are tracked inputs.
- **Deterministic esbuild output** so the drift check is stable: pin esbuild version, no date/timestamp banners, stable sorting, consistent minify setting.
- Preserve the **privacy seam** for plan `91679bbf` (configurable privacy) and stay additive to base plan `d3759118`.
- Node >= 22, pnpm only, all generator commands prefixed `NX_ISOLATE_PLUGINS=false pnpm nx g @tools/generators:...`.

## Relationship to plan f5e40886 (Outcomes & Avg duration)

`f5e40886` extends the *same* core with the automatic outcome/duration capture path. Sequencing must be decided in task 1. Recommended: land THIS package skeleton + a **behavior-preserving migration of the existing capture path first** (pure refactor, no new behavior), then author f5e40886's new outcome/complete/drain logic **inside the package** rather than in the retired `lib.cjs`. Whichever order is chosen, avoid two agents editing the same core in two forms simultaneously.

Each task carries its own acceptance criteria in `requirements`.

Per-tool adapters become esbuild bundle entrypoints that compile into self-contained committed .cjs files under each tool's hook folder (.claude/hooks, .cursor/hooks, ...), so hooks keep ZERO runtime node_modules dependency and stay fail-open. Add a codegen-style drift check so committed bundles can't rot. Motivated by additional agents (Cursor et al.) landing soon — this is the middle ground that gives package ergonomics (TS, Nx lint/typecheck/test) without the worktree resolution fragility a workspace symlink would introduce at hook runtime.

Bring react-router-shadcn into the component-shape standard
## Why this is a separate plan

`packages/react-router-shadcn` was deliberately excluded from the base audit ([OT 0f0528ff](../plans/0f0528ff-13dd-45c9-8f41-75547ecba3b3)) as vendored primitives. Owner's call: we *install and control* these files, so they deserve a standard too — but a **different** one, because they are structurally unlike an authored component.

## What makes shadcn different (measured 2026-07-30)
- **154** component files. **66** use `React.forwardRef`. **125** are **multi-export** (e.g. `Card` + `CardHeader` + `CardTitle` + `CardContent` + `CardFooter`).
- They type props via `React.ComponentProps<...>` / cva `VariantProps`, **not** a hand-written `FooProps` interface.
- Our copies have **already diverged from upstream**: PascalCase filenames (`Button.tsx`, `Card.tsx`) and compound components in `index` folders (`Accordion/`, `AlertDialog/`), vs the registry's kebab-case single files. A `components.json` exists but no longer matches our layout.

**Implication:** the base primitive shape (single `export const Foo` + single `export interface FooProps` + the six ordered markers) does **not** cleanly apply. Stamping the template on a compound cva primitive would be wrong. So step one is deciding what 'conform' *means* here.

## Central design question (the first task, human-gated)
Define a **primitive/compound variant** of the standard that fits cva + forwardRef + multi-export reality. Candidate dimensions to standardize instead of the 6-marker body:
- Consistent export style + ordering; consistent props typing (`ComponentProps`/`VariantProps` convention); `cn` import + variant (`cva`) placement; file/folder naming (single file vs `index` folder threshold); one-primitive-family-per-file.
- Whether the markers apply at all (maybe only to any genuinely-authored logic components living in the package), or a reduced marker set.

## Upstream re-sync tradeoff (decide explicitly)
Because our filenames/structure already diverge from the shadcn registry, `shadcn` CLI re-sync is **already** a manual merge. The plan must decide: do we keep pretending we can re-sync (and cap divergence), or declare these files fully owned and drop the registry contract? That decision sets how far 'conform' can go.

## Scope note / clarifying '+ vendored'
'Vendored' = code sourced from outside rather than hand-authored (shadcn is the main example). Generated/build output (`dist/**`, `__generated__/**`) and `__tests__/**` stay **permanently** excluded from every component audit — they're artifacts, not source. This plan pulls **only shadcn** back into scope, under its own variant ruleset.

## Strategy
Design the shadcn variant + re-sync policy (HUMAN GATE) → extend the ESLint rule + audit script with a 'primitive' profile → pilot on a few simple single-export primitives → bulldoze the compound/forwardRef families in batches → flip enforcement on for the package + document the ownership/re-sync policy. Reuses the enforcer infrastructure built in OT 0f0528ff.
Follow-up to the primitive-shape audit (OT 0f0528ff): the shadcn package was scoped OUT as vendored, but we install and control it, so hold it to a standard too. First define what 'conform' means for multi-export / forwardRef / cva primitives (the base template doesn't map), then extend the enforcers with a primitive profile and roll it out.

Multi-select repositories in the chat composer (primary checkout + additional context dirs)
## Goal

Let a chat conversation carry more than one repository of context. Today the composer selects exactly one checkout; that id becomes a single `cwd: string` on the server and drives the process spawn, the managed MCP config, and CLI session resume.

## The constraint that shapes the design

`packages/openthrottle-agentic-utils/src/utils/conversation-backend/types.ts:221` is `cwd?: string` — one process, one working directory. A second repository is NOT a second cwd; it is an **additional granted directory**, and only some CLIs have that concept:

- **antigravity** — already emits `--add-dir <cwd>` (`antigravity/argv.ts:67`); the flag is repeatable.
- **claude** — supports `--add-dir`.
- **cursor**, **opencode** — no equivalent modeled in this repo.

So the shipped model is **one primary checkout + N additional context dirs**, capability-gated per driver. It is not N peer repositories.

## Current chain (single-select), for reference

1. `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routing/home/demo/models.server.ts:121` — `WorkspaceLocalRepositories` → `RepositoryOption[]` (`{ id, displayName, filesystemPath }`).
2. `packages/react-router-chat-state/src/data/atom.chat-toolbar.ts` — `repositoryId: string | undefined` persisted in `chatToolbarStateAtom` (schema **v3**, key `${APP_NAME}:chat:toolbar`).
3. `packages/react-router-chat-state/src/utils/chat-toolbar-reconcile.ts:159` — re-validates each render; drops a vanished id, clears when `requiresRepository === false`, else falls back to `repositories[0]?.id`.
4. `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routing/home/demo/useHomeComposer.tsx` + `packages/react-router-chat-state/src/hooks/useHeaderChatController.tsx:198` — map to `checkouts`, render `ChatCheckoutSelector` (single-select `DropdownMenu`).
5. `packages/react-router-chat-state/src/utils/chat-turn-fields.ts` — `repositoryId: string` on the `intent=start` form; omitted for the `openai` backend.
6. `packages/react-router-chat/src/conversation-stream-action.ts:85` — form field → `StartConversationStreamInput.repositoryId`.
7. `applications/openthrottle-server/src/graphql/conversation-stream/conversation-stream.resolver.ts:479` — `findByIdForUser` (ownership check) → `toContainerPath(filesystemPath)` → `cwd`, which then feeds the spawn, `buildManagedMcpServers({ repositoryRoot: cwd })`, and `repositoryMetadataKey(backend)` in conversation metadata.

## Decisions (confirm before task 1)

- **MCP scope: primary-only.** `buildManagedMcpServers` keeps taking the primary checkout as `repositoryRoot`. Registering an OT MCP server per secondary repo is a larger change with unclear value in v1.
- **Conversation identity: primary-as-session-key.** `repositoryMetadataKey(backend)` continues to store the primary id alone, so swapping secondaries mid-conversation does not fork the CLI session. Matches how the CLIs actually resume.
- **`@`-mentions: out of scope for v1.** `useFileMentionProvider` / `/ide/files` stay keyed on the primary repository. Multi-repo mentions need repo-qualified paths (`repo-name/src/foo.ts`) or the agent cannot disambiguate — a UX design task in its own right. Track as a follow-up plan.

## Known risk to surface, not solve here

`findLiveRunsByCheckoutIds` (`packages/nestjs-repositories/src/modules/plan-runs/plan-runs.service.ts:424`) already exists because two conversations with write access to the same checkout stomp each other. Multi-select makes that collision meaningfully more likely. v1 should not add a lock, but the secondary-dir affordance should not silently imply write safety either.

## Out of scope

Multi-repo `@`-mentions; per-repo MCP servers; any checkout locking or run-concurrency guard; admin app parity beyond what the shared `useHeaderChatController` gives for free.
Turn the chat composer's single-select checkout picker into a capability-gated multi-select: one primary checkout (the spawn cwd) plus N additional granted directories threaded as repeated --add-dir for the CLIs that support it.

Make the developer-app command palette (⌘K / OpenThrottleCommander) consume the same navigation source of truth as the global sidebar, instead of a hardcoded subset in useCommanderOptions.

## Problem

`root.tsx` already feeds `GlobalLayout` from `dataNavigationV2` / `dataNavigationGuest` (`app/global/data/data.navigation.ts`). Commander groups come from a separate hardcoded list in `useCommanderOptions()`:

- Only five destinations today: Dashboard, Plans, Projects, Queues, Notes — missing Skills, Rules, Schedule, Usage, Settings/*, Docs, FAQ, Chats, and everything else already in the sidebar.
- Different icons than the sidebar (e.g. Plans uses MapIcon in the palette vs NotebookTextIcon in nav).
- Single "Navigation" heading vs sidebar groups Agents / Settings / Workspace (and Legal for guests).
- Ignores `disabled` and `beta` flags that `GlobalSidebarContent` already honors (`FEATURE_BETA_PREVIEW` hides beta; `disabled` is muted unless `FEATURE_CHARLIE_PREVIEW`).
- Always uses the authenticated list, even when `GlobalLayout` is on `dataNavigationGuest`.

Adding a sidebar link today does not add a ⌘K row. That split will keep drifting.

## Goal

One navigation record drives both the sidebar and commander groups. Adding, disabling, or beta-flagging a link in `data.navigation.ts` is enough for both surfaces.

## Approach

1. **Pure mapper** (new util under `app/global/utils/`, not inlined in the hook): `Record<string, GlobalSidebarContentLinkProps[]>` → `CommanderGroup[]`.
   - Group heading = navigation section key (Agents, Settings, Workspace, Legal).
   - Item: `label` from string `children`, `onSelect` via `navigate(to)`, same lucide icon at commander size (`h-3! w-3!`).
   - Stable `id` from path (`nav-dashboard`, `nav-settings-agents`); special-case `to: '/'` (Chats) so it is not an empty slug.
   - Set `CommanderItem.value` to include label + path so cmdk filter matches "plans", "settings", or "/plans", not only the id.
   - Omit empty groups after filtering.
2. **Filter to match sidebar visibility**
   - Drop `beta: true` unless `FEATURE_BETA_PREVIEW`.
   - Drop `disabled: true` unless `FEATURE_CHARLIE_PREVIEW` (cmdk has no good "visible but unclickable" state; omitting is the palette equivalent of `pointer-events-none`).
3. **`useCommanderOptions` takes the same record `GlobalLayout` gets.** Root picks once: `const navigation = data?.user ? dataNavigationV2 : dataNavigationGuest` and passes it to both. Do not re-branch on auth inside the hook.
4. **Leave commander-only extras alone.** Empty-state UUID/search rows (`commander-empty-extras`) and the commented Actions group (Create plan / Create project) stay out of this mapper. Re-enable Actions later as a separate optional group if needed.
5. **No shared-package change unless required.** `CommanderItem` already has `onSelect` / `icon` / `value`. Do not add `disabled` to `@openthrottle/react-router-ui` just to hide rows — filter in the app mapper.

## Out of scope

- Empty-state extras, `commander-search` POST jumps, header search chrome.
- Keyboard shortcuts per item.
- Uncommenting the Actions group.
- Changing `data.navigation.ts` destinations themselves (this plan consumes it, does not redesign IA).

## Acceptance

- Authenticated ⌘K groups match enabled, non-beta (or beta-when-flag-on) entries in `dataNavigationV2`, grouped as Agents / Settings / Workspace.
- Guest ⌘K groups match `dataNavigationGuest`.
- Selecting a row navigates to that link's `to`.
- Adding a sidebar link in `data.navigation.ts` appears in the palette with no second list to update.
- Tests treat `data.navigation.ts` as SSOT (assert mapper output against the imported nav data + flags, not a duplicated id list).
- `docs/commander-and-search-entrypoints.md` updated so `useCommanderOptions` is described as derived from navigation data.

Shard the openthrottle-developer Vitest suite across CI boxes with --shard
> Spawned from plan `88f747ff` after its Phase B (splitting `openthrottle-developer` into libraries) was **measured and rejected**. This plan is the alternative that won on the numbers.

## Why

Measured on the base commit (`0e170105`), heaviest CI unit is `openthrottle-developer`:

| target | wall clock | share |
| --- | --- | --- |
| lint | 9.6s | 5.5% |
| typecheck | 10.6s | 6.1% |
| **test** | **154.1s** | **88.4%** |

`test` is ~88% of the cost, so that is the only slice worth attacking. Vitest `--shard` splits it **within** the single Nx project, needs no code movement, and works on this suite today — verified by running it:

| shard | files | wall clock |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1/3 | 227 | **60.9s** |
| 2/3 | 226 | 54.6s |
| 3/3 | 226 | 48.4s |

**154.1s -> 60.9s on the heaviest box (-60%).** For comparison, the rejected 1,255-file project split bought ~23%.

## The stale assumption this corrects

`applications/openthrottle-developer/vitest.config.ts` currently reasons:

> "project sharding splits the affected PROJECT list, and this suite is a single Nx project, so whichever box draws it runs all of it. The matrix cannot lower this suite's wall-clock — a faster pool can."

Correct about **project** sharding — and it is why the vmForks work (plan `e448a51d`, forks 253s -> vmForks 86s) was the right call at the time. But it frames the options as "faster pool" or "move the code". Vitest `--shard` is a third lever. `.github/workflows/continuous-integration.yml` (~line 225) has the same stale framing, calling the heaviest project a floor "which suite sharding cannot split".

## The actual work

The hard part is **not** `--shard` itself; it is that the CI matrix currently assigns each project to exactly ONE shard via `scripts/parallelize-tasks.ts`. To shard a suite *within* a project, the app's `test` must run on all 3 boxes with different `--shard` arguments, which cuts across the existing partitioning contract. Design that interaction carefully:

- The partitioner's job ("which projects are mine?") and per-suite sharding are different axes. Decide whether the app's `test` is special-cased out of the partition, or whether the partitioner grows a notion of per-project shard assignment.
- `getShardSelectionErrors()`'s round-trip guarantee must keep holding — its whole point is that a project cannot silently fall off every box.
- Keep `lint`/`typecheck` on the existing project-partition path; they are 11.6% and do not need this.
- Preserve the `vmForks` + `vmMemoryLimit: '512MB'` + `maxWorkers: 4` tuning. It is orthogonal to `--shard` and still load-bearing against the silent-OOM `(0 test)` failure mode.

## Reconcile first

Plan `e448a51d` (Developer Vitest sharding) is DONE with **PR #267 unmerged** and occupies the same territory. Read it before starting — this plan may be a superset, a duplicate, or a correction of it. Do not open a competing PR without resolving that.

## Definition of done

Heaviest CI box's `openthrottle-developer` `test` wall-clock materially below the current single-box figure, `getShardSelectionErrors()` round-trip still green, no project silently unvalidated, and the stale comments in `vitest.config.ts` / `continuous-integration.yml` corrected.

OpenRouter as a model provider for OT Agents
## Goal

Let OT Agents run against **OpenRouter** — one API key, hundreds of models (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Meta, DeepSeek, Qwen, …) behind a single OpenAI-compatible endpoint at `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1`.

Today OT's model surface is **local-only**: `discoverModels` port-scans `localhost` for OpenAI-compatible servers (`ModelProvider = 'lmstudio' | 'ollama'`), and the only non-CLI chat path (`openAiConversationBackend` → `streamChatCompletion`) hardcodes `apiKey: process.env.LLM_API_KEY ?? 'not-needed'` with no per-provider auth, no attribution headers, and no remote catalog. Nothing in the repo mentions OpenRouter (`grep -ri openrouter` → 0 hits).

## Why this shape

OpenRouter is **not an agent CLI** — it is a gateway. So it does NOT get a `defineDriver` module. It lands at three existing seams:

1. **Remote model catalog** — a sibling to `utils/model-discovery/` that reads `GET /api/v1/models` instead of probing ports. The existing local types are deliberately local (`ModelEndpoint` carries `host`/`port`), so remote providers get their own type + GraphQL query rather than a widened `ModelProvider` union.
2. **Chat backend** — OpenRouter speaks the OpenAI wire protocol, so `streamChatCompletion` already covers it *once it can carry a per-request API key and headers*. That is the one real code change on the completion path.
3. **Agent-CLI drivers** — `DriverEndpointConfig` + `capabilities.supportsCustomBaseUrl` already exist for pointing `codex` and `opencode` at a non-default OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Extending that from "discovered local endpoint" to "authenticated remote provider" is additive. `claude` and `cursor` speak proprietary wire protocols (`supportsCustomBaseUrl: false`) and are **out of scope** — do not fake it.

## Non-goals (v1)

- No per-user API keys — v1 is an operator-level `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` on the server env. Per-user/BYO-key credential storage is a follow-up plan.
- No new driver id, no `ALL_DRIVERS` entry.
- No OpenRouter-specific routing features (provider preferences, `:floor`/`:nitro` variants, fallback arrays) beyond passing a model slug through.

## Constraints

- The API key is **server-side only**. It must never reach a browser bundle, a GraphQL response, or a loader payload.
- Every CLI flag or env var claimed in task 8 must be verified against that CLI's own `--help` / config docs at implementation time — never from memory (`packages/openthrottle-drivers/AGENTS.md`).
- Unconfigured must degrade cleanly: with no key set, OpenRouter simply does not appear in the picker; nothing throws, nothing blocks the composer.
- GraphQL is code-first — after resolver changes, boot the server, then `pnpm nx affected --target=codegen-graphql,codegen-react-router --parallel` and commit `applications/openthrottle-server/schema.gql` plus all `__generated__` output.

## Key files

- `packages/openthrottle-agentic-utils/src/utils/model-discovery/` — local discovery core (sibling for remote)
- `packages/openthrottle-agentic-utils/src/types/model-discovery.ts` — `ModelEndpoint`, `DiscoveryResult`
- `packages/openthrottle-agentic-utils/src/utils/chat-completions/stream.ts` — hardcoded `LLM_API_KEY`
- `packages/openthrottle-agentic-utils/src/utils/conversation-backend/openai.ts`, `registry.ts`
- `packages/nestjs-model-discovery/` — SWR-cached Nest wrapper + config namespace
- `packages/openthrottle-drivers/src/types/index.ts` (`DriverEndpointConfig`), `src/drivers/{codex,opencode}.ts`
- `packages/react-router-chat-state/src/config/chat-capabilities.ts`, `src/utils/chat-discovery-options.ts`
- `applications/openthrottle-developer/app/routing/home/demo/models.server.ts`

## Reference

- https://openrouter.ai/docs/quickstart — base `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1`, `Authorization: Bearer <key>`, OpenAI-compatible `/chat/completions`, `GET /api/v1/models`, optional `HTTP-Referer` / `X-Title` attribution headers, slug ids like `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.5`.

## Related

- a55b76ba (token-usage surfacing) — task 9 feeds it
- 7393edc6 (model-discovery SWR caching) — task 5 reuses that cache
- 9a995913 (chat model picker rail) — task 7 extends that UI
- cf9b36a1 / ce1e1e94 (driver + local-endpoint discovery) — the seams task 8 widens

🚀 Pre-launch: Sponsorship funding — FUNDING.yml + cost transparency
## Goal

Turn OpenThrottle's real, already-out-of-pocket infrastructure bill into a credible sponsorship ask. Two halves:

1. **Mechanics** — a `.github/FUNDING.yml` so GitHub renders a **Sponsor** button on the repo (docs: https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/managing-your-repositorys-settings-and-features/customizing-your-repository/displaying-a-sponsor-button-in-your-repository).
2. **Substance** — a short funding page that states what the money actually pays for, so the button converts instead of decorating. Today the owner personally pays for **Vercel**, **Blacksmith**, and **GitHub**; the near-term goal is a **fully self-deployed GCP stack**. `$100–$200/mo` of recurring sponsorship should visibly fund "OpenThrottle is a production-deployable toolset," not just a repo.

## The estimate comes first

The plan opens by rebuilding the cost model, because the numbers *are* the pitch. `infra/gcp-estimate.csv` (Cloud Pricing Calculator, us-west1, effective 2026-03-04) totals **$52.61/mo** across four SKUs — one E2, 10 GB SSD PD, Memorystore Redis Basic M1, and a zonal micro Cloud SQL + 7300 GB-mo storage — and it no longer describes the toolset:

- The Cloud SQL line is **MySQL**, but OpenThrottle is **Postgres + pgvector** end to end (`databases/`, `@openthrottle/nestjs-typeorm`, `semantic_search`). `infra/modules/gcp_cloud_sql_postgres` already exists; pgvector's index memory pushes off the smallest tiers.
- The single E2 assumes the server runs as `all`. `applications/openthrottle-server/src/config/process-role.ts` splits `api` / `worker` — production is two compute units.
- Services that exist in `docker-compose.yml` but not in the estimate: the OT MCP server, `whisper` (voice), run-once `migrations`/`bootstrap`, and local-Ollama embeddings. Plus the supporting bill entirely: Artifact Registry, Cloud Storage, Secret Manager, log/monitoring retention, egress, LB + certs.
- All four React Router apps currently deploy to **Vercel** (`applications/*/vercel.json`). Whether GCP takes them over is the single decision that moves both the GCP total and whether the Vercel bill is retired.
- The 7300 GB-mo (7.3 TB) storage row reads like a calculator default, not a projection.

So task 1 produces **two priced tiers, not one number** — **required** (the floor that actually runs: single env, single zone, no HA, honest about what breaks) and **desired** (staging + production, split API/worker, Memorystore Standard, HA or PITR, real retention). Task 2 then adds the real Vercel/Blacksmith/GitHub amounts, flags which a GCP move retires versus which persist, and reconciles everything against the ask. If required lands under $100 and desired over $200, that's a good outcome — it gives the tiers a natural shape ($100 keeps the lights on, $200 buys staging + production) and sponsorship somewhere to grow. Report real figures either way; don't tune them to fit.

## Other constraints

- **GitHub Sponsors requires owner enrollment** (Stripe Connect + tax/identity forms) before the `github:` key resolves; an unenrolled handle renders no button and no error. That is a human-only gate — see task 3. Nothing else is blocked by it: file, docs, and UI links can all ship and go live the moment enrollment completes.
- **Two remotes, unrelated histories**: `origin` = `OpenThrottle/monorepo` (canonical, private) and `openthrottle` = `OpenThrottle/OpenThrottle` (public mirror). **The public mirror is what visitors see, so that's where the Sponsor button matters** — confirm how the mirror is produced so `.github/FUNDING.yml` actually lands there. An org-level `.github` repo also exists (from the org-alignment licensing work) and can supply a default for every org repo.
- Licensing posture is settled and should be echoed, not re-litigated: open core, Apache-2.0 core with a separate EULA for commercial modules, trademarks reserved (`LICENSE.md`, `LICENSING.md`, `TRADEMARK.md`). Sponsorship copy must not imply sponsors get license or trademark rights.

## Non-goals

- **Not** performing the GCP migration or writing Terraform for it. This plan only *prices* it. The migration is separate work.
- Not setting up a legal entity, not changing licensing, not adding paid tiers/billing to the product.
- No fabricated sponsor counts, testimonials, or logos.

## Definition of done

Required and desired footprints are priced from the current stack and committed, `.github/FUNDING.yml` is in place (and present in whatever repo renders the public button), a funding page explains the cost model with numbers traceable to those estimates, README and the website footer link to it, and the only remaining step is the owner finishing platform enrollment.

Docs & FAQ refresh (openthrottle-developer) — content depth + toggleable UX upgrades
## Problem

The `/docs` and `/faq` routes in `applications/openthrottle-developer` are thin:
- `/faq` renders a 3-entry accordion (`FaqView`) topped with a literal **"Lorem ipsum" placeholder** paragraph (`app/routes/faq._index.tsx`).
- `/docs` has only 4 Markdown pages (`index`, `getting-started`, `docker-builds`, `docker-compose`); only docker-builds has real depth. Presentation is a bare sidebar + article — no search, no on-page TOC, no prev/next, no code-copy, weak landing.

Content and rendering are driven by the source-first package `@openthrottle/react-router-docs` (`FaqView`, `DocPageView`, `DocsNav`, `buildDocsManifest`, `buildDocsNav`) reading Markdown from `app/docs-content/{docs,faq}/`. Convention: `docs/openthrottle/docs-faq-convention.md`.

## Goals

1. **Content depth** — substantially expand docs pages and FAQ entries; kill placeholder copy.
2. **Four presentation upgrades**, each **independently toggleable on/off** so the owner can test with/without:
   - Client-side search across the manifest (title/description/body + FAQ), with a keyboard shortcut.
   - On-page TOC (right rail, scroll-spy) + copy-anchor links on headings.
   - Better landing/index for `/docs` (card overview) and a real `/faq` intro/category hero.
   - Prev/next sequential nav in docs + copy-to-clipboard on code blocks.

## Toggle design (key constraint)

Reuse the app's existing per-user persistence (`app/global/config/persistent-setting-storage.ts` + `useSyncExternalStore` hook pattern). Add a typed `DocsFeatureFlags` config (each upgrade its own flag, sensible defaults), overridable per-user via localStorage, and surface toggles in the Settings area (e.g. `settings.debug` / a "Docs (experimental)" panel). New package components must accept explicit props (enabled/data) so they render identically in tests both on and off; routes translate flags → props. SSR-safe: flags resolve to defaults on the server.

## Architecture constraints

- New presentation components live in `@openthrottle/react-router-docs` (source-first — no `build` target; validate via lint/typecheck/test, then `dev`/`build` on openthrottle-developer as the integration check).
- Feature-flag config, the settings toggle UI, and route wiring live in the app.
- Follow `.cursor/rules` code style; use `@tools/generators` (`NX_ISOLATE_PLUGINS=false pnpm nx g @tools/generators:react-router --subGenerator=component ...`) for new components/routes rather than hand-writing; keep the section-comment scaffold and one-component-per-file rule.
- Content is authored Markdown under `app/docs-content/` — no code changes needed for content tasks; frontmatter per the convention doc.
- No GraphQL/schema changes expected (docs/FAQ are static Markdown).

## Model guidance

- Taste-heavy UI tasks (search, TOC, landing, prev/next) → opus-4.8 or fable-5 (taste ≥ 7).
- Content-heavy Markdown tasks → sonnet-5 (bulk authoring).
- Reviews/validation → fable-5 or opus-4.8.

## Validation

Per-feature route + component tests covering flag ON and OFF; `pnpm nx run <project>:lint|typecheck|test`; consumer `dev`/`build` on openthrottle-developer; browser-preview screenshot verification of each toggle state.
Refresh the thin /docs and /faq routes in openthrottle-developer: expand the Markdown content and add four presentation upgrades (client-side search, on-page TOC + anchors, better landing/index, prev-next nav + code-copy), each independently toggleable on/off for A/B testing via a persistent feature-flag layer.

Switch plan runs from /ot-loop to /ot-loop (incl. the BullMQ path)
## Goal

`/ot-loop <planId>` is the skill we want driving plan execution. It already works interactively in Claude. The gap is the **programmatic path**: everything that today defaults `--prompt` to `/ot-loop`, and in particular the **BullMQ plan-run flow**, where the prompt is not a CLI flag at all but the first layer of a composed prompt string.

## Current state (verified 2026-08-24)

**The rename is a work-in-progress on disk.** `skills/ot-loop/SKILL.md` is a byte-identical copy of `skills/ot-claude-loop/SKILL.md` — its frontmatter still reads `name: ot-claude-loop`, and its description still says "the user runs /ot-claude-loop". Both directories exist; `skills/ot-loop/` is untracked. `skills/ot-claude-loop/SKILL.md` has one uncommitted line added (the "`$planId` is the first (and only) argument … throw an error immediately" guard).

**`/ot-loop` is the default in five independent constants** (no single source of truth):

| Location | Symbol |
| --- | --- |
| `packages/openthrottle-plan-config/src/plan-run-config-storage.constants.ts:10` | `DEFAULT_PLAN_RUN_PLAN_RUN_PROMPT` |
| `packages/openthrottle-agentic-loop/src/config/index.ts:13` | `DEFAULT_PROMPT` |
| `tools/workflows/src/config/load-plan-runner-config.ts:40` | `DEFAULT_PLAN_RUN_PROMPT` |
| `tools/workflows/src/config/messages.ts:35` | `--help` text |
| `applications/openthrottle-server/src/graphql/plans/plan.input.ts:247` | GraphQL field description |

Plus a hardcoded string literal at `packages/openthrottle-plan-config/src/plan-run-config-storage.round-trip.ts:159` (`prompt !== '/ot-loop'`) that bypasses the constant, and the seeded JSON in `databases/migrations/098_adopt_plan_run_worktree_verbose_defaults.sql:32`.

**How the BullMQ path actually composes the prompt** — this is the crux. The queue worker does *not* shell out to `plan-runner`; it runs the in-process orchestrator in `@openthrottle/openthrottle-agentic-loop`. `buildOrchestratorBasePrompt` (`packages/openthrottle-agentic-loop/src/utils/orchestrator.ts:75-105`) concatenates:

```
${context.prompt}            ← "/ot-loop" today
${foreignWorkspaceLayer}
${injectedContext}           ← plan + tasks pulled from Postgres
${WORKFLOW_PROMPT_SHELL_COMMAND_GUARDRAIL}
Plan-Id: <id>. [Task-Id: <id>.] Use the plan and tasks above … When you complete a task output <plan-run:task-complete>TASK_UUID</plan-run:task-complete>.
```

`tools/workflows/src/bin/plan-run.ts:135-140` builds the same shape for the CLI path. That whole string is handed to the agent CLI as a single `-p` prompt.

**So the prompt is a slash command sitting on line 1 of a multi-KB prompt, with the plan context as its trailing text.** `/ot-loop` takes no arguments, so nothing depended on how the CLI binds that trailing text. `/ot-loop` takes `$planId` as its first and only argument — and the skill now throws if that value isn't a plan/task id. If the CLI binds `$planId`/`$ARGUMENTS` to the remainder of the prompt (the injected plan block), or drops the remainder once it expands the command, the run breaks. **Nobody has verified which happens, per driver.** That is task 1 and it gates the design.

Note also that `promptLayer: 'file'` (`--prompt-file`) already exists as an alternative: it reads a SKILL.md, strips YAML frontmatter, and inlines the body — no slash expansion, no argument binding. It may be the correct mechanism for the programmatic path.

## Non-goals

- Changing the per-task discipline itself. `skills/ot-claude-loop/SKILL.md` § The loop is the canonical statement; three places restate it deliberately (`ot-loop`, `ot-workflow-orchestration/runner.workflow.js`). This plan renames and re-points, it does not rewrite the discipline.
- Deleting `skills/ot-loop`. It is fed to agents as a standalone prompt by design and stays as the file-layer / non-Claude fallback unless task 2 concludes otherwise.
- Touching the `/loop`-driven interactive path beyond the rename.

## Definition of done

A plan queued from the Developer UI with untouched defaults runs `/ot-loop` (or its resolved equivalent), the agent receives the plan context intact, tasks flip through `IN_PROGRESS → COMPLETED`, and the run output stream shows it — verified on a real run, not just unit tests.
Superseded 2026-11-09 by 8a529290-26a5-45cc-8705-b35496ce2e67 (ot-loop as an agent-agnostic BullMQ job). The new design makes the job the ot-loop parent and the agent CLI a step-2 worker fed a standalone task prompt, so no slash command or $planId binding reaches the CLI. Tasks 1, 2, 5 and 6 are moot; task 3 (the rename) already landed; the docs work (task 9) moved to 8a529290 task 9.

Refresh /settings/workspace into a real editor-integration surface
## Context

`/settings/workspace` in `openthrottle-developer` has been hollowed out. It used to be the hub for local repositories, but repository management moved to `/settings/repositories` (nested repositories table, toolbar, pagination — commit 5964b973). What remains is three thin pieces: `SettingsWorkspaceIntro`, `SettingsWorkspaceProfileForm` (contact name/email + editor multi-select), and `SettingsWorkspaceApplyEditors` (one button).

**Decision: keep the route, do not delete it.** It is the only surface that owns "which editors does OpenThrottle configure, and push that configuration into my linked repos." That is real, distinct functionality. The problem is that the UI is far thinner than the backend it drives.

## Concrete gaps

1. **Rich results are thrown away.** `applyWorkspaceEditorConfiguration` returns `applications[]` with `repositoryId`, `filesystemPath`, `editor`, `filesWritten[]`, `warnings[]`. `formatEditorConfigApplyMessage` collapses all of it into a single sentence like "Updated 3 editor/repo pairing(s); wrote 12 file(s)." The user never learns which files landed where, or what the warnings actually said.
2. **Per-repo apply is dead code.** The mutation input accepts `repositoryIds`, and `applyEditorConfig` in `routing/settings/actions/workspace.ts` already parses a `repositoryId` form field — but nothing in the UI ever submits one. Apply is all-or-nothing.
3. **No preview of blast radius.** The loader deliberately reads only `profile` and discards `localRepositories` (even though the shared `getWorkspaceSettings` document already fetches them). The user clicks Apply without seeing which repos will be written to.
4. **Stale cross-links.** Three places still send users here to "register a local repository", which is no longer possible on this route:
   - `app/routing/ide/components/IdeWorkspaceBody.tsx:81` — "Open workspace settings"
   - `app/routes/projects._index.tsx:138`
   - `app/routing/ide/README.md:24`
   Plus `app/routing/ide/components/__tests__/IdeWorkspaceBody.test.tsx:54` asserts the stale href.
5. **Unexplained disabled state.** `canApplyEditors = profile.enabledEditors.length > 0` disables the Apply button with no message saying why.
6. **Duplicated copy.** The sentence "OpenThrottle can write MCP, skills, and rules into linked repos for the editors you enable." renders twice inside `SettingsWorkspaceProfileForm`.
7. **Copy lives inline.** Project convention (see component/data file boundaries) puts strings in the nearest `data/data.copy.ts`; this folder has none for workspace.

## Approach

Reframe the page as **Editor integration**: pick editors -> see the repos that will be configured -> apply (all or one) -> read a real per-repo result with files written and warnings. Contact profile stays as a secondary fieldset.

Generate new components with `@tools/generators` (`react-router --subGenerator=component`), keep the generated section comments, one component per file, copy into `routing/settings/data/data.copy.ts`.

## Out of scope

- Any change to the `openthrottle-server` GraphQL schema. Everything needed is already exposed; this is a UI-side plan.
- Repository CRUD — that belongs to `/settings/repositories`.
- New editors beyond `cursor` / `vscode`.

## Validation

`pnpm nx run openthrottle-developer:lint`, `:typecheck`, `:test`, `:build` must all pass.

Season 1 narration rewrite: three iterations per episode in one file
## Goal

One new markdown file — `docs/marketing/scripts/SEASON-1-NARRATION.md` — containing **three narration iterations for every Season 1 episode**: `01` through `22`, plus `L1` and `L2`. Twenty-four episodes, seventy-two takes, one file.

## The shape of the file

One `##` per script. Under it, the beat times once as a reference row, then three iterations. An iteration is a thesis id, one line of thesis prose, and a flat cue list:

```
[
  ['0:00', 'the words'],
  ['0:07', 'the words'],
]
```

Nothing else — no per-iteration front matter, no repeated action column, no tables. That list is already the `NarrationCue[]` shape the typed episodes take, so everything about one script sits in one place and migrating it later is a copy rather than a translation.

## Founding constraints

**1. Beats are frozen. Only the words change.**

The single most important finding in `docs/marketing/episode-format.md`: all five files of episode 05 (`05-connect-ot-mcp.md` and `-v0`…`-v3`) have a **byte-identical action column and identical beat times**, verified by hashing. They differ only in narration. That is the whole economic case for iterating — a beat carries the picture, a variant carries the words, and **one recording serves all three takes**. This file never restates an action column; it lists each episode's beat times once and writes three narration tracks against them.

**2. Fill the runtime. Context beats empty space.**

This reverses the standing guidance in `docs/marketing/scripts/README.md`, which says "the budget is a ceiling, not a target" and that most shorts should land 25–35 seconds of speech across 55 seconds of picture. That produced scripts like `01` at 101 spoken words and `05-v3` at 102 — roughly 42 seconds of speech in a 55-second video, with the rest silent.

The decision for this rewrite is the opposite: **use the runtime to say more.** Shorts target **115–132 spoken words** (132 is the hard ceiling: 145 wpm × 55s, derived from `format.json`). Under 110 words a short is under-narrated and the take goes back. Silence is still allowed where the action is doing the explaining — it is no longer the default.

Long-form is the far bigger gap. `L1` currently carries **299 spoken words across ten minutes of picture** and `L2` is the same shape — both are beat outlines, not scripts, and the validator warns about it on purpose. Filling them properly means roughly **1,200–1,400 words each, per iteration**. That is where most of the writing effort in this plan actually lives.

**3. Tone: the keys to your first car.**

Positive, forward-leaning, high tempo. The feeling is a sixteen-year-old handed the keys — the road is open, the potential is limitless, and nothing about it is hedged or defensive. No fear-based framing, no "agents are broken today", no enterprise-speak. Momentum in the sentence rhythm, not just the adjectives. This tone gets written down as a charter at the top of the file in task 1, because seventy-two takes written to a vibe will not agree with each other; seventy-two takes written to a charter will.

**4. Nothing on screen that does not exist.**

`01-what-is-openthrottle.md` carries a standing note about a first draft that narrated a linked-commit UI which the app does not have. `15-kill-runaway-run.md` and `16-worktrees.md` are `blockedOn` unshipped surfaces. A denser narration track is more exposed to this failure, not less — more words means more claims. Every iteration is audited against the actual beats before the file is done.

## Relationship to the typed-episode migration (OT 2cef373a)

That plan replaces `docs/marketing/scripts/*.md` with typed TypeScript episodes carrying a `variants[]` array, and explicitly states the markdown scripts disappear with nothing regenerating them. This file is therefore a **drafting surface, not a permanent home**. The cue-list shape above is exactly what a `Variant` holds, and variant ids name a thesis (`payoff-first`), never an ordinal (`v3`), per that plan's decision.

Writing the words in markdown first is deliberate. Prose is faster to iterate on and to read in a diff than a TypeScript literal, and the words are the thing being iterated — the format is not.

## Out of scope

- Any change to an action column, a beat time, a flow, or a recording.
- Recording, narrating or assembling any video.
- The typed-episode migration itself.
- Deleting `05-connect-ot-mcp-v0…v3.md`. Their thesis prose is the record of why four openings existed and is carried into the new file first; retiring the files is a follow-up once the migration lands.
Write a single markdown file holding three narration iterations for each of the 24 Season 1 scripts (01–22, L1, L2), against frozen beats, in a denser and more optimistic voice.
